name: Sequential Chaining
description: A fundamental prompt engineering technique that breaks complex tasks into smaller, interconnected prompts where each output serves as input for the next step, creating a structured reasoning pipeline that significantly improves LLM performance on multi-step problems
features: Linear workflow execution with step-by-step processing
Context preservation and state management across prompts
Error isolation and recovery at each step
Improved accuracy on complex tasks vs monolithic prompts

tldr.what: Breaks a task into ordered prompts, each consuming the previous output as input for the next step.
tldr.when: Multi-step work where intermediate results need checking or refinement before proceeding to the next phase.
tldr.watchOut: Errors compound downstream; a mistake early on propagates through all subsequent steps unchecked.

overview.pattern: Break complex tasks into linear pipeline of focused steps
overview.why: Reduces model cognitive load, isolates errors, enables tool integration & step caching
overview.insight: Output[N] → Input[N+1] with structured data (JSON) - each step cacheable
dos: Use JSON/structured outputs between stages
Cache deterministic stage outputs (huge cost savings)
Use cache keys based on input hash + prompt version
Implement circuit breakers & retries
Set TTL for cached steps based on data freshness needs
donts: Pass verbose prose between stages
Cache non-deterministic or time-sensitive steps
Skip cache invalidation on prompt changes
Ignore partial outputs/refusals
Let errors cascade unchecked

usecases.d: parse → extract → analyze → summarize (cache parsing)
research → outline → draft → edit (cache research)
validate → transform → enrich → aggregate (cache transforms)
gather → evaluate → score → recommend (cache gathering)
fetch → process → format → deliver (cache all but delivery)

name: Parallel Chaining
description: Executes multiple independent prompts concurrently and intelligently combines their outputs, enabling faster processing and multi-perspective analysis that leverages parallel computation for complex tasks requiring diverse viewpoints or data sources

tldr.what: Runs multiple independent prompts at the same time, then combines their outputs into a single result.
tldr.when: Tasks needing diverse perspectives or data sources where waiting for one chain before starting another wastes time.
tldr.watchOut: Combining conflicting outputs from parallel chains often requires manual intervention or a clear aggregation rule.

overview.pattern: Execute multiple independent tasks concurrently to reduce latency
overview.why: Drastically reduces wall-clock time for I/O-bound operations, enables multi-perspective analysis
overview.insight: Fan-out independent tasks → aggregate results with voting/merging/synthesis strategies
overview.example: search_news AND search_social AND search_web → aggregate → synthesize
dos: Use structured outputs (JSON) for consistent aggregation
Implement timeouts and partial result handling
Use smaller models for parallel branches, stronger for merge
Batch requests and respect rate limits
Cache results from deterministic branches
donts: Parallelize dependent tasks
Ignore rate limits or burst capacity
Over-parallelize simple tasks
Skip error handling for partial failures
Use verbose unstructured data between stages

usecases.d: news + academic + social → synthesize findings
headline + body + image + CTA → complete email
format + business rules + external APIs → pass/fail
3 models generate options → select best
flights + hotels + events + restaurants → itinerary

name: Conditional Chaining
description: Implements dynamic branching logic where prompt execution paths are determined by intermediate outputs, enabling adaptive workflows that respond intelligently to varying inputs and contexts - essential for personalization and decision trees

tldr.what: Routes execution through different prompts based on intermediate outputs, with each branch tailored to specific conditions or classifications.
tldr.when: Workflows need different handling paths depending on input type, complexity level, or prior results from earlier steps.
tldr.watchOut: Condition logic errors or missing edge cases cause requests to fall through wrong branches, producing mismatched or irrelevant responses.

name: Feedback Chaining
description: Implements iterative improvement cycles where outputs are evaluated and fed back as inputs until quality criteria are met, proven to enhance output quality through convergence-based refinement - particularly effective for creative and optimization tasks

tldr.what: Generates output, evaluates it against quality metrics, feeds critique back as input, and regenerates until meeting a threshold or hitting iteration limits.
tldr.when: Tasks where quality improves through revision cycles, like writing, code generation, or optimization problems with measurable success criteria.
tldr.watchOut: Easily enters infinite loops or produces diminishing returns; set strict iteration caps and validate that metrics actually correlate with real quality.

name: Hierarchical Chaining
description: Structures prompts in multi-level parent-child relationships enabling complex task decomposition, where high-level goals are systematically broken down into manageable subtasks with context inheritance - ideal for project planning and system design

tldr.what: Organizes prompts in parent-child levels where each child inherits context from its parent and results roll up to feed higher levels.
tldr.when: Large projects needing systematic breakdown into subtasks with clear dependencies, where each level's output informs the next.
tldr.watchOut: Context bloat and token waste as inherited information accumulates through deep levels, degrading quality and increasing cost.

name: Iterative Refinement

tldr.when: Content needs polish, code needs optimization, or output quality must exceed single-pass capability before delivery.
tldr.watchOut: Each pass costs tokens; stopping too early leaves gains on table, continuing too long wastes budget with minimal improvement.

description: Advanced technique that orchestrates multiple parallel processing streams with intelligent conflict resolution and quality-weighted aggregation, enabling synthesis of diverse perspectives into coherent, comprehensive outputs - crucial for research and consensus-building

name: LLM-based Routing(LBR)
description: An intelligent query distribution system that uses a specialized LLM router to analyze incoming requests and dynamically route them to the most appropriate model, API endpoint, or processing pipeline based on query characteristics, ensuring optimal resource utilization and response quality through intent classification and capability matching
features: Custom routing rules and domain-specific logic

tldr.what: Routes incoming requests to different models or endpoints by analyzing query intent and matching it against known capabilities.
tldr.when: Systems with multiple specialized models, APIs, or pipelines where different request types need different processing paths.
tldr.watchOut: Router misclassification sends requests to wrong endpoints, potentially degrading quality or requiring expensive fallback handling.

overview.pattern: Use LLM to analyze input and determine routing path dynamically
overview.why: Handles complex, nuanced routing decisions that simple rules can't capture
overview.insight: Prompt engineering + structured outputs = reliable intent classification
dos: Use structured outputs (JSON mode) for deterministic parsing
Provide clear examples in routing prompt
Implement fallback routes for unclear classifications
Cache routing decisions for identical queries
Use temperature=0 for consistent routing
donts: Rely on free-form text parsing for routing
Skip validation of LLM routing output
Use high temperature for routing decisions
Ignore edge cases and ambiguous inputs
Route without confidence thresholds

usecases.d: analyze intent → route to sales/tech/billing specialist
parse request → select appropriate tool/API
classify type → apply correct parser/workflow
understand complexity → route to fast/powerful model
analyze task → choose sequential/parallel execution

name: Embedding-based Routing(EBR)
description: A semantic routing system that converts queries and route definitions into high-dimensional vector embeddings, using cosine similarity or other distance metrics to match incoming requests to the most semantically similar handler, enabling fuzzy matching, multi-lingual support, and context-aware routing beyond simple keyword matching
features: Semantic similarity matching using vector embeddings
Fuzzy boundary handling for ambiguous queries
Pre-computed route embeddings for fast matching

tldr.what: Converts queries and route definitions into vector embeddings, matching incoming requests to handlers by semantic similarity rather than keywords.
tldr.when: Routing needs to handle ambiguous queries, multiple languages, or fuzzy boundaries where exact keyword matching fails.
tldr.watchOut: Embedding quality and similarity thresholds drift over time; stale embeddings or miscalibrated thresholds cause silent misrouting.

overview.pattern: Route requests by comparing vector embeddings in semantic space
overview.why: Captures meaning beyond keywords, enabling fuzzy matching and cross-lingual routing
overview.insight: Same embedding model + cosine similarity + smart thresholds = semantic routing
overview.example: query_embedding = encode(query) → similarities = cosine_sim(query_embedding, route_embeddings) → if max(similarities) > 0.85: route()
dos: Use same embedding model for queries and routes
Normalize embeddings for consistent cosine similarity
Set appropriate similarity thresholds through testing
Cache embeddings for frequently used routes
Monitor embedding drift and update periodically
donts: Mix different embedding models without retraining
Use cosine similarity blindly without validation
Ignore magnitude when it carries meaning
Skip normalization if model expects it
Use fixed thresholds across all route types

usecases.d: query → embed → find most similar documents/FAQs
user input → embed → match to intent clusters
translate meaning, not words → unified routing
question → embed → relevant article section
task description → embed → appropriate tool match

name: Rule-based Routing(RBR)
description: A deterministic routing system that uses predefined rules, conditions, and decision trees to direct queries to appropriate handlers, providing fast, predictable, and auditable routing decisions through if-else statements, switch cases, and pattern matching ideal for compliance-critical and latency-sensitive agentic AI systems
features: Deterministic if-else and switch case logic
Pattern matching with regex and keywords

tldr.what: Uses if-else logic and pattern matching to deterministically route queries to handlers based on predefined rule conditions.
tldr.when: Compliance-critical systems, latency-sensitive routing, or workflows where audit trails and predictability matter more than flexibility.
tldr.watchOut: Rules become brittle and unmaintainable as edge cases accumulate; new query types often fall through or match wrong rules.

overview.pattern: Deterministic routing using predefined rules, conditions, and decision trees
overview.why: Provides traceable, auditable, ultra-fast routing decisions with guaranteed outcomes
overview.insight: If-else chains + pattern matching + config management = predictable agent orchestration
dos: Order rules from most specific to general
Implement fallback/default routes
Version control your rule definitions
Log routing decisions for debugging
Combine with AI for hybrid workflows
donts: Create overlapping or conflicting rules
Hardcode rules without config management
Ignore edge cases and exceptions
Over-complicate with too many conditions
Skip validation and testing of rules

usecases.d: if urgency="critical" AND type="security" → security_team
switch(category) { case "billing": finance_agent; case "tech": it_support }
regulated industries requiring deterministic, auditable paths
round-robin or weighted routing based on agent availability
rules for known patterns + AI fallback for complex cases

name: Machine Learning Model-Based Routing(MLMR)
description: A specialized routing approach that employs discriminative models (classifiers) fine-tuned on labeled data to make routing decisions, encoding routing logic directly in model weights rather than prompts, enabling sub-10ms inference for high-volume agentic AI systems requiring deterministic and explainable routing decisions
features: Supervised fine-tuning on domain-specific routing data
Routing logic encoded in model parameters
Model drift detection and retraining triggers
Explainable routing decisions via attention weights
Integration with MLOps pipelines for continuous improvement

tldr.what: Trains a classifier on labeled routing examples to make decisions via model inference instead of prompts, encoding routing logic in weights for reduced latency.
tldr.when: High-volume systems needing fast routing with explainable decisions, where labeled training data exists or can be generated reliably.
tldr.watchOut: Model drift degrades routing accuracy silently; requires continuous monitoring, retraining triggers, and fallback logic when confidence drops or data distribution shifts.

overview.pattern: Fine-tuned discriminative model encoding routing logic in learned weights
overview.why: Enables ultra-fast (<10ms) routing decisions with high accuracy after supervised training
overview.insight: Routing logic embedded in model parameters, not in prompts - inference without generation

impl.d: Create training corpus with routing labels

dos: Use supervised fine-tuning with domain-specific labeled data
Start with smaller models (BERT-base) for lower latency
Implement confidence thresholds for routing decisions
Monitor class distribution and retrain on drift
Use synthetic data generation from LLMs to augment training set
donts: Use generative models for real-time routing decisions
Deploy without fallback mechanisms for low-confidence predictions
Ignore class imbalance in training data
Skip A/B testing against baseline routing methods
Neglect explainability for critical routing decisions
use: High-volume routing with labeled training data

name: Map-Reduce
description: Distributes computation across multiple nodes using map and reduce operations

tldr.what: Splits a large dataset across parallel workers, each processing a subset independently, then combines results into a final answer.
tldr.when: Processing massive datasets where single-machine execution is too slow and intermediate results can be computed independently.
tldr.watchOut: Coordination overhead and network latency can outweigh parallelization gains on smaller datasets or with expensive reduce operations.

overview.pattern: Split data into chunks, process in parallel, then aggregate results
overview.why: Maximizes throughput, utilizes multiple cores/services, scales horizontally
overview.insight: Chunk[1..N] → Map(f) → [Result1..N] → Reduce → Final_Output

impl.d: Apply same operation to each chunk

overview.example: documents → [analyze, analyze, analyze] → combine insights → final_report
dos: Ensure chunks are independent and balanced
Use deterministic reduce functions for consistency
Handle partial failures gracefully
Size chunks based on processing complexity
Cache map results for repeated reduce operations
donts: Create chunks with interdependencies
Use non-commutative reduce operations
Ignore memory constraints with large datasets
Make chunks too small (overhead) or too large (imbalance)
Forget to handle empty or malformed chunks

metrics.d: Cost per processed item vs sequential

usecases.d: Split large documents → analyze sections → combine insights
Batch posts → classify each → aggregate violation reports

name: Scatter-Gather
description: Distributes requests to multiple services and collects responses

tldr.what: Sends a request to multiple services in parallel, then waits for and combines their responses into one result.
tldr.when: You need data from several independent sources and can tolerate partial results if some services are slow or fail.
tldr.watchOut: Timeout must be short enough to avoid user-facing delays, but long enough that you don't discard valid responses.

overview.why: Maximizes information coverage, improves resilience, leverages diverse capabilities
overview.insight: Request → [Service1, Service2, ServiceN] → Gather → Aggregate → Result

impl.d: Send concurrent requests to all services

dos: Design consistent interfaces across all services
Implement circuit breakers for unreliable services
Use partial result aggregation for resilience
Cache responses to reduce redundant calls
Monitor service performance and adapt strategies
donts: Create dependencies between services
Rely on all services succeeding
Use inconsistent request formats
Ignore slow or failing service patterns
Skip result validation from individual services

name: Fork-Join
description: Forks tasks into parallel subtasks and joins results when complete

tldr.what: Splits a task into independent parallel subtasks, waits for all to finish, then combines their results.
tldr.when: Large problems decomposable into independent work where parallel execution saves time versus sequential processing.
tldr.watchOut: Synchronization overhead and result-merging complexity can eliminate speedup gains on small or tightly-coupled tasks.

overview.why: Optimal parallelism through divide-and-conquer with dynamic load balancing
overview.insight: Task → [Subtask1, Subtask2, ...] → Parallel_Execute → Join → Result

impl.d: Create parallel workers for each subtask
Wait for all subtasks to complete

overview.example: large_task → [subtask_A, subtask_B, subtask_C] → parallel_process → combine → result

Balance subtask granularity for optimal parallelism
Implement work-stealing for load balancing
Use thread pools to avoid creation overhead
Cache intermediate results to avoid redundancy
donts: Create excessive decomposition overhead
Ignore load balancing across workers
Allow resource contention and deadlocks
Define inadequate base cases
Miss error handling in parallel branches

metrics.d: Success rate of subtask failure handling

name: Speculative & Parallel Tool Execution(STE)
description: Predicts the likely next tool call from recurring agent trajectories and executes it speculatively while the LLM is still generating, keeping the speculative result isolated until the model confirms the call and discarding it on a misprediction. It also covers launching retrieval partway through a streaming user turn and returning partial or streamed tool results. Distinct from async-await, fork-join, scatter-gather, and map-reduce, which all fan out already-decided, known-independent calls; the novelty here is acting on an unconfirmed predicted call so tool latency overlaps generation instead of following it.
features: Predicts the next tool call from recurring agent trajectories
Launches the predicted call while the LLM is still decoding
Speculative result kept isolated until the model confirms the call
Mispredicted calls discarded with no effect on real state
Mid-stream retrieval plus partial or streamed tool results
Overlaps tool latency with generation instead of serial round-trips

tldr.what: Predicts the next tool call from past agent patterns and executes it speculatively while the LLM is still generating, keeping results isolated until the model confirms the call.
tldr.when: Latency-sensitive workflows where the same tool sequence repeats predictably and tool execution time dominates the response delay.
tldr.watchOut: Mispredictions waste compute and can cause subtle state inconsistencies if speculative side effects leak into the confirmed execution path.

flow.title: Speculative & Parallel Tool Execution
flow.description: The scheduler predicts the next tool call from the agent trajectory and launches it speculatively while the LLM is still generating, keeping the result isolated until the model confirms it, so tool latency overlaps generation and a misprediction is discarded with no side effect.

🔮 Speculative Scheduler
Predict next call, launch early

⚡ Speculative call
search_flights("Boston", <pending date>)

🧪 Isolation Sandbox
Result quarantined until confirmed

📅 parse_date returns
date = 2026-07-24

🔑 Re-key
Bind speculative call to real date

⚠️ Misprediction path
User: "actually, cancel that"

📤 LLM emits real call
search_flights("Boston", 2026-07-24)

🗑️ Discard Speculative Result
no booking, no side effect

✅ Confirm
Predicted == emitted -> adopt result

📊 Flight Results
Streamed back, wall-clock roughly halved

✨ Answer
Flights to BOS, next Friday

steps.title: User Turn Begins
steps.description: The user asks for a flight. The agent starts streaming its response and its first tool call.

steps.title: Decode First Call and Consult Trajectory
steps.description: The LLM begins decoding parse_date while the scheduler consults the learned trajectory that search_flights almost always follows parse_date.

steps.title: Launch the Predicted Call Speculatively
steps.description: As soon as dest="Boston" is decoded, the scheduler launches search_flights with a pending date into an isolation sandbox, so the read-only round-trip is already in flight.

steps.title: Real Date Arrives, Re-key
steps.description: parse_date returns 2026-07-24; the speculative call is re-keyed to the real date without restarting the already in-flight request.

steps.title: LLM Emits the Real Call and Confirms
steps.description: The model emits the real search_flights call; it matches the speculation, so the quarantined result is adopted instead of issuing a fresh call.

steps.title: Stream Results
steps.description: Because the tool ran during generation, results stream back immediately and wall-clock time is roughly halved versus a serial think-then-call round-trip.

steps.title: Misprediction Handled Safely
steps.description: On the alternate path the user cancels; the predicted call is never confirmed, so the isolated speculative result is discarded with no booking and no side effect.

name: Self-Critique(SC)
description: Agent evaluates its own outputs through systematic analysis and generates targeted improvements

tldr.what: Agent generates output, then systematically identifies flaws and produces a corrected version without external feedback.
tldr.when: Tasks where the agent can reliably spot its own mistakes, like code review, writing polish, or logic validation.
tldr.watchOut: Agent may reinforce its own biases or miss the exact errors it originally made, especially under time pressure.

overview.pattern: Single agent evaluates and iteratively improves its own outputs
overview.why: Catches errors, improves quality, ensures completeness without external validation
overview.insight: Generate → Critique → Revise → Repeat until quality threshold met
dos: Define clear, objective critique criteria for the task
Use structured evaluation templates (accuracy, completeness, clarity)
Set maximum iteration limits (typically 2-3 cycles)
Track quality metrics to measure improvement
Document critique reasoning for transparency
donts: Allow infinite revision loops without stopping criteria
Use vague criteria like "make it better"
Over-critique acceptable responses
Ignore computational cost vs quality gain tradeoffs
Apply same critique template to all task types

usecases.d: Draft → Critique logic/evidence → Strengthen arguments → Polish
Initial code → Identify bugs/inefficiencies → Fix → Optimize
First version → Check accuracy/completeness → Fill gaps → Clarify
Raw analysis → Verify conclusions → Add context → Refine insights
Draft → Evaluate engagement/clarity → Enhance → Final edit

name: Producer-Critic Pattern(PC)
description: Architectural pattern where separate producer and critic agents collaborate for quality improvement

tldr.what: One agent generates output while a separate agent evaluates it and returns structured feedback, repeating until quality thresholds are met.
tldr.when: Work requiring iterative refinement where independent evaluation prevents the producer from reinforcing its own mistakes.
tldr.watchOut: Critic and producer can enter unproductive loops if feedback is vague, contradictory, or the producer lacks clear improvement paths.

overview.pattern: Separate producer and critic agents for unbiased quality improvement
overview.why: Prevents self-evaluation bias, enables specialized critique, improves output quality
overview.insight: Producer focuses on creation, Critic provides objective evaluation → Higher quality

impl.d: Distinct system prompts for each agent

dos: Use distinct personas (e.g., "Senior Engineer" for critic)
Provide structured evaluation criteria to the critic
Separate concerns completely between producer and critic
Consider different critic implementations (LLM, rules, human)
Implement stopping conditions to prevent infinite loops
donts: Use the same prompt/persona for both roles
Let producer see critic instructions (bias prevention)
Skip validation of critic feedback quality
Allow unlimited iterations without convergence checks
Ignore computational costs of dual-agent approach

usecases.d: Developer writes → Senior Engineer reviews → Developer refines
Writer drafts → Editor critiques → Writer polishes
Analyst presents → Peer reviews → Analyst strengthens
Architect proposes → Tech Lead evaluates → Architect improves
Multiple outputs → LLM critic ranks/scores → Select best

name: LLM as Judge(LJ)
description: Specific Producer-Critic implementation where an LLM acts as the critic to evaluate outputs

tldr.what: Generates multiple candidate outputs, then uses a second LLM to score each against a rubric and selects the highest-rated result.
tldr.when: You need consistent quality filtering and have budget for multiple LLM calls; ranking matters more than speed.
tldr.watchOut: The judge LLM may not reliably apply rubrics consistently, especially on subjective criteria or edge cases.

overview.pattern: Use LLMs to evaluate and score other LLM outputs at scale
overview.why: Automates quality assessment, enables best-of-N selection, scales evaluation
overview.insight: Specific implementation of Producer-Critic where the critic is an LLM with evaluation prompts
dos: Use clear, objective evaluation criteria
Implement panel of judges for controversial decisions
Provide rubrics and examples in judge prompts
Use structured output formats (JSON) for scores
Validate judge consistency with known test cases
donts: Use vague criteria like "good" or "better"
Rely on single judge for critical decisions
Skip calibration of judge against human evaluations
Use same model for generation and judging (bias)
Ignore judge uncertainty or confidence scores

usecases.d: Generate 5 responses → Judge ranks → Return best to user
Check if generated code/content meets standards before deployment
Compare model versions by judging outputs on same prompts
Evaluate outputs for harmful/biased content before serving
Judge relevance of retrieved documents to query

name: Reflexion(RX)
description: Agents learn from experience through verbal self-reflection and episodic memory

tldr.what: Agent runs a task, reflects on failure in natural language, stores the reflection, and uses it to improve the next attempt without retraining.
tldr.when: Tasks where the agent can fail safely, learn from mistakes, and retry; failures contain actionable signals the agent can articulate.
tldr.watchOut: Reflection quality depends entirely on the agent's ability to diagnose root causes; vague or incorrect self-analysis compounds errors across trials.

overview.pattern: Agents learn from experience through verbal self-reflection
overview.why: Converts failures into linguistic insights, enabling learning without fine-tuning
overview.insight: Actor → Evaluator → Self-Reflection → Memory → Improved Performance
overview.example: Actor(task) → Result → Evaluate → Reflect(verbal) → Memory → Actor(improved)
dos: Convert feedback into actionable linguistic hints
Maintain episodic memory of past reflections
Use specific, concrete reflection prompts
Implement clear evaluation metrics
Limit reflection depth to avoid overthinking
donts: Store raw trajectories without reflection
Use vague reflections like "do better"
Skip environment feedback integration
Allow unlimited reflection cycles
Ignore memory constraints in long tasks

usecases.d: Write → Test → Reflect on errors → Fix bugs → Improve
Move → Observe → Evaluate → Reflect on strategy → Adapt
Attempt → Check → Analyze failure → Learn → Retry
Draft → Review → Reflect on weaknesses → Revise → Polish
Act → Get reward → Reflect on decisions → Update policy

name: Function Calling
description: Structured interface for AI to invoke external functions and APIs

tldr.what: AI invokes external functions via structured schemas, passing validated parameters and receiving typed responses.
tldr.when: Tasks requiring real-time data, calculations, or state changes that the model cannot perform internally.
tldr.watchOut: Models may hallucinate function calls with wrong names, missing parameters, or impossible argument values.

overview.pattern: Enable AI to invoke external functions and APIs through structured schemas
overview.why: Breaks LLM knowledge limitations, enables real-time data access, external actions, and precise calculations
overview.insight: Schema-driven function calling with parameter validation, parallel execution, and security controls

impl.d: Add to function registry with auth

dos: Write detailed function descriptions (3-4+ sentences minimum)
Use strict JSON schemas with required/optional field validation
Implement parameter sanitization and injection attack prevention
Add timeouts, retries with exponential backoff, and circuit breakers
Use parallel execution for independent function calls
Cache deterministic function results for cost optimization
donts: Use vague function descriptions that lead to hallucinated parameters
Allow unbounded parallel calls without rate limiting
Retry non-idempotent operations after timeouts
Expose raw API credentials or secrets in function calls
Skip input validation and security scanning
use: Need real-time data beyond model training cutoff
Require external API integrations or database queries
Must perform precise calculations or code execution
Triggering actions in external systems (email, scheduling)
avoid: Information available in model knowledge with acceptable quality
Hard real-time requirements where tool overhead breaks SLOs
High-risk irreversible actions without human approval
Simple tasks solvable with basic text generation

usecases.d: get_weather("NYC") → current conditions for decision making
schedule_meeting(time, attendees) → automated scheduling workflows
query_db(table, filters) → dynamic data retrieval and updates
run_python(code) → computational tasks and data analysis
send_email(to, subject, body) → automated notifications
search_web(query) → real-time information retrieval
read_file(path), write_file(path, content) → document processing
call_api(endpoint, params) → external service interactions

name: Code Execution
description: Safely execute LLM-generated code in isolated environments for calculations and data processing

tldr.what: Generates code from prompts, runs it in isolated sandboxes, captures output and errors for the agent to process.
tldr.when: Tasks requiring calculations, data transformation, file processing, or verification where LLM reasoning alone is insufficient.
tldr.watchOut: Sandboxes leak resources or fail silently; always validate generated code logic before execution and set hard timeouts.

overview.pattern: Execute LLM-generated code safely in isolated microVM environments
overview.why: LLMs can generate code for calculations, data analysis, and algorithms but require secure execution due to potential malicious or buggy output
overview.insight: Treat LLM code as untrusted - use Firecracker microVMs for hardware isolation with <125ms startup

impl.d: Run in isolated kernel with limits

overview.example: User: "Calculate fibonacci(20)" → Generate Python → Validate imports → Launch Firecracker → Return: 6765
dos: Use Firecracker microVMs for hardware-enforced isolation
Implement VM-level security with dedicated kernels per execution
Leverage KVM hypervisor with <5 MiB memory overhead per microVM
Use jailer process for additional cgroup/namespace isolation
Destroy microVMs after each execution for perfect isolation
Pool warm microVMs for <125ms startup performance
donts: Rely solely on containers for untrusted code (shared kernel risk)
Use traditional VMs (minutes startup vs 125ms microVM)
Skip hardware virtualization for critical security boundaries
Reuse microVMs across different execution contexts
Enable unnecessary devices (keep minimal virtio interface)
use: Untrusted/AI-generated code requiring maximum security isolation
Multi-tenant environments where kernel-level isolation is critical
Production serverless workloads needing <125ms cold start performance
High-density compute requiring thousands of isolated execution contexts
avoid: Simple calculations answerable through LLM reasoning alone
Environments where container isolation is sufficient (trusted code)
Resource-constrained edge devices without KVM virtualization support
Legacy applications requiring full hardware emulation or BIOS support

metrics.d: <125ms boot to userspace (vs minutes for VMs)
Thousands of microVMs per host with <5 MiB overhead

usecases.d: AWS Lambda-style execution with Firecracker microVMs
AI agent code in isolated kernels (CI/CD, notebooks)
Separate microVMs per customer with hardware isolation
Replace Docker with microVM for critical workloads

Instant dev environments with VM-level isolation

name: Model Context Protocol(MCP)
description: Standardized protocol for sharing context and capabilities between AI models and tools

tldr.what: Standardized protocol that lets AI models discover, describe, and use tools through structured context and capability exchange.
tldr.when: Systems needing multiple models to share tools, maintain session state, or hand off work across different AI services.
tldr.watchOut: Protocol overhead and versioning mismatches between client and server implementations can silently degrade or break tool availability.

overview.pattern: Standardize AI application context sharing and tool integration via JSON-RPC protocol
overview.why: Enables seamless interoperability between AI models and external tools/data sources across platforms
overview.insight: Open standard solving N×M integration problem - 1000+ servers available, adopted by OpenAI/GitHub
overview.example: Client connects → initialize() → list_tools() → call_tool("github_search") → get_resource(handle)
dos: Use JSON Schema for all tool parameters and response validation
Implement OAuth 2.1 with PKCE for secure authentication
Use resource handles instead of inlining large content
Implement streaming for large outputs with backpressure control
Version capabilities and maintain backward compatibility
Apply least privilege principle for server access scoping
donts: Pass tokens through servers (token passthrough anti-pattern)
Skip server validation (vulnerable to spoofing attacks)
Embed large documents in prompts instead of using handles
Deploy without conformance tests (schema drift risk)
Ignore structured error codes for proper fallback handling
use: Multi-tool agent systems requiring standardized integration
Enterprise copilots needing unified data source access
IDE/development tools requiring dynamic capability discovery
avoid: Single, static tool integrations where function calling suffices
Ultra-low-latency paths that cannot afford protocol overhead
Simple applications without complex tool orchestration needs
Environments where server process deployment is infeasible

usecases.d: One-click MCP server installation via Desktop Extensions
CI/CD, issues, PRs with 35% code review latency reduction
Unified access to CRM, HRIS, payroll, accounting systems
Filesystem, VCS, documentation with real-time context
60-80% reduction in processing time with resource handles
Standardized tool sharing between autonomous agents
Document and metadata retrieval via efficient handle references
Natural language automation across device ecosystems

name: Control Plane as a Tool(CPT)
description: Exposes a single unified tool interface to the agent while an internal control plane routes each request to the right tool, service, or model behind it. The agent prompt stays stable as the tool catalog evolves, and authentication, policy, rate limiting, and observability are enforced in one place.
features: Single stable tool interface for the agent
Internal tool registry with dynamic routing logic
Centralized policy, auth, and rate-limit enforcement
Tool versioning and swaps without prompt changes
Unified logging and observability for all tool calls

tldr.what: Routes all agent tool calls through a single interface to a backend control plane that handles auth, rate limits, and tool selection without changing the agent prompt.
tldr.when: You have many tools evolving frequently and need consistent policy enforcement, audit trails, and stable agent prompts across tool catalog changes.
tldr.watchOut: Control plane becomes a bottleneck and single point of failure if routing logic is slow or the plane goes down, breaking all agent tool access.

name: Computer Use(CU)
description: Agents operate graphical user interfaces (desktop, browser, or mobile) the way a person does, by reading screenshots and issuing mouse and keyboard actions instead of calling APIs. The core challenge is GUI grounding: mapping an intent to exact pixel coordinates on the screen. The agent runs a loop of screenshot, reason, act, and observe until the task is complete.
features: Screenshot-based perception of the live screen
GUI grounding from intent to precise pixel coordinates
Low-level action space: click, type, scroll, drag, key press
Perception-reason-act-observe loop with feedback after each step
Error recovery from popups, modals, and unexpected UI states
Works on applications and sites that expose no API

tldr.what: Agent reads screenshots, grounds intent to pixel coordinates, executes mouse and keyboard actions, loops until task completion.
tldr.when: Systems with no API, complex multi-step UI workflows, or when you need to automate legacy or third-party applications.
tldr.watchOut: GUI grounding fails on dynamic layouts, small targets, or obstructed elements, causing cascading errors that are hard to recover from.

name: Agent Skills(AS)
description: Capabilities packaged as self-contained folders. Each skill is a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter (name and description) plus optional scripts and resources. Agents discover skills by their metadata and load them through three levels of progressive disclosure: read name and description to judge relevance, load the full SKILL.md once activated, then execute bundled scripts and resources on demand. This keeps context small while exposing many capabilities, and the format is an open standard adopted across vendors.
features: Self-contained folder with SKILL.md, scripts, and resources
YAML frontmatter metadata (name, description) drives discovery
Three-level progressive disclosure: metadata, full instructions, bundled files
Only the active skill's full content enters the context window
Bundled executable scripts run deterministic work outside the model
Open, cross-vendor format that is portable between agents

tldr.what: Packages agent capabilities as self-contained folders with metadata, instructions, and scripts. Agents load only active skill content into context while keeping a lightweight index of all available skills.
tldr.when: Agents need access to many tools but limited context window, or when skills must be portable across different agent platforms and vendors.
tldr.watchOut: Scripts may fail silently or produce unexpected output if the agent misunderstands skill preconditions or mismatches input formats.

flow.title: Agent Skills
flow.description: Capabilities are packaged as self-contained folders, each a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter plus optional scripts and resources. The agent discovers skills by metadata and loads them through three levels of progressive disclosure, so the context window holds only the active skill instead of all installed ones.

name: Tool Retrieval (Tool RAG)(TR)
description: When an agent can reach hundreds or thousands of tools or MCP servers, loading every schema into the prompt is expensive and hurts selection accuracy. Tool retrieval indexes tool definitions and, for each query, retrieves only the semantically relevant ones (embedding search, active discovery, and reranking) before the model chooses. RAG-MCP reports tool-selection accuracy rising from about 13 percent to 43 percent while cutting prompt tokens by more than half.
features: Vector index over tool and MCP server definitions
Per-query semantic retrieval of relevant tools only
Reranking to shortlist the top-k candidate tools
Active, on-demand discovery instead of preloading all schemas
Large prompt-token reduction versus loading every schema
Higher tool-selection accuracy at scale (thousands of tools)

tldr.what: Indexes tool definitions by embedding, retrieves only semantically relevant schemas per query, then reranks before the model selects.
tldr.when: Agents access hundreds or thousands of tools and loading all schemas wastes tokens and degrades selection accuracy.
tldr.watchOut: Retrieval failures (poor embedding match or ranking) silently omit the correct tool, causing the agent to pick a suboptimal alternative.

flow.title: Tool Retrieval (Tool RAG)

name: Structured Outputs(SO)
description: Guarantee that model output conforms to a schema by constraining decoding. A JSON Schema, regex, or grammar is compiled into a finite-state machine, and at every decode step the tokens that would violate the schema are masked out so only valid continuations can be sampled. In strict mode this makes malformed JSON and invalid tool arguments impossible. It is available natively at OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic and in open libraries such as Outlines and vLLM.
features: Constrained decoding driven by JSON Schema, regex, or grammar
Schema compiled to a finite-state machine and per-step token mask
Invalid tokens masked at every decode step in strict mode
Schema-conforming output guaranteed, not merely requested
Eliminates JSON parse errors and invalid tool-call arguments
Native provider support plus Outlines and vLLM

tldr.what: Compiles a schema into a finite-state machine and masks invalid tokens at each decode step, guaranteeing output conforms to the schema.
tldr.when: Extracting structured data, calling tools, or generating JSON where parse errors or invalid values would break downstream code.
tldr.watchOut: Schema constraints can force the model to emit technically valid but semantically nonsensical values when the true answer falls outside allowed options.

flow.title: Structured Outputs
flow.description: Constrained decoding guarantees schema-conforming output. A JSON Schema is compiled into a finite-state machine, and at every decode step the tokens that would break the schema are masked out, so only valid JSON can be produced and downstream parsing never fails.

nodes.label:
📐 JSON Schema
name: string, amount: number,
currency: enum[USD, EUR, GBP]

🛠️ Compile
Schema -> FSM

🔀 FSM / Grammar
valid-token automaton

🤖 LLM Decoder
generate token by token

📊 Logits
next-token distribution

🚧 Token Mask
zero out invalid tokens

🚫 Blocked Tokens
CAD not in enum,
letters where number expected

🎲 Sample
only a valid continuation

🔁 Per-Step Constraint
applied every decode step

📄 Valid JSON
{"name":"Acme","amount":42.5,"currency":"USD"}

✅ Downstream Code
json.loads(), no try/except,
0 violations / 10000 rows

steps.title: Define the Schema
steps.description: The extraction task fixes an exact output shape: a name string, a numeric amount, and a currency restricted to three enum values.

steps.title: Compile Schema to FSM
steps.description: The schema is compiled once into a finite-state machine that knows, at any point, which tokens are still valid.

steps.title: Decode with the Model
steps.description: The model reads a receipt and produces logits for the next token, exactly as in normal generation.

steps.title: Mask Invalid Tokens
steps.description: The FSM defines the allowed set. Tokens that would break the schema, such as CAD outside the enum or a letter where a number belongs, are masked to zero probability.

steps.title: Sample a Valid Continuation
steps.description: Only valid tokens remain, so the sampled token always keeps the output on a schema-conforming path. The constraint reapplies at every decode step.

steps.title: Emit Valid JSON
steps.description: When decoding completes, the result is guaranteed-valid JSON matching the schema, with no repair pass needed.

steps.title: Consume Without Repair
steps.description: Downstream code parses the output directly with no try/except and no retries, achieving 0 schema violations across all 10000 rows.

name: Code as Action (CodeAct)(CA)
description: Instead of emitting one JSON tool call per turn, the agent's action space is executable code that orchestrates tools with loops, conditionals, and variables. A single code block can call many tools, branch on results, and keep intermediate data in the runtime rather than passing every result back through the context window. Anthropic reports roughly a 98 percent token reduction on some multi-tool workflows when tools are called from code via MCP.
features: Action space is executable code, not a single JSON call
Loops, conditionals, and variables compose many tool calls per turn
Intermediate results stay in the runtime, not the context window
Fewer model round-trips for multi-step, multi-tool work
Large token reduction on tool-heavy workflows (up to ~98 percent reported)
Tools exposed to code (for example via MCP) with results filtered before return

tldr.what: Agent writes executable code that calls multiple tools with loops, conditionals, and variables in a single turn, keeping intermediate results in runtime.
tldr.when: Multi-tool workflows with iteration, branching, or state that would otherwise require many sequential model round-trips and context window passes.
tldr.watchOut: Code execution errors halt the entire workflow; agent must debug and retry, and sandboxing overhead can negate token savings on simple tasks.

flow.title: Code as Action (CodeAct)
flow.description: The agent expresses its action as executable code that orchestrates tools with loops, conditionals, and variables, instead of one JSON tool call per turn. Intermediate results stay in the runtime rather than the context window, so a single script can process hundreds of rows and return only a summary.

steps.title: Task and Two Options
steps.description: The agent could answer with 20-plus sequential JSON tool calls, each result flowing back through the context window, but that is slow and token-heavy.

steps.title: Write One Code Action
steps.description: Instead, the agent emits a single Python script whose loops, conditionals, and variables orchestrate the tools.

steps.title: Execute in the Runtime
steps.description: The runtime runs the script. It calls read_csv once to load 500 rows and begins iterating over them.

steps.title: Loop Calls Tools Per Row
steps.description: Inside the loop the script calls get_customer and compute_tax for each of the 500 rows, without a separate model turn per call.

steps.title: Intermediate Data Stays in Runtime
steps.description: The 500 customer records and per-row tax values live in runtime memory and are filtered by the overdue condition. None of them enter the context window.

steps.title: Only the Summary Returns
steps.description: The script accumulates a single total. Returning just that value instead of 500 records cuts tokens by roughly 98 percent versus per-row tool calls.

steps.title: One Turn, Summary Only
steps.description: The whole job finishes in one turn using three tools, and the model sees only the final total.

name: Structured Reflection (Think Tool)
description: A dedicated no-op "think" tool (Anthropic) declared in the agent tool schema that the model calls mid-trajectory to append structured reasoning between a tool result and the next action. The call has no external effect and returns nothing useful: it simply gives the model a checkpoint to re-read policy, verify constraints, and plan before acting inside a long tool-call chain. Anthropic reports a 54% relative improvement on the tau-bench airline pass^1 metric (0.570 versus a 0.370 baseline) when the tool is paired with a prompt that shows how to use it. Distinct from `metacognitive-monitoring`: that entry is the general capability of monitoring one's own reasoning, whereas the think tool is a concrete tool-schema mechanism for it, separate from extended or inference-time thinking that happens before the first response.
features: No-op tool in the schema: no side effect and no new data returned
Called mid-trajectory, between a tool result and the next action
Creates explicit reflection checkpoints inside long tool-call chains
Used to re-check policy compliance and validate plans before acting
Cheap and low-code: one tool definition plus a usage-guiding prompt
Reported 54% relative pass^1 gain on the tau-bench airline domain

tldr.what: Declares a no-op tool in the schema that the model calls mid-trajectory to pause, re-read policy, and plan before the next action.
tldr.when: Long tool-call chains where the model must verify constraints or policy compliance before committing to an irreversible action.
tldr.watchOut: The model may skip calling think if the prompt example is weak or absent; effectiveness depends entirely on showing the model when and how to use it.

Anthropic reports this lifts tau-bench airline pass^1 from 0.370 to 0.570, a 54% relative gain.

steps.title: User Asks to Change the Flight
steps.description: The user requests an earlier flight. The agent enters its tool-using loop to handle the change under airline fare rules.

steps.title: Agent Looks Up the Reservation
steps.description: The agent calls get_reservation and the tool returns the ticket: a basic-economy fare booked 20 minutes ago.

steps.title: Tool Result Arrives, Agent Calls think()
steps.description: Rather than acting on the result immediately, the agent calls the no-op think tool. The call takes no external action and returns nothing, but it opens a reflection checkpoint.

steps.title: Think Checkpoint: Recall Policy and Draft a Plan
steps.description: Inside the think call the agent writes out the relevant policy (basic economy is non-changeable, but a 24-hour free-cancellation window applies) and drafts the steps. This reasoning is now in context.

steps.title: Decision Respects the Fare Rules
steps.description: Guided by the checkpoint, the agent chooses cancel-and-rebook within the 24-hour window and rejects a direct change_flight() call, which would violate the non-changeable fare.

steps.title: Agent Cancels Within 24h, Then Rebooks
steps.description: The agent cancels the booking inside the free-cancellation window, quotes the new fare, gets user confirmation, and books the tomorrow-morning flight.

steps.title: Booking Changed Legally, Violation Avoided
steps.description: The change completes within policy. On tau-bench airline this reflection pattern lifts pass^1 from 0.370 to 0.570, a 54% relative gain over the same agent without the think tool.

name: MCP Gateway (Tool Federation & Governance)(MCPG)
description: A single governed MCP entrypoint that sits in front of many backend MCP servers as a reverse proxy, federating their tools into one curated, managed tool surface that the agent connects to. Every tool call routes through the gateway, which enforces centralized authentication, per-tool authorization that separates the caller's identity from the downstream server's permissions, policy checks, rate limiting, audit logging, and telemetry. This turns a sprawling pile of independently deployed servers into one controlled integration contract, so tools can be curated, versioned, and revoked without touching each agent. Distinct from `control-plane`: the control plane is the general pattern of exposing one interface while routing internally to any tool, service, or model, whereas the MCP gateway is the MCP-ecosystem-specific realization focused on federating many MCP servers and governing the shared tool-access surface.
features: Reverse proxy in front of many backend MCP servers
Federates their tools into one curated, managed tool surface
Centralized authentication at a single entrypoint
Per-tool authorization separating caller identity from downstream permissions
Policy enforcement, rate limiting, and request shaping per call
Full audit log and telemetry for every tool invocation

tldr.what: Single reverse proxy sits in front of many MCP servers, federating their tools into one curated surface with centralized auth, per-tool authorization, rate limiting, and audit logging.
tldr.when: Multiple independent MCP servers need unified access control, tool curation, and audit trails without modifying each agent or backend.
tldr.watchOut: Gateway becomes a critical bottleneck and single point of failure; any outage blocks all tool access across all agents and servers.

flow.title: MCP Gateway (Tool Federation & Governance)
flow.description: A single governed MCP entrypoint federates tools from many backend MCP servers into one curated surface. Every call routes through it for centralized auth, per-tool authorization, policy and rate limiting, and audit, so an allowed tool call is proxied to the right backend while an over-privileged call is denied before it ever reaches a server.

steps.title: One Entrypoint
steps.description: The agent connects only to the gateway and issues a single tool call, create_issue, instead of talking to any backend MCP server directly.

steps.title: Authenticate the Caller
steps.description: The gateway validates the agent gateway token and resolves a stable caller identity (agent:support-bot) before any tool logic runs.

steps.title: Per-Tool Authorization
steps.description: Caller scope is checked per tool. support-bot is granted jira:create_issue, and the gateway separates the caller identity from the downstream server permissions.

steps.title: Deny an Over-Privileged Call
steps.description: When the same caller later tries delete_repo, it is not in support-bot scope, so the gateway denies it before it ever reaches the GitHub server and records the deny.

steps.title: Policy and Rate Limit
steps.description: The allowed create_issue call passes policy checks and sits under the 60 calls/min quota, so it proceeds to routing.

steps.title: Route Across Federated Servers
steps.description: The router maps create_issue to the Jira MCP server. Four backend servers (GitHub, Jira, S3 Files, Payments) are federated behind one curated surface; only Jira is dispatched.

steps.title: Proxy with Scoped Credential
steps.description: The gateway swaps in its own scoped Jira service credential (the agent never sees the secret), proxies the call, and logs the allow decision with latency.

steps.title: Governed Result
steps.description: Issue JIRA-4821 is created and returned. Four servers were federated behind one entrypoint, every call authenticated, authorized per tool, rate-limited, and audited in one place.

name: Meta-Reasoning(MR)
description: Higher-order reasoning about reasoning processes, including strategy selection and monitoring

tldr.what: Agent monitors and selects its own reasoning strategies, switching approaches based on task type and performance feedback.
tldr.when: Complex multi-domain problems where different sub-tasks need different reasoning methods and the agent must adapt mid-execution.
tldr.watchOut: Overhead of strategy selection and monitoring can exceed savings from better approach choice, especially on simple or time-constrained tasks.

overview.pattern: AI system that monitors and optimizes its own reasoning processes
overview.why: Enables adaptive intelligence, strategy selection, and self-improvement in complex domains
overview.insight: Three-layer architecture: Object-level execution → Monitor layer → Meta-reasoning layer for optimal strategy selection

impl.d: Choose optimal reasoning strategy for task
Switch strategies if needed, update preferences

overview.example: detect_problem → assess_confidence → select_strategy → execute → monitor → adapt
dos: Implement three-layer architecture: Object → Monitor → Meta
Track confidence scores and decision quality metrics
Use strategy selection based on task characteristics
Monitor resource usage and computational efficiency
Build strategy performance history for learning
Implement graceful failure handling and recovery
donts: Add meta-reasoning to every simple task (overhead)
Ignore computational cost of meta-reasoning layer
Use generic confidence without domain calibration
Skip strategy switching when clearly underperforming
Implement without clear meta-cognitive questions

usecases.d: Self-driving cars adapting to weather/traffic conditions
Switching between diagnostic approaches based on symptoms
Adapting strategies based on market volatility
Choosing between vision, text, audio processing strategies
Selecting search/analysis methods based on query type
Dynamic strategy selection based on opponent behavior
Adapting manipulation strategies based on object properties
Routing strategies based on issue complexity

tldr.what: Decomposes complex tasks into hierarchical networks of subtasks using domain rules, refining abstract tasks into executable primitives.

overview.pattern: Hierarchical decomposition of complex tasks into manageable sub-tasks using domain knowledge
overview.why: Enables efficient planning through abstraction, reusable expertise, and human-interpretable solutions
overview.insight: Tasks (compound→primitive) + Methods (how to decompose) + Conditions (when to apply) = Hierarchical Plans

impl.d: Decomposition rules: when & how to break tasks
Replan if conditions change or methods fail

dos: Encode domain expertise in methods and conditions
Use clear task hierarchies with proper abstraction levels
Define preconditions and effects for each method
Implement backtracking when decomposition fails
Cache successful decomposition patterns
Design reusable method libraries for domains
donts: Create overly deep hierarchies (>5-6 levels)
Ignore method ordering constraints and dependencies
Use HTN for simple linear task sequences
Hard-code solutions without conditional methods
Skip validation of method preconditions

overview.pattern: Systematic task decomposition, progress tracking, and adaptive workflow management for complex multi-step processes
overview.why: Reduces cognitive load, ensures progress visibility, prevents work duplication, and enables adaptive coordination in complex workflows
overview.insight: Task registry + state tracking + dependency management + adaptive prioritization = organized execution

impl.d: Create task registry with state tracking schema
Break down complex objectives into actionable tasks
Manage dependencies, priorities, and execution flow
Monitor progress and update task states dynamically
Replan and reprioritize based on progress and changes

dos: Use clear task state schema (pending/in_progress/completed/blocked)
Implement dependency tracking and automatic blocking/unblocking
Design adaptive priority scoring based on deadlines and impact
Track task completion metrics and identify bottlenecks
Implement real-time progress visibility and status updates
Use atomic task operations to prevent state corruption
Design for parallel task execution where possible
Implement rollback mechanisms for failed task sequences
donts: Create overly granular tasks that increase management overhead
Ignore task dependencies leading to execution deadlocks
Use static priorities without considering changing contexts
Skip validation of task completion criteria
Allow task state inconsistencies across concurrent operations
Forget to implement timeout handling for stuck tasks
use: Projects requiring progress visibility and reporting
avoid: Real-time systems where task overhead is prohibitive
Tasks that are better handled as atomic operations

Create unbounded iterations without stop criteria
Focus on activity metrics instead of outcome measurements
Skip stakeholder alignment on goal definitions

name: Constraint Satisfaction Planning(CSP)
description: Planning approach that simultaneously satisfies multiple constraints while optimizing objectives

tldr.what: Simultaneously satisfies multiple hard and soft constraints while exploring solution space, using constraint propagation to eliminate infeasible options and resolve conflicts.
tldr.when: Complex scheduling or resource allocation where many requirements compete, feasibility matters as much as optimization, and trade-offs between constraints need explicit handling.
tldr.watchOut: Computational cost grows exponentially with constraint count; poorly ordered constraint checking can waste cycles exploring dead-end branches before backtracking.

name: Scenario-Based Planning(SBP)
description: Multi-scenario planning that prepares for different possible futures and uncertain conditions

tldr.what: Models multiple possible futures with assigned probabilities, then develops strategies robust across scenarios rather than optimized for one.
tldr.when: Planning under high uncertainty where outcomes depend on uncontrollable factors like market conditions, competition, or regulatory changes.
tldr.watchOut: Scenario probabilities are guesses; plans optimized for unlikely scenarios waste resources while neglecting preparation for probable ones.

name: Plan-Execute Decoupling (ReWOO/LLMCompiler)(PED)
description: Generates the full plan or tool-call graph up front, decoupled from tool observations, and only then executes it. ReWOO writes a variable-parameterized chain of tool calls before anything runs, cutting redundant model invocations; LLMCompiler builds a dependency DAG and dispatches independent tool calls in parallel. This differs from ReAct, which interleaves one thought and one action at a time and re-feeds every observation into the prompt.
features: Full plan or tool-call DAG generated before execution begins
Variable substitution passes results between planned steps
Dependency graph enables parallel tool dispatch (LLMCompiler)
Around 5x fewer tokens than observation-interleaved ReAct
Around 3.7x lower latency from parallel tool execution

tldr.what: Generates complete tool-call plan or dependency graph before execution, then runs all steps (or parallel-safe subsets) without re-prompting on each observation.
tldr.when: Multi-tool tasks where steps are independent or have clear dependencies, and you need lower latency or token cost than interleaved thought-action loops.
tldr.watchOut: Plan becomes stale or wrong if early tool results differ from assumptions; replanning mid-execution adds complexity and can negate token savings.

flow.title: Plan-Execute Decoupling (ReWOO / LLMCompiler)
flow.description: Generate the whole plan or tool-call DAG up front, decoupled from observations, then execute it. ReWOO writes variable-parameterized chains before any tool runs (~5x fewer tokens); LLMCompiler dispatches independent tool calls in parallel from the dependency graph (~3.7x lower latency). Unlike ReAct, no observation is re-fed mid-plan.

nodes.label:
❓ Research Query
"Which has more calories, a Big Mac
or a Whopper, and by how much?"

🗺️ ReWOO Planner
Write the FULL plan before any tool runs

📜 Variable-Parameterized Plan
#E1 = search "Big Mac calories"
#E2 = search "Whopper calories"
#E3 = compute #E1 - #E2
(no observations consumed)

🧩 LLMCompiler
Compile plan into a 6-node dependency DAG

⚡ Parallel Dispatch
n1 and n2 have no dependency,
so they run at the same time

🔍 n1: search
"Big Mac calories"
(independent)

🔍 n2: search
"Whopper calories"
(independent)

📄 n3: fetch page A
depends on n1

📄 n4: fetch page B
depends on n2

🔀 n5: Joiner
merge n3 + n4
Big Mac 563 kcal, Whopper 657 kcal

🧮 n6: Solver
657 - 563

✨ Answer
The Whopper has 94 more calories

📉 Token Efficiency
Plan decoupled from observations:
~5x fewer tokens than ReAct

🐌 vs ReAct
Interleaves 6+ thought/action turns
sequentially, re-feeding each result

steps.title: Research Query
steps.description: A multi-step question arrives that needs several tool calls and a final computation.

steps.title: Plan Before Executing (ReWOO)
steps.description: The planner writes the entire plan up front as a chain of variable-parameterized steps (#E1, #E2, #E3). Crucially it consumes no tool observations while planning, so tokens are not spent re-reading intermediate results.

steps.title: Compile the Dependency DAG
steps.description: LLMCompiler turns the plan into a 6-node graph, tracking which calls depend on which. Unlike ReAct, it does not interleave a fresh thought before each action.

steps.title: Dispatch Independent Tools in Parallel
steps.description: The two searches n1 and n2 share no dependency, so the compiler fires them simultaneously instead of one after another.

steps.title: Resolve Dependencies
steps.description: Once each search returns, its dependent fetch runs: n3 after n1 and n4 after n2, again in parallel with each other.

steps.title: Join Observations
steps.description: The joiner merges both fetched pages: Big Mac 563 kcal and Whopper 657 kcal.

steps.title: Solve and Answer
steps.description: The solver computes 657 - 563 and returns the answer in 4 sequential rounds instead of 6+ ReAct turns: about 3.7x lower latency and 5x fewer tokens.

references: ReWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations for Efficient Augmented Language Models - Xu et al. (ArXiv 2023) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18323
An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling - Kim et al. (ArXiv 2023) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04511

name: Plan & TODO Recitation(PTR)
description: The agent keeps an explicit, editable todo or plan artifact (for example a write_todos tool call or a todo.md file) and continually rewrites and recites it as work proceeds. Re-emitting the evolving plan at the end of the context window pushes the global objective back into the model recent attention on every step, which resists goal drift and lost-in-the-middle forgetting across long runs.
features: Explicit editable todo or plan artifact the agent owns
Plan recited and rewritten after each step
Keeps the global objective in recent context
Checked-off items act as external memory of progress
Counteracts goal drift and lost-in-the-middle forgetting
Used in Claude Code, Deep Agents, and Manus

tldr.what: Agent maintains an editable todo list artifact, rewrites it after each step, and recites it to keep the global objective in recent context throughout execution.
tldr.when: Long-running tasks where intermediate progress needs tracking and the agent risks forgetting the original goal or drifting between steps.
tldr.watchOut: Plan recitation consumes tokens on every step; if the plan grows large or tasks are numerous, overhead can outweigh the benefit of reduced goal drift.

flow.title: Plan & TODO Recitation
flow.description: The agent keeps an explicit editable todo/plan artifact (write_todos or todo.md) and continually recites and rewrites it, re-emitting the global objective at the tail of the context on every step. This keeps the goal in recent attention and resists drift and lost-in-the-middle forgetting over long runs. Popularized by Claude Code, Deep Agents, and Manus.

nodes.label:
🎯 Long-Horizon Task
"Migrate a 50-file service from Flask
to FastAPI without breaking the API"

🤖 Long-Horizon Agent
Runs 50+ steps over many turns

📝 todo.md v0
[ ] 1 inventory 50 routes
[ ] 2 port middleware
[ ] 3-52 convert each route
[ ] 53 tests  [ ] 54 verify
Objective: keep endpoints compatible

⚙️ Execute Next Step
Convert one route file

🔁 Recite + Rewrite Plan
Re-emit the todo at the context tail
after every step

📝 todo.md @ step 12
[x] 1-2 done
[x] 3-12 routes (10/50)
[ ] 13 orders  <- NEXT
Objective re-stated

📝 todo.md @ step 40
[x] 38/50 routes done
[ ] reports, exports, webhooks
Objective re-stated

🧠 Recent Context
Objective sits at the tail, so it stays
in the model recent attention

🛡️ Goal-Drift Guard
Objective unchanged across 50 steps

⚠️ Without Recitation
Objective sinks into the
lost-in-the-middle dead zone: drift + repeats

✨ Result
50/50 routes migrated, contract tests green,
objective preserved end to end

steps.title: Long-Horizon Task
steps.description: A migration touching 50 files will take many steps across many turns, far more than fits comfortably in one context window.

steps.title: Write the Initial Plan
steps.description: Before doing work, the agent writes an explicit todo.md that enumerates every step and states the global objective: keep every public endpoint response-compatible.

steps.title: Execute and Recite Loop
steps.description: The agent converts one route, then recites and rewrites the plan. This loop repeats: execute a step, re-emit the updated todo, move to the next step.

steps.title: Update the Todo Artifact
steps.description: After step 12 and again after step 40 the todo is rewritten: completed routes are checked off and the next target is marked. The artifact is the single source of truth for progress.

steps.title: Objective Stays in Recent Context
steps.description: Because the plan is re-emitted at the tail of the context every turn, the objective sits in recent attention, and the checked items serve as external memory so no file is ever re-converted.

steps.title: Guard Against Drift
steps.description: The drift guard confirms the objective is unchanged across all 50 steps. Without recitation the goal would sink into the lost-in-the-middle dead zone, causing drift and repeated work.

steps.title: Objective Preserved
steps.description: All 50 routes are migrated, contract tests pass, and the original goal is honored end to end with no drift into unrelated refactors.

name: World-Model Simulation Planning(WMSP)
description: The agent maintains, or uses the LLM itself as, a world model that predicts the next state and consequence of each candidate action, then runs look-ahead rollouts ("imagine before acting") to score and select an action before executing anything in the real environment. This extends model-based reinforcement learning to language agents and matters most where actions are irreversible and backtracking on a live website or GUI is impossible. Distinct from scenario-planning, which reasons across several strategic futures with no action-consequence simulator, and from reflective-mcts, which searches over reasoning traces rather than simulated environment states.
features: LLM or learned model simulates the outcome of each candidate action
Look-ahead rollouts score actions before any real execution
Avoids irreversible mistakes on live web and GUI environments
Value function or scorer ranks the simulated end states
More efficient than tree search that cannot backtrack a live action
Self-evolving variants update the world model from prediction errors

tldr.what: Agent simulates outcomes of candidate actions using an LLM or learned model, scores them, then executes the best one in the real environment.
tldr.when: Irreversible actions on live websites or GUIs where backtracking is impossible or costly and mistakes carry high consequences.
tldr.watchOut: Simulation errors compound: a wrong prediction early in the rollout cascades into poor action selection despite correct scoring logic.

flow.title: World-Model Simulation Planning
flow.description: A web agent uses the LLM as a world model to simulate the consequence of each candidate action and run look-ahead rollouts before executing anything, so it picks a reversible action instead of an irreversible one on a live site.

nodes.label:
🎯 User Goal
"Remove the ACME newsletter from my inbox"

🤖 Web Agent
Model-based planner

👁️ Observe State
Inbox DOM: message row + action buttons

🧭 Candidate Actions
Delete / Archive / Unsubscribe+Archive

🔮 World Model (LLM)
Simulate the next state per action

🅰️ sim: Delete
Message gone permanently
(irreversible)

🅱️ sim: Archive
Leaves inbox, kept in All Mail

🅲 sim: Unsubscribe+Archive
Stops future + leaves inbox

📊 Value Scorer
Score each simulated end state

🧮 Scores
Delete 0.4 | Archive 0.8 | Unsub 0.9

⛔ Irreversibility Check
Delete is permanent -> reject

✅ Select Action
argmax value = Unsubscribe+Archive

🖱️ Execute for Real
Unsubscribe -> confirm -> Archive

⚠️ Reactive Agent (no world model)
Clicks first button = Delete -> data loss

📥 Real Inbox State
Inbox -1, newsletter unsubscribed

✨ Outcome
Correct, reversible cleanup; nothing lost

steps.title: Goal Received
steps.description: The agent is asked to remove a newsletter from the inbox on a live email site where some actions cannot be undone.

steps.title: Observe and Enumerate
steps.description: The agent reads the current page state and lists the candidate actions available at the message row: Delete, Archive, and Unsubscribe+Archive.

steps.title: Imagine Outcomes
steps.description: The LLM acts as a world model and simulates the resulting state for each candidate action without clicking anything for real.

steps.title: Score Simulated States
steps.description: A value scorer ranks each imagined end state against the goal: Delete 0.4 (over-destructive), Archive 0.8, Unsubscribe+Archive 0.9.

steps.title: Reject the Irreversible Action
steps.description: The simulation of Delete shows permanent, unrecoverable loss; the irreversibility check rejects it even before value comparison.

steps.title: Select Highest-Value Action
steps.description: The planner takes the argmax over the safe simulated actions and selects Unsubscribe+Archive.

steps.title: Execute for Real
steps.description: Only now does the agent act in the real environment: Unsubscribe, confirm, then Archive, reaching a correct and reversible inbox state.

steps.title: Contrast: Reactive Agent
steps.description: A reactive agent with no world model skips simulation and greedily clicks the first prominent button (Delete), causing irreversible data loss.

references: Is Your LLM Secretly a World Model of the Internet? Model-Based Planning for Web Agents - Gu et al. (ArXiv 2024) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.06559
Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning - Zhang et al. (ArXiv 2026) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30639

name: A2A Protocol (Agent2Agent)(A2A)
description: Open standard for AI agent interoperability enabling seamless collaboration across platforms

tldr.what: Agents discover each other's capabilities via standardized cards, then exchange messages with task IDs to coordinate work across platforms.
tldr.when: Multiple independent agents from different systems need to collaborate on long-running tasks with real-time state synchronization.
tldr.watchOut: High implementation complexity and operational overhead often outweigh benefits unless you genuinely need cross-platform interoperability at scale.

overview.pattern: Open standard enabling seamless interoperability between AI agents across platforms
overview.why: Eliminates vendor lock-in, enables agent ecosystems, accelerates enterprise adoption with standardized communication
overview.insight: Universal Agent Card discovery + OAuth auth + Task ID correlation + SSE streaming = cross-platform collaboration
dos: Use standard Agent Card format for capability discovery
Implement proper OAuth 2.0 or JWT authentication
Support Server-Sent Events for real-time updates
Use unique Task IDs for correlation and tracking
Handle network failures with exponential backoff
Implement message versioning for compatibility
Use schema-first contracts for messages and artifacts
Prevent circular agent loops with hop-count limits
donts: Hardcode agent endpoints or capabilities
Send sensitive data without encryption
Ignore task lifecycle state management
Block on synchronous calls to remote agents
Skip capability validation before task delegation
Use long-lived or overly broad tokens

metrics.d: Time to fetch & parse Agent Card

Agents sharing model updates while preserving data locality
Supplier, manufacturer, and logistics agents coordinating via A2A
