name: Agent Communication Protocols
description: Standardized communication mechanisms for agent interaction including message passing, publish-subscribe, and event-driven patterns

tldr.what: Agents exchange work through message queues, topics, or events rather than direct calls, enabling asynchronous decoupling and selective routing.
tldr.when: Multiple agents must coordinate without blocking, or when some agents need to react to events published by others independently.
tldr.watchOut: Message ordering and delivery guarantees become critical; lost or delayed messages can silently break downstream workflows without obvious failure signals.

overview.pattern: Comprehensive communication protocols for agent interaction including REST APIs, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSocket, SSE, and message queuing
overview.why: Enables flexible synchronous/asynchronous communication, real-time updates, efficient data transfer, and scalable multi-protocol coordination
overview.insight: Multi-protocol support + standardized interfaces + real-time capabilities = robust agent communication

impl.d: Select REST, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSocket, SSE, or Message Queue based on needs
Design API contracts, message schemas, or event structures with versioning
Deploy API gateways, message brokers, load balancers, and monitoring
Add protocol handlers, error handling, authentication, and rate limiting
Track latency, throughput, error rates, and connection health

overview.example: REST API ↔ gRPC ↔ GraphQL ↔ WebSocket ↔ Message Queue → Multi-Protocol Agent Network
dos: Choose appropriate protocol: REST for CRUD, gRPC for performance, GraphQL for flexibility
Use WebSocket for real-time bidirectional communication and SSE for server-push updates
Implement proper API versioning, schema evolution, and backward compatibility
Add comprehensive error handling, timeouts, circuit breakers, and retry logic
Use Protocol Buffers for gRPC efficiency and OpenAPI specs for REST documentation
Implement authentication (OAuth2, JWT) and rate limiting across all protocols
donts: Use only one protocol - different use cases require different communication patterns
Ignore connection management for WebSocket and proper cleanup for SSE streams
Skip load balancing and service discovery for distributed agent networks
Use REST for real-time communication or gRPC for simple CRUD operations
Allow unbounded GraphQL queries or missing depth limiting protections
use: Multi-protocol agent networks requiring flexible communication patterns
Real-time collaboration with bidirectional WebSocket communication
RESTful agent services with standard CRUD operations and HTTP semantics
High-performance inter-agent calls using gRPC and Protocol Buffers
Complex data querying needs with GraphQL flexible query capabilities
Server-push notifications and live updates using SSE streams
avoid: Simple single-protocol systems where complexity is unnecessary
Environments with strict network restrictions blocking multiple ports
Legacy systems unable to support modern protocol implementations
Ultra-constrained devices with minimal processing capabilities
Applications with extremely simple point-to-point communication needs

metrics.d: Messages per second processed by the communication system
P50/P95 time from message send to agent processing
Percentage of messages successfully delivered and acknowledged
Average and maximum message backlog per topic/queue
Number of parallel message handlers per agent
Bandwidth usage and connection efficiency across agents

WebSocket for live market data, REST for order management, GraphQL for complex portfolio queries, and message queues for settlement
SSE for streaming responses, WebSocket for conversational flow, REST for session management, and GraphQL for context retrieval
gRPC for low-latency sensor data, MQTT for telemetry, REST for fleet management APIs, and WebSocket for real-time coordination

name: Supervisor-Worker Pattern(SVW)
description: Orchestrator-worker architecture where a lead agent coordinates specialized subagents for parallel task execution

tldr.what: A lead agent breaks work into parallel tasks, spawns specialized subagents to handle each, and collects results for synthesis or quality checks.
tldr.when: Complex problems decomposable into independent subtasks where parallel execution saves time and specialized agents improve accuracy per domain.
tldr.watchOut: Coordination overhead and result merging complexity often exceed gains unless tasks are truly independent and subagent failures are handled explicitly.

overview.pattern: Orchestrator-worker architecture where a lead agent coordinates specialized subagents for parallel task execution
overview.why: Achieves 90% performance improvement through parallel exploration and specialized expertise while maintaining centralized quality control
overview.insight: Dynamic task decomposition + separate worker contexts + real-time coordination = superior research quality at 15x token cost

impl.d: Aggregate all findings into final result

dos: Use separate context windows for each worker agent
Implement dynamic worker spawning based on complexity
Monitor worker progress and adjust strategies in real-time
Set clear objectives and success criteria for each worker
Use interleaved thinking for worker self-evaluation
Implement timeout and failure handling for workers
Cache expensive operations and intermediate results
Use structured output formats for worker communication
donts: Create too many workers (diminishing returns after 5-7)
Share context between workers (reduces parallel benefits)
Ignore token consumption explosion (15x normal usage)
Skip quality control in final synthesis step
Use for simple queries that don't need decomposition
Forget to implement worker error propagation handling

name: Shared Scratchpad Collaboration(SSC)
description: Multiple agents collaborate transparently on a common workspace with shared visibility of all work

tldr.what: Multiple agents write to and read from a shared workspace, each seeing all prior work and building incrementally on it.
tldr.when: Complex documents or outputs requiring different expertise, where agents benefit from seeing each other's contributions before adding their own.
tldr.watchOut: Agents may contradict or overwrite each other's work if conflict resolution and ordering rules are not explicit.

overview.pattern: Multiple agents collaborate transparently on a common workspace with shared visibility of all work
overview.why: Eliminates information silos, enables natural collaboration flow, and provides transparent decision-making through real-time visibility
overview.insight: Shared state + real-time visibility + progressive building + transparent process = natural collaborative intelligence

impl.d: Create shared state/workspace accessible to all agents
Establish collaboration protocols and update formats
Agents read, contribute, and build upon shared work
Real-time visibility of all agent contributions

dos: Design clear shared state schema with structured sections
Implement real-time visibility of all agent contributions
Use version control and conflict resolution mechanisms
Establish clear protocols for agent contribution formats
Enable progressive building and iterative refinement
Implement proper access control and edit permissions
Maintain clear audit trails of all contributions
Design for transparent decision-making processes
donts: Allow unstructured or conflicting update formats
Create information silos between agents
Skip conflict resolution for simultaneous edits
Ignore the computational overhead of shared state
Allow agents to overwrite each other without coordination
Forget to implement rollback mechanisms for errors

metrics.d: % time agents building vs duplicating work

name: Sequential Pipeline Agents(SPA)
description: Specialized agents process tasks in a linear pipeline where each agent's output becomes the next agent's input

tldr.what: Breaks work into ordered stages where each specialized agent processes output from the previous stage before passing results forward.
tldr.when: Multi-stage workflows where each phase needs different expertise and intermediate results benefit from validation before proceeding.
tldr.watchOut: Errors or poor quality at early stages compound downstream, wasting effort in later agents on flawed inputs.

overview.pattern: Specialized agents process tasks sequentially where each agent's output feeds the next agent's input
overview.why: Enables expertise specialization, quality control gates, independent optimization, and clear error isolation per stage
overview.insight: Linear agent pipeline with validation checkpoints - each stage optimized for specific capabilities

impl.d: Chain agents with validation & error handling

dos: Design agents for single, specialized responsibilities
Use structured data formats between agents (JSON/schemas)
Implement quality checkpoints at each stage transition
Add circuit breakers for failed stages
Log detailed execution traces for debugging
Cache intermediate results for expensive stages
donts: Create monolithic agents handling multiple concerns
Allow unstructured data to flow between stages
Skip validation between pipeline stages
Let pipeline failures cascade without recovery
Ignore stage-specific performance bottlenecks
use: Tasks requiring specialized expertise per stage
Workflows where stages can be independently optimized
avoid: Tasks requiring dynamic branching or loops

name: Concurrent Orchestration(CO)
description: Multiple agents work simultaneously on the same task to provide diverse perspectives and parallel processing power

tldr.what: Multiple agents analyze the same task in parallel, each from a different angle, then results combine into a unified output.
tldr.when: Complex decisions needing diverse expertise where speed matters more than sequential refinement of a single analysis.
tldr.watchOut: Conflicting agent conclusions require explicit resolution logic or you get contradictory recommendations instead of clarity.

overview.pattern: Multiple agents execute the same task concurrently to provide diverse perspectives and ensemble reasoning
overview.why: Harnesses collective intelligence, reduces bias through diversity, increases accuracy via consensus, and accelerates decision-making
overview.insight: Parallel execution + diverse expertise + consensus mechanisms = superior decision quality and speed

impl.d: Create diverse agents with complementary expertise
Configure concurrent processing with shared inputs
Add voting/aggregation mechanisms for result synthesis
Track performance metrics and optimize throughput

overview.example: FinancialAgent ∥ MarketAgent ∥ RiskAgent ∥ TechAgent → Consensus → Decision
dos: Design agents with truly diverse perspectives and expertise
Use confidence-weighted voting for better consensus quality
Implement timeout mechanisms to prevent blocking operations
Cache results to avoid redundant processing across agents
Monitor consensus quality and agent contribution metrics
Use structured output formats for consistent aggregation
donts: Create agents with overlapping roles and identical perspectives
Use simple majority voting without considering expertise levels
Allow infinite processing time without deadlock protection
Ignore resource contention and memory pressure issues
Accept first consensus without quality validation
use: Need diverse perspectives on complex decisions
Parallel processing can reduce overall latency
avoid: Simple tasks with clear optimal solutions
When agent coordination overhead exceeds benefits

metrics.d: Variance in agent perspectives and solutions
Time spent in synchronization and aggregation

name: Handoff Orchestration(HO)
description: Dynamic delegation where agents intelligently transfer control based on context and specialized capabilities

tldr.what: Routes requests between specialized agents based on detected context, transferring full state and control to the best-matched agent.
tldr.when: Problems span multiple domains where different agents excel, and routing decisions depend on issue content rather than fixed rules.
tldr.watchOut: Handoffs can loop or stall if agents misclassify problems or context gets corrupted during transfer between systems.

overview.pattern: Dynamic delegation where agents intelligently transfer control based on context and specialized capabilities
overview.why: Enables right expertise at right time, preserves conversation continuity, optimizes resource utilization, and improves outcome quality
overview.insight: Context-preserving handoffs + capability routing + intelligent escalation = seamless expert delegation

impl.d: Define handoff context schema and preservation rules
Map agent capabilities and routing logic
Define triggering conditions and routing decisions
Track handoff success and context continuity

dos: Preserve complete conversation context during transfers
Use structured handoff messages with metadata
Implement capability-based routing with confidence scores
Add graceful fallback mechanisms for failed handoffs
Log handoff decisions for audit and optimization
Use standardized protocols like Model Context Protocol
donts: Lose context information during agent transitions
Create circular handoff loops between agents
Hand off without checking recipient agent availability
Ignore handoff failures and continue processing
Use hardcoded routing without dynamic capability assessment
use: Tasks require specialized expertise at different stages
Dynamic routing based on conversation analysis
avoid: Simple tasks that single agents can handle
Real-time systems where handoff latency is critical
Workflows with unclear handoff trigger conditions
Systems without proper context management infrastructure
Scenarios where all agents have similar capabilities

metrics.d: Correct agent selection based on capabilities

name: Peer Collaboration
description: Decentralized collaboration between equal agents without central authority

tldr.what: Multiple agents communicate directly, debate findings, and reach consensus without a coordinator deciding outcomes.
tldr.when: Problems needing diverse expertise where no single agent should dominate, and disagreement signals important blind spots.
tldr.watchOut: Consensus-seeking often deadlocks or converges on mediocre compromise rather than discovering the strongest answer.

overview.pattern: Decentralized collaboration between equal agents without central authority using peer-to-peer communication
overview.why: Eliminates single points of failure, enables cross-organizational cooperation, harnesses collective intelligence, and provides Byzantine fault tolerance
overview.insight: P2P topology + consensus mechanisms + self-organization = resilient distributed intelligence

impl.d: Define peer-to-peer communication topology and protocols
Implement voting, reputation, and agreement mechanisms
Enable dynamic role assignment and task distribution
Add negotiation and dispute resolution protocols
Implement collective intelligence and knowledge sharing

overview.example: AgentA ↔ AgentB ↔ AgentC → Consensus → Collective Decision
dos: Implement robust consensus mechanisms for critical decisions
Enable dynamic topology adaptation based on agent performance
Use reputation systems to weight agent contributions
Design fault-tolerant protocols for agent failures
Implement privacy-preserving communication when needed
Enable emergent behavior through local interaction rules
donts: Create single points of failure in the peer network
Allow unchecked consensus manipulation by malicious agents
Ignore network partition and Byzantine fault scenarios
Use synchronous protocols that block on slow peers
Neglect scalability limits in peer-to-peer architectures
use: Research collaboration and peer review processes
Systems requiring fault tolerance and resilience
avoid: Simple problems solvable by single agents

metrics.d: Performance under node failures and attacks
Variety of perspectives and solutions generated

usecases.d: Distributed peer review with consensus-based evaluation and knowledge synthesis across institutions
Decentralized validation with Byzantine fault tolerance and proof-of-stake mechanisms for secure transactions
Peer-based code review, collaborative debugging, and consensus-driven architecture decisions
Multi-party consensus for logistics, quality control, and compliance across organizational boundaries

name: Hierarchical Coordination(HC)
description: Multi-level agent coordination with supervisory relationships, centralized orchestration, and authority delegation

tldr.what: Organizes multiple agents into supervisor-subordinate levels, where higher tiers delegate tasks, allocate resources, and escalate exceptions downward.
tldr.when: Large systems needing clear accountability, resource constraints, quality gates, or policy enforcement across many parallel agent workflows.
tldr.watchOut: Bottlenecks at supervisory levels can starve subordinate agents; escalation chains delay urgent decisions if not carefully bounded.

overview.pattern: Multi-level agent coordination with supervisory relationships, centralized orchestration, and authority delegation
overview.why: Enables scalable task decomposition, policy enforcement, quality control, and clear accountability chains
overview.insight: Hierarchical structure + task delegation + escalation protocols = enterprise-grade coordination

impl.d: Establish supervisor-subordinate tiers with clear authority levels
Break complex goals into hierarchical subtasks (HTN-style)
Implement task assignment with acceptance criteria and SLAs
Define when and how issues bubble up hierarchy
Track execution, aggregate results, enforce policies

dos: Define explicit roles, permissions, and authority boundaries per tier
Use structured task specifications with clear success criteria
Implement bounded re-decomposition with recursion depth limits
Summarize between levels to control context growth
Use smaller models for routine tasks, larger for strategic decisions
Instrument comprehensive traces and audit logs per tier
donts: Create single points of failure at supervisor level
Allow excessive escalation that inflates latency and cost
Use ambiguous authority that blocks worker task completion
Forward full transcripts across tiers instead of summaries
Skip policy enforcement checks at higher tiers
use: Complex workflows requiring approval gates and oversight
Scenarios requiring clear authority and accountability
Multi-step processes with quality control checkpoints
Operations needing resource authorization and allocation
avoid: Simple single-step tasks without coordination needs
Real-time systems where review latency breaks SLAs
Small teams where hierarchy creates unnecessary overhead
Highly dynamic environments requiring rapid adaptation

metrics.d: P50/P95 processing time per hierarchical level
Percentage of tasks requiring higher-tier review
Violations caught and resolved at checkpoints
Cost and compute efficiency across tiers

usecases.d: Multi-tier approval processes for compliance, finance, procurement with policy enforcement
Command hierarchy with incident commander, team leads, and specialists for systematic resolution
Principal investigator, project managers, research teams with peer review and publication oversight
Plant managers, line supervisors, operators with quality control and safety protocols
Architects, tech leads, developers with code review, testing, and deployment approval gates

name: Consensus Algorithms
description: Distributed agreement mechanisms for multi-agent decision making

tldr.what: Multiple agents vote or propose decisions, weighted by confidence or stake, until reaching agreement despite some agents failing or acting maliciously.
tldr.when: Distributed systems where no single agent is trusted, and you need binding decisions that survive agent failures or Byzantine behavior.
tldr.watchOut: Consensus overhead grows exponentially with agent count; slow convergence or deadlock under adversarial conditions wastes compute and delays decisions.

overview.pattern: Distributed agreement mechanisms ensuring safety and liveness in multi-agent systems with Byzantine fault tolerance
overview.why: Enables trustless coordination, handles malicious actors, guarantees consistency, and provides economic security in decentralized systems
overview.insight: Byzantine fault tolerance + economic incentives + cryptographic proofs = trustless distributed consensus

impl.d: Choose CFT, BFT, or probabilistic based on threat model
Configure validator set, quorum sizes, and voting weights
Deploy consensus mechanism with proposal and voting phases
Handle leader changes, timeouts, and view transitions
Track finality, throughput, and Byzantine resilience

overview.example: Agents → Propose → Vote → Quorum → Commit → Finality
dos: Choose protocol family matching your fault model: CFT for crashes, BFT for adversarial behavior
Size quorums correctly (majority for CFT, 2f+1 for BFT) and document safety invariants
Implement proper timeouts, view changes, and leader rotation mechanisms
Monitor consensus metrics: finality time, fork rates, participation, message complexity
Use signature aggregation (BLS) and batching to improve scalability
Test with chaos engineering: network partitions, clock skews, Byzantine scenarios
donts: Assume perfect synchrony - design for partial synchrony with bounded delays
Allow O(n²) message complexity without aggregation in large committees
Create leader bottlenecks or single points of failure
Ignore validator concentration and centralization risks in PoS systems
Deploy without comprehensive monitoring of safety and liveness violations
use: Distributed systems requiring strong consistency guarantees
Multi-agent systems needing Byzantine fault tolerance
Blockchain networks with economic security requirements
Control planes and metadata stores requiring durability
Committee-based decision making with voting mechanisms
Systems where trust assumptions need formal guarantees
avoid: Single-writer systems where primary databases suffice
Ultra-low-latency paths that cannot tolerate consensus delays
Simple aggregation tasks not requiring strong consistency
Teams lacking operational maturity for validator management
Applications where eventual consistency is acceptable

metrics.d: Transactions per second under normal and adverse conditions
P50/P95 time from proposal to irreversible commitment
Frequency of consensus reversals and safety violations
Percentage of validators actively participating in consensus
Maximum fraction of malicious validators tolerated

usecases.d: Public chains (Ethereum PoS), permissioned ledgers, and DeFi protocols requiring economic finality
Consensus-based replication for critical data with strong consistency (etcd, CockroachDB)
Committee voting for model outputs, confidence-weighted aggregation, and distributed inference
Multi-party consensus for logistics, compliance, and quality control across organizations
Trade settlement, clearing and settlement networks, and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs)

tldr.when: Complex decisions with legitimate competing priorities where no single expert perspective captures the full picture.
tldr.watchOut: Debate can mask uncertainty as consensus; models may converge on plausible-sounding answers without ground truth validation.

steps.input:
Advocate counters: "Startup complexity is temporary, scaling benefits are permanent..."

name: Mixture of Agents(MoA)
description: Layered ensemble in which multiple LLM proposer agents at each layer receive all responses from the previous layer as auxiliary context, iteratively refining their answers before a final aggregator synthesizes them. Because models produce better answers when shown peer responses, a stack of open-source proposers can outperform a single frontier model.
features: Each layer conditions on all prior-layer outputs

tldr.what: Stack of LLM agents iteratively refines answers by conditioning each layer on all prior-layer outputs, then aggregates into a final response.
tldr.when: Complex problems where diverse model perspectives improve quality and open-source models together can match or exceed frontier model performance.
tldr.watchOut: Latency and cost scale linearly with layers and proposers; diminishing returns often plateau after 2-3 layers, wasting compute.

flow.title: Mixture of Agents (MoA)
flow.description: Layered ensemble where each layer of LLM proposer agents sees all outputs from the previous layer as auxiliary context and refines the answer, before a final aggregator synthesizes the best of all responses. Layered open-source proposers can beat a single frontier model on AlpacaEval 2.0 (65.1% vs 57.5%).

steps.title: Prompt Received
steps.description: A single hard prompt enters the MoA stack. The same prompt is broadcast to every proposer in layer 1.

steps.title: Layer 1: Independent Drafts
steps.description: Three heterogeneous open-source proposers answer independently, each emphasizing a different angle (PLG, integrations, compliance).

steps.title: Concatenate Layer-1 Outputs
steps.description: All three layer-1 drafts are concatenated into an auxiliary context that will be shown to the next layer.

steps.title: Layer 2: Refine on Peer Responses
steps.description: Each layer-2 proposer sees ALL layer-1 responses and refines: merging PLG with integrations, adding pricing tiers and ICP, folding in compliance.

steps.title: Layer 3: Final Refinement
steps.description: Layer-2 outputs are concatenated and passed to layer 3, which reconciles contradictions, tightens phase sequencing, and adds KPIs.

steps.title: Aggregate
steps.description: The aggregator reads the final layer of proposals and synthesizes a single best-of-all plan rather than picking one.

steps.title: Final Answer

name: Ledger Orchestration (Magentic-One)(LO)
description: An orchestrator drives a team of specialized agents using two ledgers: a task ledger holding facts, educated guesses, and a plan, and a progress ledger where the orchestrator self-reflects each step on whether progress is being made, whether the team is stalled, and which agent should act next. When progress stalls, an outer loop updates the facts and revises the plan. Introduced in Microsoft Magentic-One.
features: Task ledger: facts, educated guesses, and current plan
Progress ledger: per-step self-reflection on progress
Stall detection via a counter and threshold
Outer loop replans and updates facts when stuck
Generalist team: WebSurfer, FileSurfer, Coder, ComputerTerminal

tldr.what: Orchestrator maintains a task ledger of facts and plan, uses a progress ledger to self-reflect each step, detects stalls by counter, and replans when stuck.
tldr.when: Complex multi-step tasks requiring web search, file handling, coding, and terminal work where the team needs dynamic redirection when progress halts.
tldr.watchOut: Stall detection threshold and replanning logic must be tuned carefully or the system loops endlessly or gives up too early.

flow.description: An orchestrator drives a generalist team using a task ledger (facts, guesses, plan) and a progress ledger (per-step self-reflection: progress being made? stalled? who acts next?). An outer loop updates facts and replans when progress stalls. Based on Microsoft Magentic-One.

steps.description: WebSurfer is blocked by a cookie wall for two turns. The progress ledger stall counter trips, signaling no real progress.

steps.title: Outer Loop Replan
steps.description: The orchestrator enters the outer loop: it updates the task ledger facts ("site X blocks bots") and revises the plan to use an alternate site, then resumes.

steps.title: Coder + Terminal Finish
steps.description: With a workable plan, Coder emits a parser and ComputerTerminal runs it to extract the five cheapest direct flights.

steps.title: Completion
steps.description: The progress ledger reports the request satisfied. flights.csv is written with 5 rows. This orchestrator posted competitive results on GAIA, AssistantBench, and WebArena.

name: Chain of Agents(CoA)
description: A training-free framework for long-context tasks that splits an oversized input into chunks, assigns each chunk to a worker agent that reads its chunk plus a running communication unit passed from the previous worker, then hands the final accumulated communication to a manager agent that produces the answer. The sequential read-and-summarize chain mitigates long-context focus loss and beats RAG and full-context baselines.
features: Worker agents read their chunk plus the prior communication unit
A running evidence summary accumulates left to right
Manager agent synthesizes the final answer
Handles inputs beyond a single model context window

tldr.what: Splits input into chunks, routes each to worker agents that read their chunk plus accumulated prior findings, then a manager synthesizes the final answer.
tldr.when: Documents or contexts exceed a single model's window and need systematic extraction across many pages without losing earlier findings.
tldr.watchOut: Worker agents may miss or misinterpret context that spans chunk boundaries, degrading answer quality if splits fall at critical junctures.

flow.title: Chain of Agents (CoA)
flow.description: A long-context input is split into chunks; each worker agent reads its chunk plus a running communication unit passed from the previous worker, accumulating evidence left to right. name: Parametric Memory(PM)
description: Knowledge implicitly stored within model parameters, enabling fast context-free knowledge retrieval for multi-agent agentic AI systems

tldr.what: Stores domain knowledge in model weights during training, letting agents retrieve facts and patterns without explicit context or retrieval systems.
tldr.when: Multi-agent systems where agents need fast, shared access to common knowledge without querying external databases or passing large context windows.
tldr.watchOut: Knowledge becomes stale or incorrect if the base model is outdated, and you cannot easily update or correct specific facts without retraining.

overview.pattern: Knowledge implicitly stored within model parameters, enabling fast context-free access
overview.why: Sub-millisecond retrieval, no external dependencies, consistent across agents, scales to 1000+ agents
overview.insight: Pre-trained knowledge → PEFT specialization → shared base parameters across agent network

impl.d: Embed domain knowledge in model weights
Use PEFT methods (LoRA, QLoRA) for efficiency

dos: Use parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, QLoRA, MoRA)
Share base parameters across agent network for consistency
Monitor parameter specialization patterns for knowledge storage
Implement knowledge consolidation to prevent parameter bloat
Version control model parameters for rollback capability
donts: Full parameter retraining for new knowledge (expensive & risky)
Store time-sensitive information in parametric memory
Ignore knowledge cutoff dates and factual accuracy degradation
Deploy without parameter redundancy for fault tolerance
Mix incompatible parameter versions across agent instances

usecases.d: Physics, chemistry, biology knowledge embedded (consistent across 100+ agents)
Case law, statutes, procedures in parameters (instant access, no external DB)
Medical knowledge, drug interactions, symptoms (HIPAA-compliant, offline)
Market fundamentals, accounting principles, regulations (real-time inference)
Programming languages, frameworks, best practices (multi-language consistency)

name: Episodic Memory Systems(EMS)
description: Time-indexed memory of specific experiences and events, storing autobiographical history of agent interactions for multi-agent agentic AI systems

tldr.what: Stores timestamped records of agent interactions and events, indexed by time, enabling agents to recall specific past experiences and their context across sessions.
tldr.when: Multi-agent systems where agents need to learn from prior interactions, detect patterns across time, or maintain consistent behavior based on shared history.
tldr.watchOut: Storage and retrieval costs grow rapidly; querying old episodes becomes slow without careful indexing, and irrelevant memories can mislead decisions.

overview.pattern: Time-indexed memory of specific experiences and events, storing agent interaction history
overview.why: Experience-based learning, pattern recognition from past interactions, continuity across sessions
overview.insight: Episodes = Context + Outcome + Timestamp → Pattern recognition → Improved future decisions

impl.d: Extract recurring patterns from episode history

dos: Include rich contextual metadata (participants, outcomes, confidence)
Use hierarchical timestamps (session > interaction > sub-action)
Implement semantic similarity search for episode retrieval
Store both successful and failed episodes for learning
Enable cross-agent episode sharing and pattern recognition
donts: Store only successful outcomes (learn from failures too)
Use episode storage for frequently changing factual data
Ignore privacy constraints when sharing episodes across agents
Store episodes without sufficient context for future understanding
Let episode storage grow indefinitely without pruning strategies

usecases.d: Multi-agent system remembers customer preferences, past issues, resolution patterns (85% faster issue resolution)
Episodes of patient interactions, treatment responses, outcome patterns (personalized care protocols)
Student learning episodes, misconception patterns, successful explanation strategies (adaptive teaching methods)
Code review episodes, bug patterns, successful debugging approaches (knowledge transfer across developers)
Client interaction history, market response episodes, successful strategy patterns (personalized investment advice)

name: Semantic Memory Networks(SMN)
description: General world knowledge systems divorced from specific acquisition context, supporting factual knowledge and concept relationships for multi-agent agentic AI systems

tldr.what: Stores factual knowledge and concept relationships in a shared graph structure, enabling agents to query and link information across domains without needing original context.
tldr.when: Multiple agents need consistent access to world facts, concept hierarchies, or domain relationships that persist across conversations and queries.
tldr.watchOut: Knowledge graphs become stale or inconsistent when updates from different agents conflict, and semantic similarity matching can return plausible but incorrect connections.

overview.pattern: General world knowledge systems divorced from acquisition context, supporting factual reasoning
overview.why: Context-independent knowledge access, cross-domain reasoning, consistent facts across agents
overview.insight: Concepts + Relationships + Embeddings → Multi-hop reasoning → Cross-agent knowledge consistency

impl.d: Create knowledge graph with concepts & relationships
Generate semantic embeddings for all entities

dos: Use hierarchical concept organization (parent-child relationships)
Implement semantic similarity scoring for concept retrieval
Enable multi-hop reasoning across concept relationships
Maintain consistent ontologies across all agents in the network
Version control knowledge graphs for reproducible reasoning
donts: Store time-sensitive or rapidly changing information
Create overly complex relationship hierarchies (keep interpretable)
Ignore semantic consistency when merging knowledge from different sources
Let knowledge graphs grow without pruning irrelevant connections
Use for personal or context-specific information storage

usecases.d: Physics, chemistry, biology concepts linked across disciplines (enables cross-domain discovery)
Diseases, symptoms, treatments, drug interactions in semantic network (diagnostic reasoning)
Laws, precedents, regulations, jurisdiction relationships (legal research & compliance)
Markets, instruments, regulations, risk factors interconnected (investment analysis)
Software concepts, APIs, dependencies, best practices linked (developer assistance)

name: Transactive Memory Systems(TMS)
description: Shared system for storing and retrieving knowledge that expands multi-agent group capacity through distributed cognitive processing

tldr.what: Agents maintain shared knowledge of each other's expertise and delegate tasks based on specialization, expanding collective problem-solving capacity.
tldr.when: Multi-agent teams tackling complex projects where agents have distinct skills and need to route work efficiently without redundant processing.
tldr.watchOut: Expertise maps become stale quickly; agents may route to outdated specializations or miss capability shifts, degrading performance over time.

overview.pattern: Shared system storing knowledge that expands multi-agent group capacity through distributed expertise
overview.why: Emergent collective intelligence, efficient knowledge distribution, automatic expertise-based coordination
overview.insight: Expertise Directory + Intelligent Routing + Collaborative Synthesis → Collective intelligence > sum of parts

impl.d: Profile each agent's specialized knowledge domains
Direct questions to most knowledgeable agents

dos: Maintain dynamic expertise confidence scores for each agent
Enable cross-training between agents to fill knowledge gaps
Implement redundancy for critical knowledge domains
Track collaboration success rates to optimize team composition
Design graceful degradation when expert agents are unavailable
donts: Create single points of failure with hyper-specialized agents
Ignore load balancing - distribute expertise requests efficiently
Let expertise mappings become stale without regular updates
Assume static expertise - allow agents to develop new capabilities
Overlook communication overhead between highly distributed expertise

usecases.d: Frontend, backend, DevOps, security agents with specialized knowledge (300% productivity increase)
Specialists in cardiology, neurology, radiology collaborating on complex cases (95% diagnostic accuracy)
Market analysts, risk assessors, compliance experts working together (automated investment strategies)
Chemistry, biology, physics agents combining expertise for drug discovery (accelerated research cycles)
Mechanical, electrical, software agents coordinating on complex product development (integrated system design)

name: Memory Reading/Writing Operations(MRWO)
description: Systematic operations for reading, writing, and managing memory access patterns based on recency, relevance, and importance for multi-agent agentic AI systems

tldr.what: Retrieves and stores agent memories using weighted scores combining recency, relevance, and importance to prioritize what each agent accesses.
tldr.when: Multi-agent systems where agents share context and need fast access to the most useful prior interactions without scanning all history.
tldr.watchOut: Weight tuning is fragile; small changes to coefficients can cause agents to ignore critical information or thrash on irrelevant old data.

overview.pattern: Systematic operations for reading, writing, and managing memory access based on intelligent scoring
overview.why: Optimized retrieval performance, multi-agent coordination, intelligent memory prioritization
overview.insight: Composite Scoring (R×0.3 + R×0.5 + I×0.2) + Caching + Concurrency Control → Intelligent memory access

impl.d: Use composite scoring for memory selection
Real-time scoring updates based on usage

dos: Use composite scoring: (Recency × 0.3) + (Relevance × 0.5) + (Importance × 0.2)
Implement read-write locks for multi-agent memory consistency
Cache frequently accessed memories with TTL expiration
Use approximate nearest neighbor search for large memory stores
Implement memory access patterns analytics for optimization
donts: Use fixed scoring weights - adapt to agent/domain needs
Ignore memory access conflicts in multi-agent environments
Cache without considering memory staleness and updates
Use linear search for large-scale memory retrieval
Forget to implement memory garbage collection strategies

usecases.d: 10M+ interaction history with 50ms retrieval (recency + customer relevance scoring)
User behavior patterns with real-time preference weighting (collaborative filtering optimization)
Context-aware dialogue history with semantic similarity ranking (coherent long conversations)
Corporate knowledge base with expertise-weighted retrieval (subject matter expert routing)
Shared world state with spatial-temporal memory access (coordinated decision making)

name: Hierarchical Memory
description: Multi-level memory structure with different retention policies

tldr.what: Organizes agent memory into tiers with different retention rules, automatically moving items between levels based on importance and access patterns.
tldr.when: Long-running agents handling thousands of interactions where keeping everything in active memory becomes too slow or expensive.
tldr.watchOut: Promotion and demotion logic can silently lose critical context if importance scoring misses what actually matters for your tasks.

overview.pattern: Multi-level memory structure with different retention policies and intelligent tier management
overview.why: Optimized storage costs, improved retrieval performance, adaptive resource allocation
overview.insight: Hot/Warm/Cold Data Tiers + Promotion Policies + Background Consolidation → Cost-efficient performance

impl.d: Create working, short-term, long-term, archival levels
Define promotion/demotion rules by access patterns
Dynamic tier sizing based on usage patterns

dos: Design tier boundaries based on access patterns (hot/warm/cold data)
Use intelligent promotion policies combining recency, frequency, importance
Implement efficient indexing optimized for each memory tier
Deploy background consolidation without blocking memory access
Monitor tier performance and adapt sizes dynamically
donts: Create overly complex hierarchies that slow down simple retrieval
Use fixed tier boundaries - adapt to workload characteristics
Ignore memory leaks in tier management causing unbounded growth
Let promotion policies become stale without access pattern updates
Implement hierarchy management harder to debug than flat memory
use: Large memory stores with varied access patterns
avoid: Uniform access patterns across all data
Real-time systems with strict latency requirements

usecases.d: Recent context in working memory, user preferences in long-term (40-60% token reduction)
Frequently accessed facts in hot tier, archives in cold storage (enterprise systems)
Active user profiles in memory, historical patterns in archives (recommendation engines)
Current projects in working tier, literature database in archival (academic systems)
Trending content in hot tier, older content in cost-efficient cold storage (media systems)

name: Contextual Structured Memory(CSM)
description: Memory organized in predefined, interpretable formats supporting symbolic reasoning and precise querying for multi-agent agentic AI systems

tldr.what: Organizes agent memory in predefined schemas with symbolic reasoning and precise querying, enabling structured knowledge graphs instead of unstructured text.
tldr.when: Multi-agent systems needing exact fact retrieval, filtering across many entities, or reasoning over relationships between structured data points.
tldr.watchOut: Schema design becomes a bottleneck; rigid structures break when real-world data doesn't fit predefined categories or requirements shift.

overview.pattern: Memory organized in predefined, interpretable formats supporting symbolic reasoning and precise queries
overview.why: Precise querying, formal logic reasoning, data integrity, consistent structured knowledge access
overview.insight: Schemas + Knowledge Graphs + Structured Queries + Symbolic Logic → Precise reasoning & consistency

impl.d: Implement knowledge graph with typed relationships

dos: Use standardized schemas (JSON Schema, RDF, OWL) for consistency
Implement precise query capabilities with structured filters
Enable symbolic reasoning with formal logic rules
Maintain referential integrity across knowledge graphs
Version control schemas and support backward compatibility
donts: Over-structure flexible data that benefits from loose schemas
Create overly complex schemas that are hard to understand
Ignore schema evolution and migration strategies
Use structured memory for highly dynamic unstructured content
Forget to validate data integrity when updating structures
use: Formal logic and symbolic reasoning needed

usecases.d: Company financials, ratios, regulations in structured schemas (SQL-like queries: "SELECT companies WHERE pe_ratio < 25 AND sector = 'technology'")
Laws, cases, precedents with formal relationship modeling (complex legal reasoning and precedent matching)
Research data with standardized ontologies and precise queries (materials science, drug discovery)
Business entities, processes, relationships in formal schemas (inventory, supply chain optimization)
Patient data, treatments, outcomes with medical ontologies (clinical decision support systems)

name: Contextual Unstructured Memory(CUM)
description: Explicit, modality-general memory system storing information across heterogeneous inputs for multi-agent agentic AI systems

tldr.what: Stores diverse input types (text, images, audio, structured data) in a shared, indexed memory accessible to multiple agents for content retrieval and coordination.
tldr.when: Multi-agent systems creating or processing heterogeneous content where agents need to reference each other's work or build on shared context across modalities.
tldr.watchOut: Memory bloat and retrieval latency grow quickly; indexing overhead and cross-modal search complexity can outpace benefits unless carefully scoped.

overview.pattern: Explicit, modality-general memory system storing heterogeneous information without rigid schemas
overview.why: Flexible content storage, cross-modal discovery, adaptive organization, emergent content relationships
overview.insight: Multimodal Embeddings + Schema-Free Storage + Contextual Metadata → Adaptive cross-modal memory
dos: Use multimodal embeddings (CLIP, ALIGN) for cross-modal similarity
Preserve rich contextual metadata alongside content
Implement hybrid storage: vectors + original content + metadata
Enable emergent organization through usage patterns
Support schema evolution and dynamic content types
donts: Force rigid schemas on inherently flexible content
Ignore modality-specific preprocessing and optimization
Store without contextual information about creation/usage
Use single-modal embeddings for multimodal content
Neglect computational costs of similarity search at scale
use: Multimodal content across text, images, audio, video
Dynamic content types requiring schema flexibility
Heterogeneous data integration from multiple sources
avoid: Highly structured data with stable schemas
Performance-critical applications requiring fast exact queries
Regulatory compliance requiring strict data validation
Resource-constrained environments with limited embedding capacity

metrics.d: New content types integrated without schema changes

usecases.d: Text writers, visual designers, audio producers, video editors sharing unstructured creative assets (78% more flexible vs structured databases)
Scientists storing papers, images, data, code, notes without predefined schemas (cross-modal pattern recognition)
Learning material development across text, visuals, audio, interactive elements (adaptive content organization)
Handling tickets with text, images, voice recordings, screen captures (flexible problem-solving knowledge base)
Marketing teams managing campaigns across multiple content types and formats (emergent content relationships)

name: Memory Consolidation
description: Process of strengthening and organizing memories over time

tldr.what: Periodically extracts patterns from raw interactions, removes duplicates, weights by importance, and forms reusable knowledge structures.
tldr.when: Long-running agents accumulating thousands of interactions where raw storage becomes unwieldy and retrieval slows down.
tldr.watchOut: Aggressive consolidation loses nuance; you may discard edge cases or minority patterns that matter for specific decisions.

overview.pattern: Process of strengthening and organizing memories over time through pattern extraction and schema formation
overview.why: Storage optimization, improved retrieval, pattern recognition, knowledge abstraction from experiences
overview.insight: Memory Fragments → Pattern Extraction → Redundancy Removal → Schema Formation → Organized Knowledge

impl.d: Gather memory fragments and experiences over time

dos: Schedule consolidation during low-activity periods to minimize interference
Use incremental multi-pass consolidation for different complexity levels
Implement quality validation through retrieval testing
Preserve critical details while generalizing common patterns
Monitor consolidation ROI: processing cost vs long-term savings
donts: Over-consolidate causing loss of important specific details
Ignore temporal aspects - some information is time-dependent
Consolidate without rollback mechanisms for quality issues
Use consolidation on frequently changing patterns
Let consolidation processes become more expensive than original storage
use: Large volumes of experiential data accumulating

usecases.d: Consolidate interaction patterns into service templates (40-70% storage reduction, faster resolution)
Extract generalizable knowledge from specific training experiences (continuous learning without catastrophic forgetting)
Organize findings from large-scale data collection into actionable insights (literature review automation)
Consolidate user behavior into preference models (behavioral pattern recognition and prediction)
Transform accumulated business experiences into operational best practices (institutional memory preservation)

name: Working Memory Patterns(WMP)
description: Short-term context management for active cognitive processing

tldr.what: Maintains a limited set of active facts and goals during problem-solving, discarding or archiving lower-priority items as capacity fills.
tldr.when: Multi-step tasks where the agent must track intermediate results, current goals, and constraints without re-reading the full context each step.
tldr.watchOut: Agents often retain too much or the wrong information, causing later steps to reference stale data or lose critical constraints.

overview.pattern: Capacity-limited active memory for cognitive processing with attention control and interference suppression
overview.why: Enables complex reasoning, multi-step tasks, real-time cognitive processing within bounded resource constraints
overview.insight: Central Executive + Limited Capacity (4±1 chunks) + Attention Control + Temporal Maintenance → Human-like cognitive processing

impl.d: Define working memory limits (4±1 chunks for complex tasks)
Implement central executive for selective information filtering
Load, maintain, update, clear information dynamically
Block irrelevant information and manage conflicts
Synchronize working memory across multi-agent system

dos: Use 4±1 item capacity for complex tasks (Cowan, 2001) vs 7±2 for simple items
Implement central executive for attention control and task switching
Use chunking strategies to group related information effectively
Apply rehearsal mechanisms to prevent 15-30 second decay
Monitor cognitive load and implement offloading when approaching limits
donts: Ignore individual differences in working memory capacity across agents
Let irrelevant information consume working memory without filtering
Assume unlimited capacity - working memory constraints are crucial
Forget to implement interference suppression for competing information
Overlook the temporal dynamics - information decays without maintenance
use: Complex multi-step reasoning requiring active information maintenance
Interactive systems with dynamic information updates
Multi-agent coordination needing shared cognitive state
Planning tasks with multiple constraints and goals
Learning systems integrating new with existing knowledge

metrics.d: Effective chunks maintained vs theoretical limit
Consistency of shared working memory states

usecases.d: Mathematical reasoning, code debugging, scientific analysis (maintain intermediate results across reasoning steps)
Conversation context management, user intent tracking (dynamic information updates within cognitive limits)
Shared task state, distributed problem solving (synchronized working memory across agent network)
Goal management, constraint satisfaction, resource allocation (juggle multiple factors within capacity limits)
Knowledge integration, skill acquisition, concept formation (active manipulation of new information with existing knowledge)

name: Distributed Memory Architectures(DMA)
description: Scalable memory systems distributed across multiple agents with coordinated access patterns and consistency mechanisms

tldr.what: Splits memory storage across multiple agents with protocols ensuring data consistency and coordinated reads/writes across nodes.
tldr.when: Many agents need shared state at scale, geographic distribution is required, or single memory bottleneck would limit throughput.
tldr.watchOut: Consistency protocols add latency and complexity; network partitions can cause divergent state or cascading failures across agents.

overview.pattern: Scalable memory systems distributed across multiple agents with coordinated access and consistency mechanisms
overview.why: Massive scale support, fault tolerance, geographic distribution, elastic scaling for large multi-agent systems
overview.insight: CAP Theorem Trade-offs + Consensus Protocols + Partitioning Strategy → Scalable fault-tolerant memory

impl.d: CAP theorem trade-offs: CP (consistency+partition) vs AP (availability+partition)
Consistent hashing, range-based, or agent-affinity sharding
Raft, PBFT, or blockchain consensus for coordination
Multi-master or master-slave with conflict resolution
Dynamic membership, load balancing, fault detection

dos: Choose consistency level based on use case: strong for transactions, eventual for scalability
Implement consistent hashing for uniform load distribution across memory nodes
Use vector clocks or logical timestamps for causally consistent ordering
Design for network partitions - implement graceful degradation patterns
Monitor system health: latency, throughput, consistency lag, partition events
donts: Assume strong consistency is always necessary - eventual consistency often sufficient
Ignore the CAP theorem trade-offs when designing distributed memory systems
Forget to handle Byzantine failures in adversarial multi-agent environments
Overlook network latency impacts on memory access patterns
Deploy without proper backup and disaster recovery mechanisms
use: High availability and fault tolerance requirements
Dynamic agent membership and elastic scaling
avoid: Strong consistency requirements with low latency

metrics.d: Time to propagate updates across all replicas
% uptime under network partitions and node failures
Memory and request distribution across nodes
Time to restore full functionality after failures

name: Generative Agents Memory(GAM)
description: Give an agent a memory stream of timestamped observations that is retrieved by a weighted score of recency, importance, and relevance rather than similarity alone. Periodically the agent reflects, synthesizing higher-level insights from recent memories and writing them back into the stream so they drive future planning. This is the design from the Stanford generative agents (Smallville) study.
features: Exponential recency decay on last access

tldr.what: Maintains timestamped observation stream scored by recency, importance, and relevance; periodically synthesizes insights back into stream to shape future decisions.
tldr.when: Long-running agents needing to learn patterns from past interactions and adapt behavior based on accumulated context over hours or days.
tldr.watchOut: Reflection synthesis can hallucinate patterns or drift agent behavior away from original intent if importance scoring lacks clear grounding.

flow.title: Generative Agents Memory
flow.description: A memory stream of timestamped observations retrieved by weighted recency, importance, and relevance. Periodic reflection synthesizes higher-level insights back into the stream, which then drive planning. This is the Stanford generative agents (Smallville) design.

steps.title: Observations Append to the Stream
steps.description: Throughout the day, timestamped observations are appended to an append-only memory stream: meetings moved, invites declined, early email replies.

steps.title: Query Triggers Retrieval
steps.description: The question "When to schedule the design review?" activates the retrieval scorer over the candidate memories in the stream.

steps.title: Score by Recency, Importance, Relevance
steps.description: Each memory is scored: exponential recency decay, LLM-rated importance (poignancy 1-10), and cosine relevance to the query. The three combine into one score.

steps.title: Reflection Synthesizes an Insight
steps.description: When accumulated importance crosses a threshold, reflection asks "What can I conclude?" over the top memories and synthesizes: "User prefers mornings, avoids after 4pm."

steps.title: Insight Written Back to the Stream
steps.description: The synthesized insight is written back into the memory stream as a high-importance memory, so future retrieval surfaces the conclusion, not just raw events.

steps.title: Planning Uses Insight and Memories
steps.description: The planner combines the synthesized insight with directly retrieved memories to propose 9:30am and explain the reasoning, driving believable long-horizon behavior.

name: Temporal Knowledge Graph Memory(TKG)
description: An agent memory substrate that stores facts as edges in a knowledge graph, each edge carrying explicit bi-temporal validity: valid time (when the fact was true in the world) and transaction time (when it was ingested). When new information contradicts an existing fact, the edge is invalidated by writing a t_invalid timestamp rather than deleted, so the graph can answer what was believed and when, and never serves a stale fact as current. This is the Zep and Graphiti design. Distinct from `semantic-memory-networks` and the static `knowledge-graph-construction` pattern in knowledge-representation, which model a graph with no time dimension or fact-supersession.
features: Facts stored as graph edges, not opaque vectors
Bi-temporal stamps: valid time plus transaction time
Contradiction invalidates an edge (writes t_invalid) instead of deleting it
Point-in-time queries reconstruct past belief states
Current-view queries filter to edges with no t_invalid
Incremental entity and relationship extraction from new events

tldr.what: Stores facts as graph edges with valid-time and transaction-time stamps, invalidating contradictions by marking t_invalid rather than deleting.
tldr.when: Long-running agents tracking entities where facts change over time and you need to query what was believed at any past moment without serving stale data.
tldr.watchOut: High operational cost: extraction, deduplication, and temporal index maintenance grow with fact volume; stale extraction can create false contradictions and bloat the graph.

flow.title: Temporal Knowledge Graph Memory
flow.description: Agent memory stores facts as knowledge-graph edges with bi-temporal validity. A contradicting event invalidates the old edge (sets t_invalid) instead of deleting it, so current-view queries return the new fact while point-in-time and audit queries still recover history.

nodes.label:
🟢 Jan 2026 Event
"I just moved to Austin"

🤖 Fact Extractor
Entities + relationships from the event

🕰️ Temporal Knowledge Graph
Edges carry valid_from / valid_to + ingested_at

🔗 Edge: User LIVES_IN Austin
valid_from 2026-01-10, valid_to null (open)

🟢 Mar 2027 Event
"We relocated to Denver last week"

⚠️ Contradiction Check
New fact conflicts with open Austin edge

🛑 Invalidate, not delete
Set Austin valid_to = 2027-03-01 (t_invalid)

🔗 Edge: User LIVES_IN Denver
valid_from 2027-03-01, valid_to null (open)

🔵 Current-view Query
"Where does the user live now?"

📤 Result: Denver
Filter valid_to = null. Stale Austin never served

🔵 Point-in-time Query
"Where did the user live in June 2026?"

📤 Result: Austin
valid_from <= Jun 2026 < valid_to. History kept

🧾 Audit Timeline
Austin [Jan26..Mar27], Denver [Mar27..now]

steps.title: Ingest the first fact
steps.description: The January event is extracted and written as an open edge with valid_from set and valid_to left null (still true).

steps.title: A contradicting life event arrives
steps.description: Fourteen months later the user moves. The contradiction check compares the new fact against the still-open Austin edge.

steps.title: Invalidate, do not delete
steps.description: Rather than removing the Austin edge, the system stamps it with valid_to = 2027-03-01 (t_invalid). The fact is retired, not erased.

steps.title: Write the new open edge
steps.description: A fresh Denver edge is written with valid_from = 2027-03-01 and valid_to null, becoming the current fact.

steps.title: Current-view query returns Denver
steps.description: Filtering to edges with valid_to = null returns Denver. The stale Austin fact is never served as current.

steps.title: Point-in-time query still returns Austin
steps.description: Asking where the user lived in June 2026 filters valid_from <= Jun 2026 < valid_to and correctly returns Austin. History is preserved.

steps.title: Audit the full belief timeline
steps.description: Because invalidation keeps both edges, the graph answers what was believed and when: Austin then Denver, with exact intervals.

name: Memory Decay & Forgetting Policies(MDF)
description: Explicit governance of what an agent drops rather than what it keeps: time-based expiry (TTL), usage and relevance decay (Ebbinghaus-style exponential decay that is boosted each time an item is accessed), staleness detection for facts that are still relevant but no longer true, and hard deletion for right-to-be-forgotten and GDPR Article 17 compliance. Unbounded memory measurably degrades agent performance, so forgetting is a first-class design axis. Distinct from `memory-consolidation` (which compresses and abstracts memories into schemas, the opposite operation) and from `generative-agents-memory` (which uses recency decay only as a retrieval score, not as an eviction or deletion policy).
features: Ebbinghaus-style decay scores boosted by access frequency
Staleness detection for high-relevance but outdated facts
Budget-driven eviction and archival when memory exceeds a cap
Hard deletion with an audit record for right-to-be-forgotten requests
Separation of decay (soft, reversible) from deletion (hard, permanent)

tldr.what: Removes or deprioritizes memories by time-based expiry, access frequency decay, staleness detection, and budget-driven eviction rather than keeping everything.
tldr.when: Long-running agents accumulating thousands of facts where unbounded memory slows retrieval, or compliance requires hard deletion of user data.
tldr.watchOut: Aggressive decay can discard facts still needed for context; recovery after accidental deletion is impossible if audit trails are incomplete.

flow.title: Memory Decay & Forgetting Policies
flow.description: Governance of what an agent drops: decay scores rank items for budget-driven eviction and archival, staleness detection supersedes high-relevance facts that quietly became false, and a right-to-be-forgotten request triggers hard deletion with an audit record as proof.

nodes.label:
🟢 Budget Exceeded
42,000 items stored, cap is 40,000

🤖 Decay Scorer
score = importance * 0.5^(age / half_life)

📌 Keep (warm)
"Allergic to penicillin" imp 9 -> 8.6

📄 Evict (cold)
"Weather 2024-11-03" imp 1 -> 0.02

📊 Rank by decay score
All 42,000 items ordered low to high

📦 Archive bottom 2,000
Move to cold storage (recoverable)

📤 Live memory back to 40,000
Latency and distraction drop

⚠️ Staleness Detector
High-relevance but no longer true?

🔴 "Works at Acme Corp"
Relevance HIGH, decay would keep it

🟣 Supersede
Signal "I started at Globex" replaces it

🟢 Right-to-be-forgotten
Delete everything about user U-8842

🛑 Hard Delete
Purge U-8842 from live + cold storage

🧾 Audit Record
who / when / scope = deletion proof

steps.title: Memory exceeds its budget
steps.description: Accumulated memory crosses the cap. Rather than growing unbounded (which degrades performance), the agent scores every item for eviction.

steps.title: Decay scoring separates warm from cold
steps.description: Ebbinghaus-style decay is boosted by access. A frequently used allergy fact stays warm; an unused one-off weather note decays toward zero.

steps.title: Rank and archive the coldest items
steps.description: All items are ranked by decay score and the bottom 2,000 are archived to cold storage (recoverable, not deleted), returning live memory to budget.

steps.title: Staleness is a different failure than low relevance
steps.description: A high-relevance fact ("Works at Acme Corp") would never be dropped by decay, yet it can quietly become false. A staleness check flags it.

steps.title: Supersede the stale high-relevance fact
steps.description: A contradicting signal ("I started at Globex") supersedes the outdated employer fact, the problem decay alone cannot solve.

steps.title: Right-to-be-forgotten triggers hard deletion
steps.description: A GDPR Article 17 request cannot be satisfied by soft decay. Every item keyed to the user is purged from both live and cold storage.

steps.title: Emit deletion proof
steps.description: The purge writes an audit record (who, when, what scope) so the erasure is provable, which consolidation and retrieval-scoring can never provide.

name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback(RLHF)
description: Fine-tuning a policy with reinforcement learning against a reward model learned from human preference judgments

tldr.what: Trains a reward model from human preference comparisons, then optimizes agent behavior against that model while constraining drift from baseline.
tldr.when: Aligning agent outputs to nuanced human values where simple metrics fail and you can afford substantial human annotation and compute.
tldr.watchOut: Reward model learns reviewer biases and edge cases poorly; agent exploits model gaps rather than genuinely improving, requiring expensive monitoring.

overview.pattern: Three-phase training: SFT → Reward Model → PPO optimization with human preference alignment
overview.why: Aligns AI behavior with human values, improves safety, helpfulness, and reduces harmful outputs
overview.insight: Human preferences > reward model > policy optimization creates scalable alignment mechanism
dos: Use diverse, high-quality human preference data
Apply KL regularization to prevent policy drift
Monitor reward hacking and Goodhart's law effects
Use multiple evaluation metrics beyond reward scores
Implement careful hyperparameter tuning for PPO
Validate reward model correlation with human judgments
donts: Skip reward model validation on held-out data
Use biased or low-quality preference annotations
Ignore distribution shift in deployment
Optimize purely for reward model scores
Use unstable RL training without safety measures
avoid: Simple objective tasks with clear metrics

usecases.d: Align chatbots for helpful, harmless, honest responses
Optimize creative writing for human preferences
Improve code quality and safety recommendations
Generate summaries matching human quality judgments
Provide accurate, well-formatted answers
Align AI art/music generation with aesthetic preferences

name: Direct Preference Optimization(DPO)
description: Offline preference optimization with a classification loss over chosen and rejected responses, without training an explicit reward model

tldr.what: Trains a policy directly on preference pairs by minimizing a classification loss that compares chosen versus rejected responses relative to a frozen reference policy, skipping explicit reward modeling.
tldr.when: You have paired preference data (chosen and rejected outputs) and want to align behavior without the overhead of training a separate reward model first.
tldr.watchOut: Policy can drift far from the reference, degrading performance on tasks outside the preference dataset or causing mode collapse if preference pairs are narrow.

overview.pattern: Two-phase training: SFT → Direct preference optimization without explicit reward modeling
overview.why: Simplifies RLHF pipeline, improves training stability, reduces computational overhead while maintaining alignment quality
overview.insight: Treats the language model as an implicit reward model, optimizing preferences directly via classification loss
dos: Use high-quality, balanced preference datasets
Tune beta parameter for KL regularization strength
Validate preference accuracy on held-out human data
Monitor for length bias in preference judgments
Use stable learning rates (1e-6 to 5e-7)
Apply gradient clipping for training stability
donts: Skip preference data quality validation
Use inconsistent or contradictory preferences
Ignore distribution shift from SFT to preferences
Set beta too high (causes mode collapse)
Use same data for SFT and preference optimization

usecases.d: Efficient alternative to RLHF for preference alignment
Align conversational AI with human preferences
Optimize for code quality and correctness preferences
Align creative outputs with human aesthetic judgments
Improve summary quality based on human preferences
Optimize for fluency and accuracy preferences

name: In-Context Learning(ICL)
description: Conditioning a model on instructions and demonstrations in the current context, without updating model parameters

tldr.what: Conditions a model on task instructions and examples in the prompt, without changing model weights, to guide behavior for new inputs.
tldr.when: Tasks with clear, fixed categories or patterns where a few labeled examples reliably show the model what to do.
tldr.watchOut: Performance degrades sharply if examples don't match the distribution of real inputs or if the model misinterprets which features matter.

overview.pattern: Provide task examples in prompt to enable model learning without parameter updates
overview.why: Enables rapid task adaptation, requires no training, leverages model's pattern recognition for immediate performance
overview.insight: Models can learn from demonstrations in context, performing implicit gradient descent during inference

impl.d: Choose relevant examples for task context
Apply learned pattern to new input

dos: Use diverse, high-quality examples representative of task
Maintain consistent formatting across all examples
Order examples from simple to complex when possible
Include edge cases and boundary conditions
Test with different example counts (1-shot to few-shot)
Use clear separators between examples
donts: Use contradictory or inconsistent examples
Overload context with too many examples
Use biased or non-representative examples
Mix different task types in same prompt
Ignore example selection and ordering effects
use: Quick adaptation to new tasks needed
Limited or no training data available
Model needs to understand complex patterns
avoid: Large amounts of training data available
High precision requirements exceed ICL capability

usecases.d: Sentiment analysis, topic categorization with labeled examples
Named entity recognition, information extraction from documents
JSON to XML, structured data transformation
Domain-specific QA with example question-answer pairs
Programming tasks with input-output code examples
Style transfer, content generation with stylistic examples

name: Meta-Learning Systems(MLS)
description: Optimizing across a distribution of tasks so a model can adapt to a new related task from limited data

tldr.what: Trains a model on many related tasks so it adapts quickly to new tasks using only a few examples and gradient steps.
tldr.when: Few-shot learning where you have many similar tasks but sparse labeled data per new task at deployment.
tldr.watchOut: Requires carefully curated task distributions; poor task sampling or misaligned meta-train and meta-test tasks kills performance.

overview.pattern: Learn to learn: acquire meta-knowledge enabling rapid adaptation to new tasks with minimal data
overview.why: Enables few-shot learning, rapid domain adaptation, and efficient knowledge transfer across related tasks
overview.insight: Models learn optimization procedures and inductive biases that generalize across task distributions

impl.d: Define distribution of related learning tasks
Learn to adapt quickly across task distribution
Provide few examples of new target task
Rapidly specialize to new task using meta-knowledge
Perform target task with minimal examples

dos: Design diverse meta-training task distributions
Balance task complexity and similarity in meta-training
Use proper train/validation/test task splits
Monitor for overfitting to meta-training tasks
Implement gradient-based and gradient-free approaches
Track adaptation speed and final performance metrics
donts: Use identical tasks in meta-training and meta-testing
Ignore computational overhead of meta-optimization
Apply to domains with insufficient task diversity
Skip ablation studies on meta-learning components
Use inadequate support set sizes for evaluation
use: Many related tasks with limited data each
Need rapid adaptation to new domains
Tasks share underlying structure or patterns
avoid: Single task with abundant training data

metrics.d: Performance with K examples per class
Performance vs baseline on new tasks

usecases.d: Image recognition with limited labeled examples per class
Rapidly adapt models to new domains with minimal data
Learn to design architectures for new tasks
Learn optimal hyperparameters across task families
Quick adaptation to new environments and reward structures
Few-shot text classification and named entity recognition

name: Continual Learning(CL)
description: Learning from a sequence of tasks or data distributions while measuring and mitigating loss of earlier capabilities

tldr.what: Trains sequentially on new tasks while measuring and preventing loss of performance on earlier tasks through rehearsal, regularization, or task-specific adapters.
tldr.when: Systems must learn from multiple tasks or data distributions over time without forgetting prior capabilities or requiring access to all historical data.
tldr.watchOut: Measuring true catastrophic forgetting requires maintaining a full evaluation matrix across all tasks at every stage, which becomes expensive as task count grows.

overview.pattern: Learn new tasks sequentially while retaining knowledge from previous tasks without catastrophic forgetting
overview.why: Enables lifelong learning, adapts to changing environments, and maintains accumulated knowledge over time
overview.insight: Balance plasticity for new learning with stability for old knowledge through specialized retention mechanisms

impl.d: Train initial model on first task/domain
Learn new tasks while preserving old knowledge
Test performance on all tasks seen so far
Adjust strategy based on forgetting metrics

dos: Use regularization techniques to constrain weight changes
Implement experience replay with diverse sample selection
Monitor backward and forward transfer metrics
Apply dynamic architectures for capacity expansion
Use meta-learning for rapid task adaptation
Implement memory-efficient storage strategies
donts: Ignore catastrophic forgetting measurement
Use naive fine-tuning without protection mechanisms
Store all previous data (privacy/storage issues)
Skip baseline comparison with multi-task learning
Use single metric for continual learning evaluation
use: Sequential task arrival with limited memory
Privacy constraints prevent storing old data

usecases.d: Continuously learn new dialogue patterns and domains
Adapt to changing user preferences over time
Learn new driving scenarios without forgetting existing skills
Incrementally learn new diseases and conditions
Continuously adapt to new attack patterns and threats
Update capabilities while maintaining existing functionality

flow.title: Continual Learning
flow.description: Adaptive learning system that acquires new knowledge over time while preventing catastrophic forgetting, using techniques like elastic weight consolidation and progressive neural networks.

name: Self-Improving Systems(SIS)
description: Controlled systems that propose changes to prompts, tools, or policies and retain them only after independent evaluation and approval

tldr.what: Agent proposes changes to prompts or policies, validates them against test suites in isolation, then deploys only after human approval.
tldr.when: Production systems where failures are costly and you need to evolve behavior safely without breaking existing functionality.
tldr.watchOut: Evaluation suites become stale or incomplete, causing bad changes to pass validation and reach production anyway.

overview.pattern: Systems that automatically analyze, modify, and improve their own capabilities and performance over time
overview.why: Enables continuous optimization, reduces manual maintenance, and adapts to changing requirements automatically
overview.insight: Combines monitoring, analysis, and safe deployment mechanisms to achieve autonomous capability enhancement

impl.d: Collect performance and error data continuously

dos: Implement robust safety checks and rollback mechanisms
Use gradual deployment and A/B testing for improvements
Monitor for unintended side effects and emergent behaviors
Maintain human oversight and intervention capabilities
Log all improvement attempts and their outcomes
Set clear boundaries and constraints on self-modification
donts: Allow unconstrained self-modification without safety bounds
Deploy improvements without thorough testing
Ignore potential security vulnerabilities in self-modification
Remove human oversight and control mechanisms
Optimize for single metrics without considering trade-offs
avoid: Systems with unclear or unmeasurable objectives
Highly regulated environments requiring static behavior

metrics.d: Number of constraint breaches or failures

usecases.d: Automatically improve code quality and efficiency through iterative refinement
Continuously optimize algorithms based on user feedback and engagement
Adapt strategies based on market performance and changing conditions
Iteratively improve writing, design, or creative outputs based on success metrics
Automatically optimize configurations and resource allocation
Improve hypothesis generation and experimental design through iterative learning

flow.title: Self-Improving Systems
flow.description: Autonomous systems that continuously enhance their performance through real-world interaction analysis, self-evaluation, and iterative improvement cycles.
