name: Constitutional AI(CAI)
description: Using an explicit set of principles to guide self-critique, revision, and AI-generated preference feedback during training

tldr.what: Model learns to critique and revise its own outputs against explicit principles, then ranks responses using principle-aligned feedback without human labeling.
tldr.when: Training systems where you have clear behavioral principles but limited human feedback capacity, and need interpretable alignment during learning.
tldr.watchOut: Principles that conflict or are vague produce inconsistent training signals; model may learn to game principle-checking rather than internalize values.

overview.pattern: Train AI systems using explicitly defined principles and AI-generated feedback to achieve harmless, helpful behavior
overview.why: Scales oversight beyond human capacity, reduces harmful outputs, and creates transparent value-aligned AI systems
overview.insight: Constitutional principles guide AI feedback generation, creating self-supervising systems aligned with explicit values

impl.d: Train preference model on AI feedback

dos: Create clear, specific, and actionable constitutional principles
Use diverse constitutional principles covering multiple values
Implement iterative constitutional refinement processes
Monitor for constitutional principle conflicts and trade-offs
Validate AI feedback quality against human judgment
Test edge cases and adversarial scenarios thoroughly
donts: Use vague or contradictory constitutional principles
Skip human validation of AI-generated feedback
Apply single constitutional framework to all domains
Ignore cultural and contextual variations in values
Deploy without extensive red team testing
use: Building systems requiring strong ethical alignment
Reducing human annotation costs for safety training
Scaling oversight to complex AI behaviors
Creating self-regulating AI with explicit principles
avoid: Simple tasks with clear objective metrics
Applications with zero tolerance for errors
Contexts with highly contested moral principles

usecases.d: Align chatbots with ethical principles and reduce harmful outputs
Automatically enforce community guidelines and platform values
Ensure compliance with professional ethics and legal standards
Implement age-appropriate and pedagogically sound interactions
Maintain patient privacy and medical ethics in AI-assisted care
Ensure fair lending practices and regulatory compliance in AI decisions

flow.title: Constitutional AI

name: Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback(RLAIF)
description: Training a policy from preference judgments produced by an AI evaluator under human-defined criteria and oversight

tldr.watchOut: The AI evaluator can silently drift from the rubric or amplify human biases baked into the calibration set, corrupting the entire training run.

overview.pattern: Use AI models to generate feedback and preferences for training, replacing or augmenting human evaluation
overview.why: Scales preference learning beyond human capacity, reduces annotation costs, and enables rapid iteration cycles
overview.insight: AI evaluators can provide consistent, scalable feedback when properly aligned with human values and principles

Create preference pairs using AI evaluator
Train reward model on AI-generated preferences

Combine AI feedback with human oversight mechanisms

donts: Rely solely on AI feedback without human validation
Use biased or poorly aligned AI evaluators
Ignore scalability limitations of AI feedback generation

Apply without considering domain-specific evaluation criteria

name: Test-Time Scaling(TTS)
description: Allocating additional inference-time computation to candidate generation, search, verification, or refinement

tldr.what: Generates multiple candidate solutions at inference time, then ranks or filters them using verifiers before returning the best result.
tldr.when: High-stakes outputs where quality matters more than latency, and you can afford multiple forward passes to find better answers.
tldr.watchOut: Compute costs multiply by candidate count; verification overhead can exceed generation cost if verifiers are expensive or poorly targeted.

overview.pattern: Allocate additional compute at inference time to improve performance through multiple attempts and verification
overview.why: Enables better accuracy on complex tasks, flexible compute allocation, and performance scaling without retraining
overview.insight: More inference-time compute can substitute for larger models or more training data on reasoning tasks

impl.d: Create multiple reasoning paths or solutions
Use verification model or self-consistency checks
Score and rank solutions by quality/confidence
Choose best solution or aggregate top candidates
Increase compute budget for better performance

dos: Use process-based verification over outcome-only evaluation
Implement majority voting and self-consistency checks
Scale compute allocation based on problem difficulty
Use search algorithms and tree-based reasoning
Monitor latency vs accuracy trade-offs carefully
Implement early stopping for confident solutions
donts: Apply uniform compute to all problems regardless of difficulty
Ignore verification quality and just generate more samples
Use test-time scaling without proper evaluation frameworks
Scale compute without considering inference cost budgets
Rely solely on quantity without improving reasoning quality
use: Complex reasoning tasks requiring multiple solution paths
High-stakes decisions where accuracy is prioritized over speed
Problems where verification is easier than generation
Tasks with clear objective evaluation criteria
Applications with flexible inference time budgets
avoid: Real-time applications with strict latency requirements
Tasks where first attempt is typically sufficient

usecases.d: Multiple solution paths for complex proofs and problem solving
Generate and verify multiple implementations to find optimal solutions
Explore multiple hypotheses and experimental designs
Evaluate multiple scenarios and decision pathways
Generate diverse solutions and select most promising approaches
Systematic solution exploration with verification

flow.title: Test-Time Scaling

name: Odds Ratio Preference Optimization(ORPO)
description: Reference-free preference alignment that adds an odds-ratio penalty for rejected responses to the chosen-response language-modeling objective

tldr.what: Trains a model on chosen responses while penalizing rejected responses via odds-ratio loss, skipping the reference model entirely.
tldr.when: You have paired preference data and want faster, cheaper alignment without maintaining a separate reference model.
tldr.watchOut: Odds-ratio penalty can destabilize training if lambda is mistuned; requires careful hyperparameter search to avoid capability loss.

overview.pattern: Single-phase training combining supervised fine-tuning with odds ratio-based preference optimization
overview.why: Simplifies alignment pipeline, reduces training complexity, and achieves competitive preference alignment without separate reward modeling
overview.insight: Odds ratio penalty directly optimizes preference likelihood ratios during supervised training for efficient alignment

impl.d: Combine SFT loss with odds ratio penalty
Train simultaneously without separate reward model

dos: Use balanced preference datasets with clear winner/loser pairs
Tune lambda parameter for optimal SFT/preference balance
Monitor for training instability with gradient clipping
Validate against human evaluation and benchmark tasks
Use appropriate learning rates (typically lower than standard SFT)
Implement early stopping based on preference accuracy
donts: Use unbalanced or low-quality preference data
Set lambda too high (causes training instability)
Ignore the relative log-probabilities in the loss function
Skip comparison with DPO and other preference methods
Apply without understanding the odds ratio formulation
use: Want single-phase training without separate reward model
Have high-quality pairwise preference data available
Need simpler alternative to multi-stage RLHF pipeline
Prefer monolithic training over modular approaches
avoid: Need explicit reward model for interpretability
Require fine-grained control over reward shaping
Training stability is a major concern

Use without proper hyperparameter tuning
Apply to domains where reference models are critical
Skip comparison with DPO and other reference-based methods

avoid: Need explicit KL regularization for safety

name: Memory-Based Learning(MBL)
description: Improves agent behavior by retrieving and reusing stored experiences at decision time instead of updating model weights. tldr.when: Personalization matters across repeated interactions and you can capture reliable feedback signals to weight which past experiences to reuse.
tldr.watchOut: Recall quality degrades sharply if memories lack clear outcome labels or if similarity matching pulls irrelevant past cases into current decisions.

overview.pattern: Learn by storing, retrieving, and adapting from a memory bank of past experiences and examples
overview.why: Enables few-shot learning, prevents catastrophic forgetting, and supports personalization through accumulated experience
overview.insight: Effective memory systems combine efficient storage, smart retrieval, and adaptive integration of past experiences

impl.d: Build memory bank of experiences, examples, or patterns
Find relevant memories based on current context
Use retrieved memories to inform current predictions
Add new experiences and manage memory capacity

dos: Use efficient similarity search (FAISS, approximate nearest neighbors)
Implement memory consolidation and forgetting mechanisms
Store both positive and negative examples for better learning
Use hierarchical memory structures for different time scales
Apply memory replay techniques to prevent catastrophic forgetting
Implement adaptive memory capacity based on importance
donts: Store memories without considering retrieval efficiency
Use unlimited memory without pruning strategies
Ignore memory quality and redundancy issues
Apply without proper similarity metrics for domain
Neglect privacy and security considerations for stored data
use: Few-shot learning scenarios with limited training data
Tasks benefit from analogical reasoning and case-based learning
Need to maintain long-term knowledge and prevent forgetting
avoid: Memory storage and retrieval costs are prohibitive
Task has abundant training data and stable patterns
Simple pattern recognition without need for examples

metrics.d: Time to find and use relevant memories

Store user preferences and behavior patterns for customization
Maintain knowledge across multiple tasks without catastrophic forgetting
Solve new problems by retrieving and adapting similar past solutions
Remember promising architectures and design patterns
Replay important experiences to maintain performance on old tasks

name: Automatic Prompt Optimization(APO)
description: Treats the prompts and instructions inside an agent pipeline as learnable parameters that are optimized programmatically against a metric and a labeled dataset, instead of being hand tuned. Optimizers bootstrap few-shot demonstrations and search over instruction wordings, and reflective methods mutate prompts by reading execution traces of past failures.
features: Reflective prompt evolution over execution traces (GEPA)

tldr.what: Treats prompts as learnable parameters optimized against metrics using few-shot bootstrapping, instruction search, failure trace analysis, and LLM feedback loops instead of manual tuning.
tldr.when: You have labeled validation data, a clear metric, and enough compute budget to run many pipeline iterations to improve prompt quality systematically.
tldr.watchOut: Optimization can overfit to your validation set or metric, producing prompts that fail on new domains or reward gaming instead of genuine capability gains.

flow.title: Automatic Prompt Optimization (APO)
flow.description: Treats the prompts of an agent pipeline as learnable parameters. An optimizer reads failure traces, proposes instruction mutations and few-shot demonstrations, evaluates candidates against a metric, and iterates until the pipeline improves from 61% to 84%.

steps.title: Baseline Measurement
steps.description: The pipeline runs on the 200-example set with its hand-written prompts and scores 61% exact match. This becomes the target to beat.

steps.title: Collect Failure Traces
steps.description: For every wrong answer the optimizer logs the input, the intermediate retrieve and answer outputs, and the metric. These traces carry the signal about why the pipeline fails.

steps.title: Reflect on Failures
steps.description: A reflective optimizer reads the traces and writes a natural-language diagnosis, for example that the answer stage ignores dates present in the retrieved passage.

steps.title: Propose Mutations
steps.description: Guided by the diagnosis, the optimizer rewrites the answer-stage instruction while MIPROv2 bootstraps and searches candidate few-shot demonstrations in parallel.

steps.title: Generate Candidates
steps.description: The proposals combine into candidate programs: a new instruction, new demonstrations, and a mix of both.

steps.title: Evaluate and Keep Improvers
steps.description: Each candidate is scored on a held-out minibatch. Only candidates that beat the current best survive, which keeps the search cheap and grounded in the metric.

steps.title: Select and Iterate
steps.description: The best candidate is selected and seeds the next round of reflection and proposals. After about 15 rounds validation accuracy has climbed from 61% toward 84%.

steps.title: Validate and Ship
steps.description: The converged pipeline is re-checked on a separate held-out test split to guard against overfitting the validation metric, confirming 84% before it ships.

name: RL from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR)(RLVR)
description: Trains reasoning models with reinforcement learning against automatically checkable rewards, such as whether a math answer matches ground truth or code passes its tests, rather than against learned preference models. Because the reward only scores final correctness, long chains of thought with backtracking and self-verification emerge without supervised rationales. This is distinct from RLHF, RLAIF, and DPO, which optimize human or AI preferences.
features: Automatically verifiable rewards (math or code correctness)
Distinct from preference-based RLHF, RLAIF, and DPO

tldr.what: Trains a model with RL using automatically checkable rewards (math correctness, code tests) on final outputs only, allowing reasoning chains and self-verification to emerge without supervised rationales.
tldr.when: Problems with deterministic, verifiable ground truth answers where you want the model to discover its own reasoning process without labeled step-by-step solutions.
tldr.watchOut: Requires massive compute for sampling many candidate solutions per problem; most fail, making training expensive and slow compared to supervised approaches.

flow.title: RL from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR)
flow.description: Trains a reasoning model with reinforcement learning against automatically checkable rewards. The policy samples solutions, a deterministic verifier grades final answers, GRPO updates the policy, and long chain-of-thought with backtracking and self-verification emerges over training without any supervised rationales.

steps.title: Problem and Base Model
steps.description: Training starts from a pretrained base model. For each problem only the final answer will be graded, and no human-written reasoning traces are provided.

steps.title: Sample a Group of Solutions
steps.description: The policy samples a group of G=8 candidate solutions for the problem, each a full chain of thought that ends in a boxed final answer.

steps.title: Verify Final Answers
steps.description: A deterministic verifier checks each final answer by numeric match or unit tests. Here solutions 1 and 3 are correct and solution 2 is wrong. A guardrail watches the verifier for reward hacking.

steps.title: Assign Verifiable Rewards
steps.description: The verifier assigns +1 to correct answers and 0 otherwise, plus a small format reward for well-formed output. No preference model is involved.

steps.title: GRPO Policy Update
steps.description: GRPO computes each sample advantage relative to the group mean reward and updates the policy, reinforcing above-average solutions without training a separate value network.

steps.title: Update and Repeat
steps.description: The updated policy replaces the base model for the next step, and the loop repeats over thousands of steps on many problems.

steps.title: Emergent Reasoning
steps.description: As training proceeds the average response length grows and the model spontaneously backtracks and self-verifies. The R1 work documents an aha moment where the model pauses to reconsider its approach.

steps.title: Reasoning Model
steps.description: Using only automatically checkable rewards, pass@1 on AIME-style problems rises sharply above the base model, with no supervised rationales at any point.

name: Process Reward Models & Verifier-Guided Search(PRM)
description: Uses a reward model that scores each intermediate reasoning step (process supervision) rather than only the final answer (outcome supervision). The per-step scores rank and prune candidate solutions during best-of-N sampling or tree search, concentrating test-time compute on the most promising branches and on harder problems.
features: Ranks and prunes candidates in best-of-N or tree search
More sample-efficient than outcome-only reward models
Verifier-guided selection of the final answer

tldr.what: Scores each reasoning step with a learned model, then prunes low-scoring solution branches early during search or sampling.
tldr.when: Multi-step problems where intermediate correctness matters, test-time compute is flexible, and you can afford to train a step-level verifier.
tldr.watchOut: Process reward model quality directly limits pruning accuracy; poor step scores waste compute or cut off correct paths prematurely.

flow.title: Process Reward Models & Verifier-Guided Search
flow.description: A reward model scores every intermediate reasoning step rather than only the final answer. The scores prune weak branches early in a best-of-N or tree search, concentrate test-time compute on promising paths, and select the final answer by aggregating step scores.

steps.title: Sample Solution Paths
steps.description: The policy generates 8 candidate solution paths for the problem, each a sequence of labeled reasoning steps rather than a single final answer.

steps.title: Score Each Step
steps.description: The process reward model assigns a correctness probability to every step as it is produced. Path 1 and Path 4 hold high scores while Path 2 and Path 3 drop.

steps.title: Prune Weak Branches
steps.description: Paths whose running step scores fall below a threshold are stopped early. Here 5 of the 8 paths are cut after step 3 before more tokens are spent on them.

steps.title: Compute Saved
steps.description: By not expanding doomed branches and adapting search to difficulty, the PRM-guided approach is more than 4x more efficient than naive best-of-N under a matched budget.

steps.title: Expand Survivors
steps.description: The three surviving high-scoring paths continue and may branch further, forming a verifier-guided tree search focused on the most promising reasoning.

steps.title: Aggregate and Select
steps.description: Completed paths are ranked by aggregating their step scores, for example the minimum or product across steps, instead of a plain majority vote.

steps.title: Verified Solution
steps.description: The selected path is returned. On MATH, process supervision plus weighted selection clearly beats self-consistency at the same sample budget.

name: Skill Library (Voyager)(SL)
description: An agent writes reusable, executable skills (programs) for behaviors it discovers, stores them in a library indexed by embeddings of their descriptions, and later retrieves and composes them into more complex skills. The library grows as a form of procedural memory, so capability compounds over time without gradient updates or catastrophic forgetting.
features: Skills stored as executable code, not weights
Embedding-indexed library for retrieval by meaning
Automatic curriculum proposes the next skill to learn
Iterative code refinement from execution feedback
Composition of simpler skills into complex ones

tldr.what: Agent writes executable code for discovered behaviors, stores them in an embedding-indexed library, and composes them into complex skills that grow without retraining.
tldr.when: Open-ended learning where the agent discovers many reusable behaviors over time and needs to build on prior discoveries without forgetting or retraining.
tldr.watchOut: Code quality and correctness degrade rapidly if execution feedback is noisy or the refinement loop fails to catch bugs before library storage.

flow.title: Skill Library (Voyager)
flow.description: An open-ended agent writes reusable executable skills for behaviors it discovers, stores them in an embedding-indexed library, then retrieves and composes them into more complex skills. Capability compounds over time without gradient updates or catastrophic forgetting.

steps.title: Curriculum Proposes a Goal
steps.description: An automatic curriculum inspects the agent state in the world and proposes the next goal, here to obtain wooden planks.

steps.title: Write an Executable Skill
steps.description: The agent writes a program, a function such as craftPlanks(), that calls the environment API to achieve the proposed goal.

steps.title: Run, Verify, Refine
steps.description: The code executes in the environment. Execution errors and feedback are returned to the agent, which iteratively fixes the program until it succeeds.

steps.title: Store the Skill
steps.description: The verified craftPlanks skill is added to the library and indexed by an embedding of its description, joining earlier skills like mineWood and craftTable.

steps.title: Retrieve by Meaning
steps.description: The curriculum advances to a harder goal, build a shelter. The agent retrieves craftPlanks and other relevant skills from the library by embedding search rather than exact name.

steps.title: Compose into a Complex Skill
steps.description: The retrieved skills are composed into a new program, buildShelter(), that calls craftPlanks and others to accomplish the larger task.

steps.title: Store and Compound
steps.description: buildShelter is stored back into the library. Because skills are external code that is kept, adding one never overwrites the others, so capability compounds without catastrophic forgetting.

steps.title: Tech Tree Unlocked
steps.description: Later tasks reuse earlier work, so the agent obtains more unique items and unlocks the tech tree far faster than baselines that re-plan from scratch, and the learned library transfers to new worlds.

references: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models (2023) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291

name: Agentic Context Engineering (Evolving Playbook)(ACE)
description: Treats an agent's context as an evolving playbook of concrete strategies that is improved by three roles: a Generator that produces reasoning traces on real tasks, a Reflector that extracts lessons from what succeeded or failed, and a Curator that merges those lessons into the playbook as compact structured delta updates. Because updates are incremental appends and edits rather than full rewrites, the playbook accumulates domain detail instead of suffering context collapse and brevity bias, where iterative rewriting erodes hard-won specifics. It needs no labeled supervision and applies both offline as an improved system prompt and online as agent memory, with the ICLR 2026 ACE paper reporting roughly +10.6% on agent tasks and +8.6% on finance. Distinct from `prompt-optimization`: DSPy and GEPA optimize a prompt artifact against a metric, whereas ACE grows a natural-language playbook through delta curation with an explicit anti-collapse mechanism spanning prompt and memory, and unlike `skill-library` (executable skills) or `self-improving-systems` (governed prompt and tool edits behind approval gates) the improving artifact is a curated natural-language playbook.
features: Context as an evolving strategy playbook
Compact structured delta updates (append and edit, not full rewrite)
Anti-collapse mechanism against context collapse and brevity bias
Offline (system prompt) and online (agent memory) adaptation
Self-improvement from execution traces without labeled supervision

tldr.what: Divides an agent into Generator, Reflector, and Curator roles that build a natural-language playbook of strategies through incremental delta updates rather than full rewrites, preventing context collapse.
tldr.when: Multi-step domain tasks where the agent must accumulate and retain specific lessons from execution traces without labeled data, and where prompt brevity erodes hard-won detail.
tldr.watchOut: Curator must distinguish signal from noise; poor delta selection pollutes the playbook faster than good curation can clean it, degrading performance.

flow.title: Agentic Context Engineering (Evolving Playbook)
flow.description: The agent context is an evolving playbook improved by a Generator, Reflector, and Curator. A mistake becomes a compact delta bullet appended to the playbook, so domain detail accumulates and is reused, while a full-rewrite baseline compresses the same lesson away and suffers context collapse.

Extract a lesson from the mistake

steps.title: Task and Playbook
steps.description: A task arrives and the agent context starts as a small warm-start playbook of reviewed strategy bullets: locate the named statement, match the fiscal period. Context, not weights, is what will improve.

steps.title: Generator Attempts
steps.description: The Generator reads the current playbook and produces a full reasoning trace with an answer. It reports the raw figure but ignores the statement header that says "(in millions)".

steps.title: Grader Flags a Mistake
steps.description: The grader signal shows the answer is wrong by a factor of 1000, a scale error. No labeled rationale is needed, just the pass or fail signal on the outcome.

steps.title: Reflector Extracts a Lesson
steps.description: The Reflector reads the trace and the grader signal and distills a specific, reusable lesson: the statement declared millions, so scale every numeric answer by the stated unit.

steps.title: Curator Merges a Delta
steps.description: The Curator turns the lesson into a compact delta bullet tagged [units] and appends it to the playbook. The rest of the playbook is untouched, so the warm-start detail is preserved and the context grows incrementally.

steps.title: Reuse on the Next Task
steps.description: A later free-cash-flow question arrives. The Generator retrieves the [units] bullet from the evolved playbook, applies the scale, and the grader passes. Capability compounded through context, without any weight update.

steps.title: Contrast: Full-Rewrite Collapse
steps.description: A baseline that rewrites the whole playbook into a shorter summary each round shows brevity bias. After a few rounds the [units] rule is compressed away (context collapse), and the baseline repeats the original scale error that delta curation had already fixed.

references: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models (2025) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618

ACE prevents context collapse with evolving playbooks for self-improving AI - VentureBeat (2025) - https://venturebeat.com/ai/ace-prevents-context-collapse-with-evolving-playbooks-for-self-improving-ai

name: LLM Checkpoint Recovery (Mnemosyne)(LCR)
description: Lightweight device proxy architecture for LLM fault recovery with just-in-time checkpointing and partial topology reconstruction

tldr.what: Maintains lightweight device proxies that capture gradient and optimizer state on-demand, then reconstruct the training topology and resume from the last checkpoint after failures.
tldr.when: Large-scale distributed LLM training where frequent failures occur and you need sub-minute recovery without full retraining or elastic scaling.
tldr.watchOut: Just-in-time checkpointing adds latency during normal training; misconfigured triggers can cause cascading failures or memory exhaustion under high fault rates.

overview.pattern: Device proxy architecture with just-in-time checkpointing for LLM fault recovery
overview.why: Reduces recovery overhead by 58.8% vs traditional approaches, enables partial topology reconstruction
overview.insight: Lightweight device proxies + flexible CCL + incremental communication reinitialization = 3.6% daily overhead

impl.d: Deploy device proxy layer for error interception
Track failure patterns and recovery times

dos: Use lightweight device proxies optimized for fault tolerance
Implement partial topology reconstruction around failed nodes
Cache gradient states and optimizer checkpoints separately
Use incremental communication reinitialization (not full restart)
Monitor memory usage patterns to predict failures
donts: Rely on elastic training features for pure fault tolerance
Perform global communication reinitialization on single failures
Store massive checkpoints to slow storage during training
Ignore temporal dominance of communication overhead
Use generic checkpointing for 70B+ parameter models

usecases.d: 70B+ parameter models with week-long training cycles
Multi-node adaptation with frequent hardware failures
Sparse mixture-of-experts with massive checkpoint sizes
Data/tensor/pipeline parallel combinations with complex failure modes
Spot instance training with predictable interruptions

name: Agent Context Preservation and Recovery(ACP)
description: Systematic preservation and recovery of agent conversation context, memory state, and reasoning chains during failures

tldr.what: Saves agent conversation state, memory, and reasoning chains at checkpoints, then reconstructs them after failures to resume work.
tldr.when: Long-running multi-turn conversations where interruptions lose progress, or when agent reasoning chains must survive system restarts.
tldr.watchOut: Stale or corrupted snapshots can cause agents to repeat work, contradict earlier decisions, or hallucinate missing context.

overview.pattern: Systematic preservation and recovery of agent conversation context, memory state, and reasoning chains
overview.why: Enables seamless conversation continuity across failures, 73% reduction in redundant computations, 89% improvement in context relevance
overview.insight: Hierarchical memory (STM/LTM/semantic) + vector search + secure context sharing = persistent agent intelligence

impl.d: Vector DB + knowledge graph for context
Rebuild agent state from stored context

dos: Use hierarchical memory (short-term, long-term, semantic)
Implement vector-based semantic search for context discovery
Cache conversation state with TTL based on importance
Use knowledge graphs for temporal and multi-hop reasoning
Implement secure access controls (SAMEP protocol)
donts: Store all conversation history without pruning strategies
Ignore semantic validation during context reconstruction
Mix episodic and semantic memory without clear boundaries
Skip encryption for sensitive conversation context
Assume all past context is equally relevant for recovery

usecases.d: Maintain context across support ticket sessions and agent handoffs
Remember user preferences, history, and ongoing projects
Track learning progress and adapt based on student history
Preserve patient interaction history for continuity of care
Maintain context across multi-session business workflows

name: Predictive Agent Fault Tolerance(PAF)

tldr.when: Large agent fleets where failures cascade, downtime is costly, and you have historical data showing predictable failure patterns.
tldr.watchOut: False positives trigger unnecessary restarts, degrading availability more than the failures they prevent.

overview.pattern: AI-driven predictive systems that anticipate agent failures before they occur using ML-based anomaly detection
overview.why: Proactive failure prevention vs reactive response, 78% reduction in unplanned downtime, 67% faster mean time to recovery
overview.insight: Ensemble ML models (Random Forest + LSTM + Isolation Forest) + behavioral monitoring = failure prediction with lead times

impl.d: Train anomaly detection models on historical failure patterns
Implement LSTM, Isolation Forest, and ensemble methods
Configure tiered alerts with confidence thresholds
Trigger preemptive actions based on predictions

dos: Use ensemble methods (Random Forest + LSTM + Isolation Forest)
Monitor behavioral patterns, not just performance metrics
Implement dynamic baselines that evolve with system behavior
Create prediction confidence intervals and uncertainty quantification
Use federated learning for multi-agent anomaly detection
donts: Rely solely on reactive threshold-based monitoring
Ignore communication anomalies between agents
Train models on incomplete or imbalanced failure datasets
Deploy predictions without interpretability mechanisms
Skip validation on real-world deployment environments

usecases.d: Monitor 100+ agents with 97.2% accuracy for behavioral anomalies
Predict resource exhaustion and capacity issues before failures
Detect model drift and performance degradation in real-time
Monitor diagnostic agent reliability and prevent misdiagnosis cascades

name: Agent Communication Fault Tolerance(ACF)
description: Comprehensive fault tolerance mechanisms for agent-to-agent communication failures, message routing recovery, and protocol-agnostic resilience

tldr.what: Persists messages, retries with backoff, routes around failures, and syncs context when agents cannot reach each other.
tldr.when: Multi-agent systems where communication breaks unpredictably and lost messages or stale state cause wrong decisions.
tldr.watchOut: Complexity balloons fast; debugging distributed state mismatches across retry loops and topology changes consumes significant engineering effort.

overview.pattern: Comprehensive fault tolerance mechanisms for agent-to-agent communication using modern protocols
overview.why: Prevents cascading failures, enables network partition tolerance, achieves 99.94% message delivery reliability
overview.insight: Protocol-agnostic resilience (MCP/A2A/ACP/ANP) + circuit breakers + dynamic routing = robust agent communication

impl.d: Implement MCP/A2A/ACP with message delivery guarantees
Deploy per-agent-pair circuit breakers with thresholds
Configure exponential backoff with jitter and dead letter queues
Enable dynamic topology adaptation and alternative routing

overview.example: agent_message → protocol_send → failure_detection → circuit_breaker → retry_backoff → alternative_route → success
dos: Use protocol-agnostic fault tolerance (MCP/A2A/ACP/ANP)
Implement circuit breakers with 3-5 failure threshold per minute
Use exponential backoff with jitter to prevent thundering herd
Enable message persistence with dead letter queues
Support both synchronous and asynchronous communication patterns
donts: Rely on single communication path without redundancy
Ignore message ordering guarantees in distributed scenarios
Skip authentication and encryption for agent communication
Use static routing without dynamic topology adaptation
Forget to implement timeout and rate limiting mechanisms

metrics.d: Seconds to restore communication after failure
Time to detect and adapt to partitions

usecases.d: Coordinate 100+ agents across departments with 99.94% delivery rate
Route analysis tasks between specialized agents with fallback paths
Maintain factory agent coordination during network instability
Ensure market data flow between trading agents with sub-second recovery
Coordinate diagnostic agents with strict reliability requirements

name: Agentic SRE (Self-Healing Operations)(ASRE)
description: A closed-loop operations architecture in which agents keep an external system healthy: detect an anomaly, diagnose the probable root cause, execute a policy-bounded remediation, then verify recovery against reliability objectives before closing the loop. It is typically built as a role-specialized team (detector, diagnoser, remediator, verifier) running under human-on-the-loop governance, where engineers define policy, guardrails, and the set of allowed actions while the agents execute within those bounds and report. Least-privilege permissions and policy-as-code keep remediations inside a safe envelope, with higher-risk actions gated on human approval. Distinct from `predictive-agent-fault-tolerance`: that keeps the agent system itself alive, whereas this is agents performing reliability work on the external systems they operate.
features: Closed loop: detect, diagnose, remediate, verify
Role-specialized team: detector, diagnoser, remediator, verifier
Policy-bounded autonomy with a least-privilege set of allowed actions
Human-on-the-loop: engineers set policy, agents execute and report
Recovery verified against SLOs before an incident is closed
Automatic rollback and generated incident reports for audit

tldr.what: Agents detect anomalies, diagnose root causes, execute policy-bounded fixes, then verify recovery against SLOs in a closed loop under human oversight.
tldr.when: External systems need autonomous recovery from known failure modes while keeping humans in control of what actions agents can take.
tldr.watchOut: Overly permissive policies or weak verification can cause agents to mask symptoms instead of fixing root causes or cascade failures.

flow.title: Agentic SRE (Self-Healing Operations)
flow.description: A role-specialized agent team keeps an external service healthy through a closed loop: a detector opens an incident on a latency spike, a diagnoser traces it to a bad deploy, a remediator rolls back within policy, and a verifier confirms SLO recovery before an incident report is generated for the humans on the loop.

📜 Action Policy

Checks policy bounds

steps.title: Detect the Anomaly
steps.description: The detector agent correlates a p99 latency spike (1,900ms against a 450ms SLO budget) across traces, metrics, and error rates and opens a high-severity incident.

steps.title: Diagnose the Root Cause
steps.description: The diagnoser agent lines the spike up against the change log and finds deploy v317 shipped 9 minutes before onset; the error signature matches a new N+1 query, giving a root-cause hypothesis at 0.86 confidence.

steps.title: Check Policy Bounds
steps.description: The remediator checks the proposed action against the on-call policy. Rolling back a deploy is on the allowed-actions list; a riskier action such as a schema migration would fall out of policy and escalate to a human instead.

steps.title: Remediate Within Policy
steps.description: Because the rollback is in policy and least-privilege, the remediator executes it immediately, reverting the service to deploy v316 without waiting for a human.

steps.title: Verify Recovery
steps.description: The verifier agent watches p99 for 10 minutes against the SLO rather than assuming the fix worked, tracking latency and error rate as they settle.

steps.title: SLO Recovered
steps.description: Latency returns to 380ms and the error rate normalizes, confirming recovery. The incident is auto-resolved.

steps.title: Close the Loop
steps.description: An incident report is generated (timeline, root cause, action taken, verification) and left for the humans on the loop to review, closing the detect-diagnose-remediate-verify loop.

name: Naive RAG(NRAG)
description: Foundational "Retrieve-Read" framework following traditional indexing, retrieval, and generation process

tldr.what: Retrieves top matching document passages via semantic search, concatenates them into the prompt, then generates an answer.
tldr.when: Straightforward factual questions over well-indexed documents where retrieval quality is high and no multi-step reasoning is needed.
tldr.watchOut: Retrieved passages may contradict each other or contain irrelevant noise, degrading answer quality without ranking or filtering.

overview.pattern: Simple retrieve-then-read pipeline: query → retrieve documents → concatenate → generate
overview.why: Provides external knowledge access with minimal complexity - foundational approach established by Lewis et al. (2020)
overview.insight: Direct concatenation of top-k retrieved documents to query prompt - no optimization or post-processing

impl.d: Create vector embeddings of knowledge base
Find top-k relevant documents via similarity
Append retrieved docs to query prompt

dos: Use semantic embeddings (e.g., sentence-transformers)
Implement basic chunking strategy (fixed size 512-1024 tokens)
Set clear top-k retrieval limits (typically 3-5 documents)
Include document metadata and source attribution
Use FAISS or similar for efficient vector search
donts: Skip query preprocessing or normalization
Retrieve too many documents (causes context pollution)
Ignore relevance scoring thresholds
Concatenate without clear document boundaries
Expect sophisticated reasoning from basic approach

metrics.d: % of retrieved context used in response

usecases.d: Simple factual questions over company documents or knowledge bases
Automated responses to frequently asked questions using existing documentation
Basic information retrieval from academic papers or research collections
Level 1 support queries answerable from documentation and manuals
Simple question-answering over textbooks and educational materials

description: Enhanced RAG with pre-retrieval and post-retrieval optimizations including query expansion, reranking, and context curation

tldr.when: Knowledge-heavy tasks where retrieval quality directly impacts answer accuracy, especially with large or noisy document collections.
tldr.watchOut: Compounding latency from multiple retrieval passes and reranking stages can make response time unacceptable for real-time applications.

overview.pattern: Enhanced retrieval pipeline with query preprocessing, multi-stage retrieval, neural reranking, and context optimization
overview.why: Addresses limitations of naive RAG through query understanding, relevance scoring, and context quality optimization

Apply sentence window retrieval for context preservation
Implement relevance filtering with confidence thresholds
Use multiple embedding models for retrieval diversity
donts: Skip query preprocessing and expansion
Rely solely on semantic similarity for ranking
Ignore document quality and freshness signals
Over-retrieve without proper filtering mechanisms
Neglect context window optimization
use: Production RAG systems requiring high accuracy
Large knowledge bases with noisy content
avoid: Simple factual Q&A with clean data
Small knowledge bases with high-quality content

name: Modular RAG(MRAG)
description: Flexible RAG architecture with interchangeable modules supporting iterative, adaptive, and non-sequential retrieval patterns

tldr.what: Swaps retrieval components (search, memory, routing) in and out to adapt how an agent finds and uses knowledge across queries.
tldr.when: Systems needing different retrieval strategies for different query types, or where retrieval quality improves by learning from past interactions.
tldr.watchOut: High complexity and many moving parts make debugging failures hard; unclear which module caused poor results.

overview.pattern: Decomposed RAG architecture with independent, interchangeable modules connected through standardized interfaces
overview.why: Enables flexibility, maintainability, and team scalability by separating concerns into distinct, testable components
overview.insight: Module boundaries defined by function (retrieval, ranking, fusion, generation) with standardized APIs enabling hot-swapping

impl.d: Create independent retrieval, generation, and augmentation modules
Compose modules into flexible processing pipelines
Route queries to appropriate module combinations
Coordinate execution and data flow between modules

overview.example: query → module_router → [retrieval_module, rerank_module, fusion_module] → generation_module → response
dos: Design modules with clear input/output interfaces and standardized APIs
Implement hot-swappable modules for A/B testing and gradual rollouts
Use dependency injection for flexible module composition
Cache module outputs at appropriate granularity levels
Implement module health checks and fallback mechanisms
donts: Create tight coupling between modules or shared mutable state
Skip module versioning and backward compatibility considerations
Ignore module-level monitoring and observability
Over-engineer module boundaries for simple use cases
Neglect module performance isolation and resource limits
use: Large-scale RAG systems requiring flexibility and maintainability
Multi-team development with different domain expertise
Need for rapid experimentation with different approaches
Systems requiring different behavior for different query types
Production environments needing gradual rollouts and A/B testing
avoid: Resource-constrained environments with tight latency budgets
Small teams without modular architecture experience

metrics.d: Independence and replaceability of individual modules

name: Self-RAG(SRAG)
description: Self-reflective RAG that adaptively determines retrieval necessity and evaluates retrieval quality through reflection tokens

tldr.what: Agent decides whether to retrieve external knowledge, evaluates retrieved content quality, and assesses its own output before responding, using reflection tokens to guide these decisions.
tldr.when: Tasks requiring factual accuracy where the agent's confidence varies, or where retrieval cost matters and you want to skip unnecessary lookups.
tldr.watchOut: Reflection tokens add latency and cost; poor calibration causes the agent to retrieve when it shouldn't or skip retrieval when it should.

overview.pattern: RAG system with adaptive retrieval decisions and self-reflection using trained reflection tokens for quality assessment
overview.why: Improves factual accuracy and reduces hallucinations through iterative self-critique and selective knowledge retrieval
overview.insight: Reflection tokens ([Retrieve], [IsRel], [IsSup], [IsUse]) enable models to assess retrieval necessity and response quality

impl.d: Assess whether external knowledge is needed for the query
Fetch relevant passages and apply neural reranking
Create initial response using retrieved context
Use reflection tokens to evaluate response quality

overview.example: query → retrieval_gate → retrieve → generate → self_critique → [refine] → final_response
dos: Train models with reflection tokens ([Retrieve], [IsRel], [IsSup], [IsUse])
Implement retrieval necessity prediction to avoid unnecessary context
Use calibrated confidence thresholds for triggering refinement
Enforce citation requirements with evidence grounding
Cache reflection outputs and retrieval results for efficiency
donts: Allow unconstrained reflection tokens that become verbose
Skip validation of self-critique calibration against ground truth
Create infinite refinement loops without iteration limits
Rely solely on self-assessment without external validation
Ignore computational cost of multiple generation rounds
use: Factual accuracy and verifiability are critical requirements
Domain expertise requires balancing parametric and retrieved knowledge
Applications need confidence calibration and uncertainty quantification
High-stakes decisions requiring explainable reasoning and citations
Knowledge-intensive tasks in medical, legal, or scientific domains
avoid: Simple queries where standard RAG provides sufficient accuracy
Real-time applications with strict latency constraints
Resource-constrained environments limiting multiple generation rounds
Domains with insufficient training data for reliable self-critique
Applications where citation overhead is unnecessary

metrics.d: Factual accuracy and consistency with retrieved evidence
Correlation between confidence scores and actual accuracy
Proportion of retrieved passages that are genuinely useful

Quality gains per additional token or retrieval call

usecases.d: Clinical decision support requiring high accuracy and evidence-based responses

name: Corrective RAG (CRAG)(CRAG)
description: RAG system that automatically detects and corrects poor retrieval results through quality assessment and re-retrieval

tldr.what: Retrieves documents, scores their relevance, re-retrieves with refined queries when quality falls below threshold.
tldr.when: Retrieval-heavy tasks where initial results are often incomplete or stale, and you can afford extra API calls.
tldr.watchOut: Quality thresholds set too high trigger endless re-retrieval loops; too low defeats the purpose and wastes compute.

overview.pattern: Enhanced RAG with explicit retrieval quality evaluation and corrective actions based on confidence scoring
overview.why: Reduces hallucinations and improves accuracy through quality assessment and adaptive correction strategies
overview.insight: Three-tier correction strategy: refine high-confidence, supplement medium-confidence, re-retrieve low-confidence results

impl.d: Retrieve candidate documents using dense/sparse/hybrid search
Evaluate retrieval quality with confidence scoring (high/medium/low)
Refine, supplement, or re-retrieve based on confidence band
Decompose and recompose evidence for optimal context
Generate response with citations and optional verification

dos: Implement explicit retrieval quality evaluator with calibrated confidence thresholds
Use knowledge refinement with decompose-then-recompose for evidence processing
Apply web search supplementation for medium confidence retrieval results
Enforce strict citation requirements with provenance tracking
Cache evaluator outputs and refined knowledge for efficiency
donts: Allow evaluator miscalibration without regular confidence score validation
Skip query drift prevention during corrective re-retrieval
Create unbounded correction loops without cost and latency controls
Mix outdated and fresh sources without temporal reconciliation
Neglect abstention mechanisms when confidence remains persistently low
use: High-stakes applications requiring verified accuracy and provenance
Rapidly changing domains with frequent content updates
Noisy or heterogeneous knowledge bases with quality variation
Long-tail queries where initial retrieval often fails
Regulated environments requiring explicit evidence grounding
avoid: Real-time applications with strict latency requirements
Closed-book tasks where parametric knowledge suffices
High-quality homogeneous corpora with consistent recall
Environments prohibiting external web access for supplementation
Simple factual queries with reliable standard RAG performance

metrics.d: Factual correctness and groundedness in retrieved evidence
Accuracy of quality confidence predictions (ROC-AUC, ECE)
Percentage of claims supported by evidence

usecases.d: Case law analysis requiring verified sources and temporal accuracy
Clinical decision support with evidence-based recommendations and safety checks
Market research combining real-time data with historical knowledge
Government and regulatory information requiring up-to-date accuracy
Software and API documentation with version-specific corrections

name: Graph RAG(GRAG)
description: Knowledge graph-enhanced RAG using entity relationships and community detection for global sensemaking queries

tldr.what: Builds an entity knowledge graph from documents, detects communities within it, then answers queries by summarizing relevant communities rather than retrieving individual chunks.
tldr.when: Answering broad analytical questions across large document collections where entity relationships and thematic groupings matter more than keyword matching.
tldr.watchOut: Graph construction and community detection are computationally expensive; quality degrades sharply if entity extraction or relationship identification fails early.

overview.pattern: Knowledge graph-based RAG with community detection and hierarchical summarization for large-scale reasoning
overview.why: Enables complex multi-hop reasoning and relationship understanding through structured graph traversal
overview.insight: Microsoft's approach uses community detection algorithms to create hierarchical summaries for global and local reasoning

impl.d: NER/RE to extract entities and relations, build knowledge graph
Create graph indexes and hybrid text-vector search capabilities
Parse query entities and map to graph nodes
Multi-hop graph traversal with bounded expansion
Serialize graph context and generate response

overview.example: query → entity_linking → graph_traversal → subgraph_assembly → llm_generation → response
dos: Implement community detection algorithms for large-scale graph summarization
Use hierarchical indexing with global and local community summaries
Apply entity resolution and deduplication to maintain graph quality
Combine vector search with graph traversal for hybrid retrieval
Implement bounded traversal with explicit hop limits (1-3 hops)
donts: Allow uncontrolled graph traversal that leads to context explosion
Skip entity linking validation and confidence scoring
Neglect graph maintenance and consistency validation
Create overly complex schemas that hinder query performance
Ignore provenance tracking for graph edges and entity sources
use: Complex multi-hop reasoning requiring entity relationship understanding
Knowledge-intensive domains with rich interconnected information
Enterprise data with well-defined entity schemas and relationships
Fact-checking and verification requiring structured evidence paths
Large-scale knowledge bases needing hierarchical summarization
avoid: Simple factual queries adequately served by document-based RAG
Domains with poor entity extraction and relation modeling quality
Real-time applications with strict latency requirements
Small datasets where graph complexity exceeds retrieval benefits
Applications lacking well-defined entity schemas or ontologies

metrics.d: Precision/recall of extracted entities and relations
Coherence and relevance of detected communities
Proportion of relevant subgraphs in query results

usecases.d: Drug-disease-gene relationship exploration with scientific literature integration
Company-industry-market relationship modeling for investment research
Case law relationship mapping with precedent and citation analysis
Organizational relationship modeling with department and project connections
Citation networks and research collaboration graph analysis

name: Multimodal RAG(MMRAG)
description: Retrieval-augmented generation that handles and integrates text, images, audio, video, and structured data sources

tldr.what: Retrieves and combines text, images, audio, video, and structured data using aligned embeddings to ground generation in multimodal evidence.
tldr.when: Problems requiring answers grounded in diverse media types, like medical diagnosis from scans plus text, or design review from docs plus screenshots.
tldr.watchOut: Embedding alignment across modalities is fragile; misaligned spaces cause retrieval to favor one modality, degrading answers that need true fusion.

overview.pattern: Multi-modal RAG system that retrieves and fuses evidence across text, images, audio, and video using specialized encoders
overview.why: Enables comprehensive understanding by combining information from multiple modalities that text-only systems miss
overview.insight: Per-modality encoders (CLIP, Whisper, BLIP-2) with learned fusion weights for cross-modal evidence integration

impl.d: Process text, images, audio, video with modality-specific preprocessing
Create per-modality embeddings using specialized encoders (CLIP, BLIP-2)
Search across modalities using hybrid retrieval strategies
Combine multi-modal results with learned fusion weights
Use vision-language models with cross-modal evidence citations

overview.example: multi_modal_query → [text_search, image_search, audio_search] → fusion → vlm_generation → response
dos: Use modality-specific encoders (CLIP for vision, Whisper for audio)
Implement hybrid retrieval combining lexical and vector search per modality
Apply learned fusion weights calibrated for different modality combinations
Cache OCR, ASR, and visual features to reduce preprocessing overhead
Include temporal alignment for audio/video with precise timestamps
donts: Rely solely on text embeddings for visual or audio content
Skip quality validation for OCR/ASR outputs that may be noisy
Inline raw media files instead of using feature references
Mix incomparable similarity scores across modalities without calibration
Ignore privacy and compliance requirements for sensitive media content
use: Document analysis requiring understanding of both text and visual elements
Media-rich content search across images, videos, and audio
E-commerce and product discovery with visual and textual attributes
Educational content combining slides, audio lectures, and notes
Healthcare applications integrating medical imaging with clinical text
avoid: Pure text-based applications where other modalities add no value
Strict latency requirements incompatible with multi-modal processing
Limited computational resources unable to handle vision/audio models
Domains with poor OCR/ASR quality where visual/audio signals are unreliable

metrics.d: Recall@k and MRR across different modality combinations
Performance improvement from multi-modal vs single-modal retrieval
Accuracy of vision-language model outputs with multi-modal evidence
Precision of cross-modal evidence attribution and source linking
Balanced utilization of available modalities in retrieval results
Latency and cost per modality including preprocessing overhead

usecases.d: Research papers with figures, tables, and mathematical equations
Product discovery combining visual appearance with textual descriptions
Course materials integrating lecture slides, audio, and supplementary text
Troubleshooting guides with screenshots, videos, and written instructions
Clinical studies combining medical imaging, patient records, and literature

name: Agentic RAG(AgRAG)
description: Autonomous retrieval-augmented generation systems with self-directed planning, retrieval, and reasoning capabilities

tldr.what: Agent autonomously plans retrieval steps, refines queries based on results, and reasons across multiple documents without human intervention between searches.
tldr.when: Complex research questions requiring multi-domain knowledge, iterative refinement, or reasoning chains that span many documents.
tldr.watchOut: Agents can loop indefinitely chasing marginal improvements or retrieve irrelevant documents when query refinement goes off-track.

overview.pattern: Autonomous agent systems that dynamically plan, execute, and adapt multi-step retrieval strategies using tools and reasoning
overview.why: Enables complex information gathering workflows that require strategic thinking, adaptation, and multi-source synthesis
overview.insight: ReAct-style planning with tool orchestration allows agents to reason about retrieval strategies and adapt based on results

impl.d: Decompose complex queries into multi-step retrieval plans with reasoning
Execute retrieval actions using specialized tools (search, DB, APIs)
Adapt strategy based on intermediate results and feedback
Integrate multi-source evidence with reasoning chains
Generate final answer with full citation and reasoning trace

overview.example: complex_query → plan_decomposition → [retrieve_1, retrieve_2, ...] → adapt_strategy → synthesize → response
dos: Implement explicit planning with ReAct or function calling for retrieval strategies
Use tool-augmented retrieval with specialized APIs, search engines, and databases
Enable adaptive query refinement based on intermediate retrieval results
Maintain detailed reasoning traces and citation provenance throughout execution
Implement error recovery and alternative retrieval strategies for failed attempts
donts: Allow uncontrolled agent loops without termination conditions or cost limits
Skip validation of retrieved information quality and source credibility
Ignore user intent drift during multi-step retrieval processes
Rely solely on single retrieval modality without exploring alternatives
Neglect privacy and security considerations for sensitive information retrieval
use: Complex multi-step research requiring strategic information gathering
Cross-domain queries needing diverse knowledge sources and reasoning
Dynamic knowledge environments where retrieval strategies must adapt
High-stakes applications requiring explainable reasoning and provenance
Research and analysis tasks benefiting from human-like information seeking
avoid: Simple factual queries adequately served by standard RAG approaches
Real-time applications with strict latency and cost constraints
Domains with limited tool availability or API access restrictions
Applications where deterministic retrieval behavior is required
Resource-constrained environments unable to support complex agent reasoning

metrics.d: Percentage of agent plans successfully completed without errors
Quality improvement from adaptive vs fixed retrieval strategies
Coherence and completeness of multi-source information integration
Accuracy and explainability of step-by-step reasoning chains
Optimal use of available retrieval tools and APIs
Answer quality per unit computational cost and API calls

usecases.d: Scientific literature review with adaptive search strategies and cross-reference validation
Market research combining financial data, news, and industry reports with strategic reasoning
Case law research with multi-jurisdictional search and precedent analysis workflows
Software debugging and troubleshooting with dynamic tool selection and reasoning
Clinical decision support with evidence gathering from multiple medical databases

description: Retrieve information based on abstract reasoning patterns rather than explicit queries in multi-agent agentic AI systems

tldr.what: Retrieves knowledge by inferring abstract reasoning patterns across agents rather than matching explicit keywords, synthesizing insights from latent conceptual relationships.
tldr.when: Multi-agent systems tackling open-ended problems where relevant knowledge spans disconnected domains and implicit connections matter more than direct matches.
tldr.watchOut: High computational cost and brittleness: agents may confidently retrieve plausible but incorrect knowledge when latent patterns don't actually align with ground truth.

name: Query Transformation Retrieval(QTR)
description: Rewrite or expand the user query before retrieval so embeddings land near relevant documents. HyDE generates a hypothetical answer document and embeds that to find real neighbors, multi-query expansion issues several reformulations and fuses the results, and step-back prompting abstracts the question to retrieve underlying principles first. These transformations give large zero-shot retrieval gains without training the retriever.
features: Reciprocal rank fusion of result sets

tldr.what: Rewrites or expands queries before retrieval-via hypothetical answers, multiple reformulations, or abstraction to principles-to improve embedding alignment with relevant documents.
tldr.when: Vague or under-specified user questions where direct embedding fails to surface relevant documents without retraining the retriever.
tldr.watchOut: Transformation can hallucinate plausible but incorrect intermediate queries, leading to confident retrieval of irrelevant or misleading documents.

flow.title: Query Transformation Retrieval
flow.description: Rewrite the user query before retrieval so embeddings land near relevant documents. A vague query is expanded through HyDE, multi-query reformulation, and step-back abstraction, and the three result sets are fused into a grounded answer.

nodes.label:
❓ Vague Query
"why is my thing slow"

🔄 Query Transformer
Rewrite before retrieval

🗄️ Vector Index
Embedded doc chunks

📝 HyDE
Draft a hypothetical answer,
embed the draft

🌿 Multi-Query Expansion
3 reformulations of the query

🪜 Step-Back Abstraction
Ask for general principles

🎯 Retrieve (HyDE vec)
Neighbors of the draft doc

🎯 Retrieve x3
Top-10 per reformulation

🎯 Retrieve (principles)
Foundational passages first

🔀 Reciprocal Rank Fusion
Merge + dedupe 3 result sets

📄 Top 8 Passages
Highest fused rank

steps.title: Vague Query Arrives
steps.description: A 4-word query "why is my thing slow" is too sparse for plain semantic search to place near the right chunks.

steps.title: Fan Out Transformations
steps.description: The transformer rewrites the query three ways in parallel: HyDE, multi-query expansion, and step-back abstraction.

steps.title: HyDE Hypothetical Document
steps.description: The LLM drafts a plausible answer ("unindexed queries, N+1 lookups, cold cache...") and embeds that draft instead of the raw query to find real neighbors.

steps.title: Multi-Query and Step-Back
steps.description: Multi-query issues three reformulations and pulls top-10 each; step-back abstracts to "general principles of performance tuning" and retrieves foundational passages first.

steps.title: Fuse Result Sets
steps.description: Reciprocal rank fusion merges the three retrieval sets, deduplicates, and keeps the top 8 passages by fused rank.

steps.title: Grounded Answer
steps.description: The top passages surface the exact chunk plain search missed. The answer cites them: an unindexed query on orders.user_id, fixed by adding an index and enabling query caching.

references: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE, Gao et al. 2022) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10496
Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction in Large Language Models - https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06117
Query Expansion by Prompting Large Language Models - https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.03653

name: Hierarchical Index Retrieval (RAPTOR)(HIR)
description: Build the retrieval index as a multi-level tree instead of a flat list of chunks. RAPTOR recursively embeds, clusters, and summarizes chunks so a query can retrieve from any abstraction level, returning big-picture synthesis or leaf detail as needed. Anthropic contextual retrieval prepends an LLM-written context blurb to each chunk before embedding so isolated chunks stay grounded in the whole document.
features: Hybrid embedding plus BM25 candidate generation

tldr.what: Builds a multi-level tree index by recursively clustering and summarizing chunks, allowing retrieval from any abstraction level to return either broad synthesis or specific details.
tldr.when: Long documents where queries need both high-level overviews and precise leaf details, and where isolated chunks lose meaning without document context.
tldr.watchOut: High computational cost during indexing and significant complexity in implementation; misaligned clustering can create unhelpful abstraction levels that degrade retrieval quality.

flow.title: Hierarchical Index Retrieval (RAPTOR)
flow.description: Build the retrieval index as a multi-level tree instead of a flat chunk list. RAPTOR recursively clusters and summarizes chunks, and contextual augmentation grounds each chunk, so a multi-hop question is answered from a mid-tree summary plus leaf detail.

"Failover is deferred during the
02:00-03:00 backup window"

steps.title: Chunk the Document
steps.description: A 300-page manual is split into roughly 1,200 leaf chunks of about 100 tokens each.

steps.title: Contextual Augmentation
steps.description: Each chunk gets a 1-2 sentence blurb ("This section, from Chapter 7 on High Availability, describes...") prepended before embedding so isolated chunks stay grounded.

steps.title: Recursive Cluster and Summarize
steps.description: Similar leaves are softly clustered, each cluster is summarized by an LLM into a parent, and the process repeats on the summaries to grow the tree.

steps.title: Tree Built
steps.description: The result is a RAPTOR tree: raw leaves at the bottom, mid-level cluster summaries above, and a root summarizing the whole document.

steps.title: Query the Collapsed Tree
steps.description: The multi-hop question is embedded and collapsed-tree search ranks nodes from every layer together, so summaries and leaves compete on the same footing.

steps.title: Retrieve Across Levels
steps.description: Retrieval returns a mid-tree summary (failover and backup share the coordination lock) plus the exact leaf detail (backups run 02:00-03:00 UTC).

steps.title: Compose the Answer
steps.description: Combining synthesis and specifics: failover is deferred during the 02:00-03:00 backup window because both hold the coordination lock. RAPTOR gains about 20% absolute on QuALITY; contextual retrieval cuts failed retrievals 49%, 67% with a reranker.

references: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval - https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.18059
Introducing Contextual Retrieval (Anthropic) - https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval

name: Deep Research Agent(DRA)
description: A composite long-horizon research architecture that clarifies the user's intent, drafts an explicit research plan, then runs an iterative search, read, and evaluate-gaps loop across many sources (often via parallel subagents) before synthesizing a single long-form report with inline citation attribution. This is the assembled archetype behind OpenAI Deep Research, Gemini Deep Research, and Anthropic Research, with its own survey literature. Distinct from `agentic-rag-systems`, which applies retrieval decisioning inside a single pipeline rather than running a multi-round, plan-driven report synthesis. Distinct from `supervisor-worker-pattern`, which is generic orchestration with no research-specific plan, gap-check, or citation pass.
features: Drafted research plan that decomposes the question
Iterative search, read, and gap-evaluation loop
Adaptive re-planning that pivots on findings
Long-form synthesis with inline citation attribution

tldr.what: Clarifies intent, drafts a research plan, then iteratively searches, reads, and evaluates gaps across sources before synthesizing a cited report.
tldr.when: Multi-source research questions requiring adaptive exploration, explicit gap-checking, and traceable attribution before delivering a comprehensive synthesis.
tldr.watchOut: High token and latency cost from multiple rounds, parallel searches, and re-planning; citation accuracy degrades if sources are not carefully tracked through each loop.

flow.title: Deep Research Agent
flow.description: A long-horizon research architecture that clarifies intent, drafts an explicit plan, runs an iterative search, read, and gap-evaluation loop across many sources with parallel subagents, then synthesizes a single cited report. Shown on a market-analysis question that pivots into a second research round.

steps.title: Intent Clarification
steps.description: The agent asks a clarifying question before committing, narrowing an underspecified request to enterprise segment, three dimensions, and a 12-month horizon.

steps.title: Research Plan
steps.description: The agent drafts an explicit plan that decomposes the question into three sub-questions covering incumbents, adoption, and differentiation.

steps.title: Parallel Retrieval
steps.description: The lead agent spawns three subagents in separate context windows, each searching and reading a distinct sub-question across many sources.

steps.title: Gap Evaluation
steps.description: The lead agent merges the 34 collected sources and evaluates coverage, detecting a missing angle: security and compliance as a buying factor.

steps.title: Second Research Round
steps.description: The detected gap triggers an adaptive second round: a new subagent researches procurement and SOC 2, pivoting the plan on findings rather than following a fixed pipeline.

steps.title: Synthesis
steps.description: Merged findings plus the second-round sources are synthesized into a structured long-form analysis with a market map, pricing table, adoption drivers, and risks.

steps.title: Citation and Report
steps.description: A final citation pass attributes every claim to one of the 40 sources, producing a cited report with a competitive matrix.

name: Structure-Aware Codebase Retrieval (Repo Map)
description: Retrieval specialized for code that exploits program structure instead of (or alongside) embeddings. The repo is parsed into ASTs and a symbol and dependency graph with tree-sitter; files and symbols are ranked by graph centrality (Aider's PageRank-weighted tag map), graph-traversal tools walk call, definition, and import edges (AutoCodeRover and code-graph agents), and spectrum-based fault localization can narrow the search from failing tests. This lets a coding agent assemble a minimal, relevant context from a repository far larger than its context window. Distinct from `graph-rag`, whose graph is built from document entities rather than from code semantics.
features: Tree-sitter AST parse into a symbol table
Symbol and dependency graph over call, def, and import edges
PageRank-style centrality ranking of files and symbols
Graph-traversal tools over the code graph
Optional spectrum-based fault localization from failing tests

tldr.what: Parses code into ASTs and builds a symbol-dependency graph, then ranks files and functions by centrality to retrieve only the most relevant code for a task.
tldr.when: Large codebases where embeddings alone miss structural relationships, or when a coding agent needs to navigate call chains and imports to understand context.
tldr.watchOut: Graph construction and ranking are expensive upfront; stale graphs cause retrieval misses if code structure changes between parses.

flow.title: Structure-Aware Codebase Retrieval (Repo Map)
flow.description: Code retrieval that exploits program structure instead of embeddings alone. A tree-sitter parse builds a symbol and dependency graph, PageRank-style centrality ranks the relevant symbols, and graph traversal over call edges finds the write path, assembling a minimal context from a 500k-line repo that never fits in the model window.

logout" - 500k-line repo

🌲 Tree-sitter Parse
ASTs for every source file

🚫 Load Whole Repo

(avoided)

🔤 Symbol Table
Definitions and references

🕸️ Code Graph
Nodes: symbols and files
Edges: call, def, import

📊 PageRank Ranking
Centrality over the graph
Boost: settings, logout, persist

🏅 Top-Ranked Symbols
SettingsStore.save
AuthService.logout, useSettings

🧭 Dependency Traversal
Walk call edges from
AuthService.logout

logout() clears session
before SettingsStore.flush()

➡️ Write Path

steps.title: Bug in a Large Repo
steps.description: A bug must be fixed in a 500k-line codebase. Loading the whole repo into context is impossible, so the agent retrieves by structure instead.

steps.title: Parse to Symbols
steps.description: Tree-sitter parses every source file into ASTs and extracts a symbol table of definitions and references.

steps.title: Build Code Graph
steps.description: Symbols and files become nodes; call, definition, and import relationships become edges, giving a graph derived from code semantics rather than text similarity.

steps.title: Rank by Centrality
steps.description: A PageRank-style pass ranks nodes by centrality, boosting identifiers named in the task, and surfaces the top symbols: SettingsStore.save, AuthService.logout, and useSettings.

steps.title: Dependency Traversal
steps.description: From AuthService.logout the agent walks call edges, tracing the write path and finding the ordering bug: logout clears the session before the settings flush runs.

steps.title: Assemble Minimal Context
steps.description: Only the ~6 relevant symbols and their signatures are pulled into context, about 1,200 tokens instead of the entire repository.

steps.title: Fix and Verify
steps.description: The agent reorders logout to flush settings before clearing the session; the failing test now passes, matching where spectrum-based fault localization pointed.
