name: Chain-of-Thought(CoT)
description: Breaks down complex problems into step-by-step intermediate reasoning steps
features: Decomposes complex problems into manageable sub-problems

tldr.what: Prompts the model to show intermediate reasoning steps before reaching a final answer, making the solution path explicit.
tldr.when: Problems requiring multi-step logic, math, or causal reasoning where showing work helps catch errors and improves accuracy.
tldr.watchOut: Longer reasoning can amplify early mistakes; each step compounds errors from prior steps, degrading final answers.

overview.pattern: Generate explicit step-by-step reasoning before final answer
overview.why: Makes reasoning transparent, improves accuracy on complex problems, enables error detection
overview.insight: Add 'Let's think step by step' trigger + numbered reasoning steps → 2-5x accuracy gain

impl.d: Add "Let's think step by step" trigger

dos: Use consistent step numbering (Step 1, Step 2, etc.)
Include verification steps for calculations
Provide diverse few-shot examples
Break complex problems into sub-problems
Use clear reasoning triggers ("Let's think...")
donts: Skip intermediate steps for "obvious" calculations
Use CoT for simple, direct questions
Ignore token cost increase (2-5x overhead)
Make reasoning steps too verbose or redundant
Forget to validate logical consistency

usecases.d: "If a train travels 60 mph for 2 hours..." → step-by-step calculation
Multi-conditional problems requiring systematic elimination
Trace execution path step-by-step to find errors
Break down ROI calculations with intermediate steps
Systematic symptom analysis → differential diagnosis

nodes.label:
Problem:
"If 5 machines make 5 widgets
in 5 minutes, how long for
100 machines to make 100 widgets?"

Standard Prompt:
Just the question

CoT Prompt:
Question +
"Let's think step by step"
LLM (Direct Response)

Same LLM
(Step-by-Step Mode)

❌ Wrong Answer:
"100 minutes"

✓ Correct Answer:
"5 minutes"

Shows reasoning:
"Each machine makes
1 widget in 5 minutes.
100 machines make
100 widgets in 5 min."

steps.title: Problem Presentation
steps.description: A classic reasoning problem that trips up many LLMs when asked directly. This tests the model's ability to avoid linear thinking traps.
steps.input: If 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes, how long would it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets?

steps.title: Standard Approach (No CoT)
steps.description: Without Chain-of-Thought prompting, the model often jumps to a conclusion using faulty linear reasoning: "5 machines → 5 widgets, so 100 machines → 100 widgets must take 100 minutes."
steps.input: Direct question without any prompting strategy

steps.title: Standard LLM Response
steps.description: The model gives a quick, intuitive but wrong answer. It fails to work through the rate calculation properly.

steps.title: CoT Approach - Add Magic Phrase
steps.description: Now we ask the exact same question but add "Let's think step by step" at the end. This simple addition triggers a completely different reasoning process in the same model.
steps.input: Same question + "Let's think step by step"

steps.title: CoT Triggers Systematic Reasoning
steps.description: With the magic phrase, the same LLM now breaks down the problem systematically instead of jumping to conclusions.

steps.title: Step-by-Step Reasoning Process
steps.description: The model now shows its work: "Let's think step by step. If 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes, then each machine makes 1 widget in 5 minutes. So the rate is 1 widget per machine per 5 minutes. Therefore, 100 machines would make 100 widgets in... 5 minutes!"

steps.title: Correct Answer Through CoT
steps.description: By simply adding "Let's think step by step", we get the correct answer. The same model, same weights, same everything - just better prompting. This is the power of Chain-of-Thought: dramatic improvement from a simple prompt modification.

references: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models (Wei et al., 2022) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11903
Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning (Wang et al., 2022) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171
Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning (Zhou et al., 2022) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.10625
Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners (Kojima et al., 2022) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.11916
Anthropic Claude Chain of Thought Best Practices - https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/chain-prompts

name: Tree-of-Thought(ToT)
description: Explores multiple reasoning paths through branching and backtracking
features: Ideal for strategic planning and complex decisions

tldr.what: Explores multiple reasoning branches in parallel, evaluates each path, backtracks to promising nodes, and selects the best solution.
tldr.when: Complex decisions with multiple valid approaches, strategic planning requiring trade-off analysis, or problems where early choices constrain later options.
tldr.watchOut: Exponential token cost and latency grow quickly; most branches waste compute on paths that won't be selected.

overview.pattern: Explore multiple reasoning paths through branching tree structure with evaluation and pruning
overview.why: Enables backtracking, lookahead, and exploration of alternatives for complex problem-solving
overview.insight: Generate K candidates → Evaluate → Prune weak paths → Expand promising ones → Repeat until solution

impl.d: Set branching factor K & max depth
Create K candidate thoughts per node
Keep top candidates, discard weak paths

overview.example: Problem → [Branch 1, Branch 2, Branch 3] → Evaluate → Prune → Expand best → Solution
dos: Use small branching factor (K=3-5) to control costs
Implement explicit evaluation criteria/rubrics
Cache and deduplicate equivalent states
Set budget limits (max tokens/time) with fallbacks
Use beam search for balanced exploration
donts: Allow unlimited branching (combinatorial explosion)
Skip evaluation steps (leads to random exploration)
Use for simple problems (overkill vs CoT)
Ignore cycles/loops in reasoning paths
Over-prune early promising paths
use: Complex problems with multiple solution paths

usecases.d: Explore different operator combinations → evaluate validity → prune impossible paths
Generate scenario branches → assess outcomes → select optimal strategy
Develop plot alternatives → evaluate narrative coherence → pursue best storylines
Try multiple solution approaches → verify correctness → backtrack if needed
Explore design patterns → evaluate trade-offs → select best approach

flow.title: Tree of Thoughts (ToT) Pattern
flow.description: Shows parallel exploration of multiple solution paths with evaluation

steps.title: Solution Evaluation
steps.description: Each branch calculates its solution and measures the total distance.
steps.input: Calculate total distance for each route

steps.title: Solution Refinement

name: Graph-of-Thought(GoT)
description: Non-linear reasoning with thoughts as nodes and dependencies as edges
features: Thoughts as vertices, dependencies as edges
Superior to linear CoT for complex problems

tldr.what: Models reasoning as a directed graph where thoughts are nodes, dependencies are edges, and the agent explores multiple paths with backtracking and synthesis.
tldr.when: Problems with many interdependent factors where linear reasoning misses emergent solutions or requires revisiting earlier conclusions.
tldr.watchOut: Computational cost and latency grow sharply; easy to lose coherence across a large graph without explicit synthesis steps.

overview.pattern: Non-linear reasoning network with nodes (thoughts) and edges (dependencies) enabling cross-path synthesis
overview.why: Supports complex interdependent problems through backtracking, merging, and conflict resolution
overview.insight: Thoughts as graph nodes → Explicit dependencies → Cross-path merging → Coherent synthesis

impl.d: Extract coherent solution from best subgraph

overview.example: Problem → [Node A ← Node B → Node C] → Merge paths → Synthesize solution
dos: Use explicit dependency tracking between thoughts
Implement robust cycle detection & deduplication
Design evaluators for scoring subgraphs not just nodes
Cache intermediate results & maintain visited states
Enable cross-path synthesis & conflict resolution
donts: Allow unlimited graph expansion (combinatorial explosion)
Merge incompatible branches without conflict checks
Skip thought granularity planning (too coarse/fine)
Use weak evaluators that mis-rank solution paths
Ignore token costs from graph exploration overhead

usecases.d: Node[Theory A] ← Node[Evidence 1] → Node[Synthesis] ← Node[Theory B]
Connect market analysis → product strategy → resource allocation → risk assessment
Link requirements → architecture → implementation → validation with feedback loops
Map stakeholder interests → regulatory constraints → implementation options → outcomes
Merge diverse solution approaches through cross-pollination nodes

name: ReAct
description: Combines reasoning with acting through external tool use

tldr.what: Agent loops through thought, calls external tools, observes results, then reasons on new data to decide next action.
tldr.when: Tasks requiring real-time information lookup, verification, or multi-step tool chains where each step depends on live feedback.
tldr.watchOut: Tool calls can fail or return stale data, forcing the agent into retry loops or hallucinated recovery attempts.

overview.pattern: Interleaved Reasoning and Acting through iterative Thought → Action → Observation cycles
overview.why: Enables dynamic problem-solving with real-time information and tool integration
overview.insight: Think before acting → Execute tools → Observe results → Reason about next step
overview.example: Thought → search("weather NYC") → Observation: "72°F sunny" → Thought → Done
dos: Clearly separate Thought and Action phases
Use structured action formats (function calls)
Process all observations before next reasoning
Implement proper tool error handling
Set maximum iteration limits to prevent loops
donts: Skip observation phase after actions
Use ambiguous or unstructured action formats
Allow infinite reasoning loops without convergence
Ignore tool failures or partial results
Mix reasoning and action in single step

usecases.d: Thought → search("AI trends 2024") → Observe results → search("specific trend") → Synthesize
Thought → query_database() → Observe data → calculate_stats() → Interpret results
Thought → run_tests() → Observe failures → examine_code() → Fix & retest
Thought → check_flights() → Observe options → check_hotels() → Book best combo
Thought → lookup_account() → Observe history → check_policy() → Provide solution

name: Forest-of-Thoughts(FoT)
description: Generates multiple reasoning trees to enhance diversity and robustness

tldr.what: Generates multiple independent reasoning trees exploring different angles, then synthesizes insights across trees to find robust solutions.
tldr.when: Complex problems requiring diverse perspectives, where single reasoning paths miss critical trade-offs or failure modes.
tldr.watchOut: Computational cost scales steeply with tree count; synthesis quality depends heavily on how well you weight and combine tree outputs.

overview.pattern: Generate multiple independent reasoning trees to enhance diversity and robustness
overview.why: Provides error tolerance, solution diversity, and cross-validation for complex problems
overview.insight: Multiple trees → Different strategies → Cross-validate → Robust consensus or best path

impl.d: Score each tree for quality & validity

overview.example: Problem → [Tree1: Strategy A, Tree2: Strategy B, Tree3: Strategy C] → Evaluate → Best Solution
dos: Generate trees with different starting assumptions
Use diverse reasoning strategies per tree
Implement robust cross-tree validation
Set limits on forest size (typically 3-7 trees)
Cache tree results to avoid redundant computation
donts: Generate too many similar trees (redundancy)
Skip diversity checks between trees
Allow unlimited tree generation (cost explosion)
Use same evaluation criteria for all trees
Ignore computational overhead vs single ToT
use: When single tree might miss solutions

usecases.d: Tree1(Technical), Tree2(Fundamental), Tree3(Sentiment) → Consensus decision
Multiple specialist perspectives → Cross-validate symptoms → Robust conclusion
Different scenario trees → Stress-test strategies → Optimal approach
Approach problem from multiple angles → Verify findings → Reliable results
Generate diverse concept trees → Evaluate aesthetics/function → Best design

name: Metacognitive Monitoring(MCM)
description: Self-awareness and monitoring of reasoning quality and confidence

tldr.what: Agent tracks its own reasoning quality, confidence levels, and knowledge gaps, then adjusts strategy or requests clarification based on self-assessment.
tldr.when: High-stakes decisions where wrong answers cause real harm and intermediate confidence checks can trigger additional data gathering or expert review.
tldr.watchOut: Confidence estimates often correlate poorly with actual accuracy; overconfident agents skip necessary verification steps despite high self-reported certainty.

overview.pattern: Continuous self-awareness and strategy adjustment during reasoning processes
overview.why: Enables adaptive problem-solving through confidence tracking, error detection, and method switching
overview.insight: Monitor reasoning quality → Detect low confidence/errors → Adapt strategy → Validate improvements
overview.example: Problem → Monitor confidence → "Low confidence, switch strategy" → New approach → Validate
dos: Continuously assess reasoning confidence levels
Implement explicit strategy evaluation checkpoints
Use calibrated confidence scoring (0-100%)
Build error detection patterns for common mistakes
Create strategy switching triggers and fallbacks
donts: Monitor without acting on low confidence signals
Use vague confidence assessments ("maybe", "probably")
Skip validation when switching reasoning strategies
Ignore consistent pattern of reasoning failures
Over-monitor simple tasks (cognitive overhead)

metrics.d: Alignment between confidence and actual accuracy
Percentage of mistakes caught before final answer
Time to recognize and change ineffective strategies

usecases.d: Monitor confidence → "Low confidence on rare disease" → Switch to specialist consultation mode
Track reasoning quality → Detect overconfidence in predictions → Apply conservative adjustments
Monitor understanding → "Complex logic, low confidence" → Request additional validation steps
Assess source integration → Identify knowledge gaps → Adapt search strategy
Monitor assumption validity → Detect weak reasoning → Strengthen analysis foundation

name: Test-Time Compute Scaling(TTC)
description: Dynamically allocates computational resources based on problem complexity

tldr.what: Allocates more reasoning steps or processing power to harder problems, fewer to simpler ones, adjusting in real time based on detected difficulty.
tldr.when: Problems vary widely in complexity and you can afford variable latency, or when some queries need deep reasoning while others need quick answers.
tldr.watchOut: Estimating problem complexity upfront is unreliable; you may overspend on easy problems or underspend on hard ones before detecting the mismatch.

overview.pattern: Dynamic allocation of computational resources based on problem difficulty and quality requirements
overview.why: Optimizes performance-cost trade-offs by investing more compute in harder problems while saving resources on easier ones
overview.insight: Assess difficulty → Scale compute allocation → Monitor quality gains → Adjust resources dynamically

impl.d: Use more search/reasoning for harder problems
Track solution quality vs compute spent

overview.example: Easy: 100 tokens → Medium: 500 tokens → Hard: 2000 tokens + search
dos: Implement difficulty detection heuristics early
Use progressive compute allocation (start small)
Monitor quality-to-compute efficiency ratios
Set maximum compute budgets to prevent runaway
Cache intermediate results for reuse
donts: Use fixed compute regardless of problem difficulty
Scale linearly without diminishing returns analysis
Ignore early quality signals (continue bad paths)
Allocate maximum compute to trivial problems
Skip difficulty calibration on diverse problem sets
use: Quality is more important than speed
avoid: When speed matters more than quality

metrics.d: Performance improvement per additional compute unit
Performance gains following predicted scaling curves

usecases.d: Easy algebra (50 tokens) → Complex proofs (2000+ tokens + verification)
Simple functions (200 tokens) → Complex algorithms (1000+ tokens + testing)
Basic queries (100 tokens) → Deep synthesis (1500+ tokens + cross-referencing)
Short responses (150 tokens) → Detailed narratives (1000+ tokens + revision)
Quick decisions (200 tokens) → Comprehensive strategies (2000+ tokens + scenario analysis)

name: Reflective Monte Carlo Tree Search(R-MCTS)
description: Enhanced MCTS with contrastive reflection for improved exploration
features: Gains that scale with how branchy the search space is

tldr.what: Expands a decision tree by sampling paths, then reflects on contrasts between successful and failed branches to guide future exploration.
tldr.when: Complex strategic problems requiring deep exploration of many options where you can evaluate partial solutions and learn from their differences.
tldr.watchOut: Computational cost grows rapidly with tree depth and branching factor, often exceeding gains unless reflection meaningfully prunes the search space.

overview.pattern: Monte Carlo Tree Search enhanced with reflective analysis at each phase for improved decision quality
overview.why: Combines systematic tree search with self-reflection to identify and correct reasoning errors during exploration
overview.insight: Select with reflection → Expand reasoning → Simulate with quality assessment → Reflect on errors → Backpropagate insights

impl.d: Navigate tree using UCB1 + reflection score
Generate new child nodes with reasoning

overview.example: UCB1 selection → Expand with reasoning → Simulate → Reflect on mistakes → Update tree
dos: Integrate reflection into all MCTS phases
Use domain-specific reflection criteria
Balance exploration vs reflection overhead
Maintain separate reflection and value networks
Cache reflection results for similar states
donts: Add reflection without clear quality metrics
Reflect on every node (computational explosion)
Use shallow reflection that misses key insights
Ignore reflection feedback in future selections
Apply uniform reflection depth regardless of uncertainty
use: Complex strategic domains with long-term consequences
Problems requiring error correction and learning
When simulation quality matters more than speed
avoid: Simple search problems with clear evaluation
Real-time applications with strict latency limits
When standard MCTS already performs well

usecases.d: Chess/Go with position evaluation reflection → Identify weak moves → Improve future selections
Generate solution → Reflect on bugs/efficiency → Backpropagate insights → Better code paths
Explore proof steps → Reflect on logical validity → Correct reasoning errors → Stronger proofs
Evaluate strategic options → Reflect on risk/assumptions → Update decision criteria → Optimal strategy
Design experiments → Reflect on methodology flaws → Improve research design → Better outcomes

name: Least-to-Most Prompting(LtM)
description: Progressive problem decomposition from simple to complex components

tldr.what: Solves complex problems by first solving simpler versions, then progressively adding constraints or complexity to reach the full solution.
tldr.when: Multi-step problems where each step builds on prior results and simpler cases reveal patterns applicable to harder ones.
tldr.watchOut: Early mistakes in simple cases compound through all subsequent steps, making the final answer wrong despite correct later reasoning.

overview.pattern: Problem decomposition strategy that solves complex tasks by breaking them into simpler subproblems solved sequentially
overview.why: Enables tackling complex problems by building solutions incrementally from simple to complex components
overview.insight: Decompose complex problem → Solve simplest first → Use previous solutions → Build up to final answer

impl.d: Break complex problem into simpler subproblems
Solve subproblems from simplest to most complex
Use previous solutions to inform next steps
Maintain growing context of solved parts
Combine all solutions into complete answer

overview.example: Complex Problem → [Sub1, Sub2, Sub3] → Solve Sub1 → Use Sub1 in Sub2 → Use Sub1+Sub2 in Sub3 → Final Answer
dos: Decompose into truly independent subproblems first
Solve subproblems in strict order of dependency
Explicitly pass previous solutions to next steps
Validate each subproblem solution before proceeding
Use clear problem reduction prompts and examples
donts: Skip the decomposition step (jump to complex reasoning)
Solve subproblems out of logical dependency order
Lose context between subproblem solving steps
Use when problems cannot be meaningfully decomposed
Over-decompose into trivial or atomic steps
use: Complex problems with clear hierarchical structure
avoid: Simple problems solvable in one step
Highly interconnected problems without clear decomposition
Problems where context accumulation hurts performance

metrics.d: Appropriateness and completeness of problem breakdown
Effective use of previous solutions in later steps
Accuracy vs direct problem solving approaches
Success across different problem types and domains

usecases.d: Complex equation → Break into steps → Solve algebraically → Combine for final answer
Large program → Decompose into functions → Implement each function → Integrate into working code
Complex topic → Outline main points → Develop each argument → Synthesize into coherent essay
Complex dataset → Break into analysis components → Solve each analysis → Integrate insights
Business challenge → Identify key areas → Develop solutions for each → Create comprehensive strategy

flow.title: Least-to-Most Prompting
flow.description: Progressive problem decomposition that breaks complex problems into simpler sub-problems, solving from easiest to most complex while building understanding

nodes.label:
🧮 Complex Problem
"Calculate compound interest
for $10,000 invested at 8%
for 15 years with quarterly
compounding"

🔍 Problem Decomposition
"This requires understanding:
1. Simple interest
2. Compound periods
3. Compound interest formula"

📐 Level 1: Simple Interest
"What is 8% of $10,000?
$10,000 × 0.08 = $800
per year"

📅 Level 1: Time Periods
"Quarterly = 4 times/year
15 years = 15 × 4 = 60
compounding periods"

📈 Level 1: Growth Concept
"Money grows each period
New amount becomes
base for next period"

🔢 Level 2: Quarterly Rate
"Annual 8% ÷ 4 quarters
= 2% per quarter
= 0.02 decimal"

💰 Level 2: Compound Growth
"After Q1: $10,000 × 1.02
After Q2: (result) × 1.02
Pattern: multiply by 1.02"

🧮 Level 2: Simple Calculation
"After 2 quarters:
$10,000 × (1.02)²
= $10,404"

📚 Level 3: General Formula
"For n periods at rate r:
Final = Principal × (1 + r)ⁿ
A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt)"

✅ Final Answer
A = $10,000 × 3.281
A = $32,810

"Built understanding step-by-step!"

❌ Direct Approach Fails
"Jump to complex formula
without understanding
→ Confusion & errors"

steps.title: Level 2: Combine Simple Concepts

steps.title: Level 3: Generalize to Formula

steps.title: Level 4: Apply to Original Complex Problem

name: Analogical Reasoning(AR)
description: Solves problems by finding and applying similar patterns from known domains

tldr.what: Solves novel problems by mapping structures from familiar domains onto unfamiliar ones, transferring known patterns across contexts.
tldr.when: Design or strategy problems where you lack direct precedent but can find structurally similar systems in other fields.
tldr.watchOut: Surface similarities can mask critical differences; transferred patterns often fail when domain constraints or incentives actually diverge.

overview.pattern: Reasoning by finding structural similarities between familiar and unfamiliar domains to transfer knowledge and solutions
overview.why: Leverages existing knowledge to solve new problems by identifying patterns and relationships that transcend specific domains
overview.insight: Identify analogous source → Map structural relationships → Transfer insights → Adapt to target context → Validate

impl.d: Find relevant analogous situations or domains
Identify correspondences between source and target
Apply insights from source to target problem
Modify transferred knowledge for target context
Verify analogy validity and solution quality

overview.example: Target Problem → Find Similar Case → Map Structure → Transfer Solution → Adapt & Validate
dos: Focus on structural similarities rather than surface features
Use multiple analogies to strengthen reasoning
Explicitly map relationships between source and target
Consider disanalogies and limitations of the mapping
Validate transferred knowledge in target domain
donts: Rely solely on superficial similarities
Use weak or irrelevant analogies without justification
Transfer knowledge without adapting to context
Ignore when analogies break down or fail
Over-extend analogies beyond their valid scope
use: Novel problems with existing similar solutions
When direct solution methods are unclear
avoid: When direct methods are more efficient

metrics.d: Structural similarity and relevance to target problem
Correctness in target domain after adaptation
Novel solutions generated through analogical thinking
Speed of solution discovery vs direct methods

usecases.d: Darwin's evolution theory inspired by Malthus population theory → Natural selection mechanism
Velcro invention inspired by burr seeds → Hook and loop fastener design
Netflix disruption analogous to Amazon retail model → Platform-based streaming strategy
Circuit breaker pattern from electrical systems → Fault tolerance in distributed systems
Heart pump analogy for understanding circulatory problems → Treatment approach insights

name: Causal Reasoning(CR)
description: Establishes and follows explicit cause-and-effect relationships

tldr.what: Traces effects backward through cause layers, identifies root causes, and models counterfactuals to plan interventions.
tldr.when: Problems with multiple contributing factors, where surface symptoms hide underlying mechanisms you must fix.
tldr.watchOut: Causal chains are speculative; correlations you identify may not reflect true causation without domain validation.

overview.pattern: Reasoning about cause-effect relationships, mechanisms, and interventions to understand how changes produce outcomes
overview.why: Enables prediction, explanation, and decision-making by understanding the underlying causal structure of systems
overview.insight: Identify causes → Understand mechanisms → Control confounds → Predict interventions → Analyze counterfactuals

impl.d: Identify variables and potential causal relationships
Consider what would happen if conditions changed

overview.example: X causes Y → Mechanism: X→M→Y → Control Z → Predict: do(X) → Counterfact: X=0?
dos: Distinguish correlation from causation explicitly
Identify plausible causal mechanisms and pathways
Consider confounding variables and alternative explanations
Use interventional thinking (what if we change X?)
Apply temporal precedence (causes precede effects)
donts: Assume correlation implies causation
Ignore potential confounding factors
Use post-hoc reasoning without mechanism
Make causal claims without sufficient evidence
Oversimplify complex causal systems
avoid: When only correlational data is available

metrics.d: Accuracy of predicted outcomes from actions
Synthesis of multiple sources for causal claims

usecases.d: Symptoms → Disease mechanism → Treatment intervention → Predicted recovery
Marketing spend → Customer acquisition mechanism → Revenue impact → ROI optimization
Error symptoms → Root cause identification → Code fix → System restoration
Regulation → Behavioral change mechanism → Economic effects → Unintended consequences
Hypothesis → Experimental design → Causal inference → Theory validation

flow.title: Causal Reasoning

steps.title: Correlation vs Causation Distinction
steps.description: Observes sales drop after website redesign but questions whether correlation implies causation. Generates multiple competing hypotheses: website, external factors, or competition.

steps.title: Causal Mechanism Exploration
steps.description: Goes beyond correlation to explore HOW redesign could cause sales drop. Maps detailed causal pathway: UI confusion → cart abandonment → lost sales.

steps.title: Counterfactual & Alternative Validation
steps.description: Considers counterfactual (what if no redesign?) and validates that external factors (economy, competition) are ruled out as primary causes.

steps.title: Causal Intervention Design
steps.description: Uses causal understanding to design targeted intervention: if UI confusion causes the problem, then fixing UI should restore sales performance.

steps.title: Causal Hypothesis Testing
steps.description: Tests causal model with A/B experiment comparing old vs new UI. Results confirm causation: old UI (2.1%) vs new UI (1.5%) conversion, validating causal chain.

name: Abductive Reasoning(ABR)
description: Infers the most likely explanation from incomplete observations

tldr.what: Generates competing hypotheses from incomplete data, then ranks them by likelihood given available evidence.
tldr.when: Diagnosing root causes with incomplete information, troubleshooting failures, or inferring hidden states from observable effects.
tldr.watchOut: Favors the most coherent story over the most probable one; confirmation bias can lock you into wrong hypotheses early.

overview.pattern: Inference to the best explanation by generating and evaluating hypotheses that explain observed phenomena
overview.why: Enables discovery and explanation by finding the most plausible account of surprising or puzzling observations
overview.insight: Observe surprising facts → Generate explanations → Rank by plausibility → Select best → Test predictions

impl.d: Identify surprising facts or phenomena to explain

overview.example: Surprising fact → Multiple explanations → Rank by plausibility → Best explanation → Test predictions
dos: Generate multiple competing hypotheses
Apply Occam's razor (prefer simpler explanations)
Consider prior knowledge and domain constraints
Evaluate explanatory power and coherence
Generate testable predictions from hypotheses
donts: Stop at the first plausible explanation
Ignore contradictory evidence or anomalies
Confuse abduction with deduction or induction
Accept explanations without considering alternatives
Overly complex explanations when simple ones suffice

metrics.d: Coherence and completeness of generated hypotheses
Quality of testable predictions from hypotheses
Optimal trade-off between simplicity and completeness

usecases.d: Patient symptoms → Multiple disease hypotheses → Most likely diagnosis → Treatment plan
Error behavior → Potential bug causes → Most probable root cause → Fix strategy
Anomalous data → Theoretical explanations → Best theory → New experiments
Performance decline → Possible causes → Primary factor → Action plan
Crime evidence → Suspect theories → Most likely scenario → Investigation direction

steps.title: Multiple Hypothesis Generation

name: Step-Back Prompting(SBP)
description: Abstracts to higher-level principles before tackling specific problems

tldr.what: Asks the agent to abstract to general principles before solving the specific problem, then applies those principles back down.
tldr.when: Complex decisions or technical problems where surface-level reasoning fails or loops, and underlying principles matter more than details.
tldr.watchOut: Abstraction can drift too far from the actual problem, making principles irrelevant or adding delay without improving the answer.

overview.pattern: Reasoning strategy that steps back to broader principles before tackling specific problems
overview.why: Improves reasoning by accessing relevant foundational knowledge and applying general principles to specific cases
overview.insight: Specific problem → Ask broader questions → Answer general principles → Apply to specific → Enhanced solution

impl.d: Present the specific problem to solve
Use general knowledge for specific problem
Solve original question with enhanced context

overview.example: Specific Q → "What are the general principles?" → Answer principles → Apply to specific Q → Solution
dos: Ask genuinely broader conceptual questions
Connect general principles to specific instances
Use step-back questions to access relevant knowledge
Ensure step-back questions are answerable
Bridge abstract reasoning back to concrete problem
donts: Make step-back questions too similar to original
Step back so far that context is lost
Skip the connection between general and specific
Use when direct reasoning is more efficient
Generate step-back questions without clear purpose
avoid: When direct knowledge access is sufficient

metrics.d: Appropriateness and relevance of step-back questions
Quality of connection between abstract and specific
Speed of applying general knowledge to specific case

usecases.d: "What's the acceleration?" → "What are Newton's laws?" → Apply F=ma → Calculate acceleration
"Why did Rome fall?" → "What causes empire collapse?" → General patterns → Rome-specific factors
"What's this rash?" → "What are dermatological principles?" → Apply to symptoms → Diagnosis
"How to increase sales?" → "What drives customer behavior?" → Apply behavioral insights → Strategy
"Why is this slow?" → "What causes performance issues?" → Performance principles → Specific optimization

flow.title: Step-Back Prompting
flow.description: Abstracts to higher-level principles and concepts before tackling specific problems, gaining broader perspective to improve solution quality

nodes.label:
📐 Specific Problem
"Calculate the area of
a trapezoid with bases
12cm and 8cm, height 5cm"

⚡ Direct Approach
"Just apply trapezoid formula:
A = ½(b₁ + b₂)h
A = ½(12 + 8)5 = 50cm²"

🔄 Step Back
"What higher-level concepts
apply here? What general
principles govern area?"

📚 Area Principles
"Area = space enclosed
Can be decomposed
Can be approximated
Units must be consistent"

🔺 Geometric Decomposition
"Complex shapes = 
sum of simple shapes
Trapezoid = triangle + rectangle"

📊 Approximation Methods
"Average the bases
Multiply by height
Estimate vs exact"

✅ Verification Strategies
"Multiple approaches
should yield same result
Check units and reasonableness"

🔍 Method 1: Decompose
"Split into rectangle + triangle
Rect: 8×5 = 40cm²
Triangle: ½×4×5 = 10cm²
Total: 50cm²"

🔍 Method 2: Average
"Average bases: (12+8)÷2 = 10
Multiply by height: 10×5
Result: 50cm²"

🔍 Method 3: Verify
"Use standard formula:
A = ½(b₁ + b₂)h
A = ½(12+8)×5 = 50cm²
✓ All methods agree!"

💡 Deeper Insight
"Trapezoid formula IS averaging!
½(b₁ + b₂) = average base
All area methods connect
to fundamental principles"

🌟 Transferable Knowledge
"These principles apply to:
• Any polygon decomposition
• Integration approximation
• 3D volume problems"

❌ Direct Approach Limits
"Formula memorization
No deeper understanding
Hard to verify
No transfer to new problems"

steps.title: Problem Recognition & Step-Back Decision
steps.description: Encounters specific trapezoid area problem. Instead of applying formula directly, consciously steps back to explore higher-level principles governing area calculation.

steps.title: Higher-Level Principle Identification
steps.description: Abstracts to fundamental area principles: area represents enclosed space, can be decomposed into simpler shapes, approximated through averaging, and verified through multiple methods.

steps.title: Principle-Driven Approach Generation
steps.description: From abstract principles, derives three concrete approaches: geometric decomposition (split into simple shapes), approximation method (average bases), and verification strategy (multiple methods).

steps.title: Multiple Method Application
steps.description: Applies all three principle-based methods to specific problem: decomposition (40+10=50), averaging (10×5=50), formula verification (50), showing they all yield the same result.

steps.title: Deep Understanding & Knowledge Transfer
steps.description: Synthesizes methods to reveal that trapezoid formula IS averaging, connecting all approaches. This principle-based understanding transfers to polygon decomposition, integration, and 3D problems.

name: Buffer of Thoughts(BoT)
description: Maintains a dynamic buffer of reusable thought patterns for analogical reasoning
features: Large task-dependent gains (e.g. ~11% Game of 24, ~51% Checkmate-in-One)

tldr.what: Stores reusable reasoning patterns from past problems, then retrieves and adapts analogous patterns when solving new problems.
tldr.when: Complex reasoning tasks where similar problem structures recur across domains and analogical transfer can accelerate solution discovery.
tldr.watchOut: Buffer quality degrades if patterns are too generic or domain-specific; irrelevant analogies waste compute and mislead reasoning.

overview.pattern: Thought-augmented reasoning that collects diverse approaches in a buffer, distills patterns, and creates reusable templates
overview.why: Builds reasoning expertise over time by learning from diverse thought processes and creating reusable knowledge structures
overview.insight: Generate diverse thoughts → Buffer storage → Distill patterns → Create templates → Apply to new problems

impl.d: Store thoughts in structured buffer memory
Extract key insights and patterns from buffer
Apply distilled knowledge to new problems

overview.example: Problem → Generate many thoughts → Store in buffer → Distill patterns → Create templates → Apply
dos: Encourage diverse and creative thought generation
Implement efficient buffer storage and retrieval
Focus distillation on actionable insights
Create templates that generalize across problems
Update buffer with new successful reasoning patterns
donts: Fill buffer with redundant or low-quality thoughts
Skip the distillation step (raw thoughts ≠ knowledge)
Create overly specific templates without generalization
Ignore buffer capacity limits (memory overflow)
Use stale templates without updating from experience
use: When building reasoning expertise over time
avoid: Problems with no reusable reasoning patterns

metrics.d: Variety and creativity of generated reasoning approaches
Effectiveness of pattern extraction from buffer
Success rate of applying templates to new problems
Improvement in similar problem-solving over time

usecases.d: Collect research approaches → Buffer strategies → Distill best practices → Create methodology templates
Generate solution ideas → Store in buffer → Extract patterns → Build innovation frameworks
Collect design patterns → Buffer approaches → Distill principles → Create architecture templates
Gather strategic thoughts → Buffer insights → Extract frameworks → Build planning templates
Accumulate reasoning examples → Buffer successful approaches → Distill learning patterns → Create educational templates

name: Skeleton of Thoughts(SoT)
description: Generates a skeleton outline, then expands each point in parallel to cut latency while keeping structure

tldr.what: Generates a skeletal outline of a problem's structure, then expands each branch in parallel to reduce latency while preserving logical organization.
tldr.when: Complex problems with clear hierarchical structure where you need fast answers and can parallelize expansion of independent subtopics.
tldr.watchOut: Skeleton quality determines output quality; poor initial structure forces rework or produces incoherent expansions across branches.

overview.pattern: Structured reasoning that creates a high-level skeleton then expands each component in parallel for efficient processing
overview.why: Accelerates complex response generation through parallel development while maintaining logical structure and coherence
overview.insight: Create skeleton structure → Expand points in parallel → Integrate sections → Ensure consistency → Final synthesis

impl.d: Create high-level structure with key points
Combine expanded sections into coherent whole

overview.example: Problem → [Point 1, Point 2, Point 3] → Expand each in parallel → Integrate → Final answer
dos: Create comprehensive skeleton covering all key aspects
Ensure skeleton points are logically ordered
Use parallel processing to expand multiple points
Maintain consistency across parallel expansions
Validate final integration for coherence
donts: Create skeleton without clear logical structure
Expand points sequentially when parallel is possible
Ignore contradictions between parallel sections
Skip integration step (fragmented response)
Over-decompose into trivial skeleton points
use: When parallel processing can accelerate reasoning
When consistency across sections is crucial
avoid: When parallel processing is not beneficial

metrics.d: Coverage of all essential aspects in structure
Coherence and flow of combined sections

usecases.d: Outline main arguments → Develop each argument in parallel → Integrate into coherent essay
Structure sections → Write each section independently → Combine into manual
Framework components → Analyze each component → Synthesize comprehensive assessment
Key findings outline → Elaborate each finding → Integrate into cohesive report
Plan components → Develop each strategy area → Combine into unified strategy

tldr.when: Complex problems requiring deep exploration of solution space where intermediate reasoning steps don't need human inspection or external feedback.
tldr.watchOut: Latent reasoning is opaque; you cannot inspect, debug, or steer intermediate steps if the final answer goes wrong.

name: Self-Consistency(SC)
description: Samples multiple diverse chain-of-thought paths at nonzero temperature, then aggregates their final answers by majority or confidence-weighted vote. Because a correct answer tends to be reached by many different reasoning paths while individual mistakes scatter, the consensus answer is far more reliable than any single greedy decode.
features: Samples N independent reasoning paths at nonzero temperature
Marginalizes over reasoning by voting on final answers only
Majority or confidence-weighted aggregation of candidates
Correct answers converge while sporadic errors are outvoted
Foundation of best-of-N test-time compute scaling
Universal Self-Consistency extends voting to free-form outputs

tldr.what: Samples multiple reasoning paths at nonzero temperature, then selects the final answer by majority vote or confidence weighting.
tldr.when: Problems with verifiable correct answers where diverse reasoning paths exist and errors scatter across samples.
tldr.watchOut: Requires N times more inference cost; majority vote fails if most paths converge on the same wrong answer.

flow.title: Self-Consistency
flow.description: Samples multiple diverse chain-of-thought paths at nonzero temperature and aggregates their final answers by majority vote. Correct answers recur across independent paths while errors scatter and get outvoted, giving roughly +17.9% on GSM8K over greedy chain-of-thought.

nodes.label:
🧮 Problem (GSM8K)
"Weng earns $12/hr babysitting.
Yesterday she babysat 1.5 hours.
How much did she earn?"

🎲 Diverse CoT Sampler
Decode N=5 paths at temperature 0.7

🔗 Path 1
$12 x 1.5 = $18
Answer: 18

🔗 Path 3
rounds 1.5 up to 2h
$12 x 2 = $24
Answer: 24

🔗 Path 4
$12 x 1.5 = $18
Answer: 18

📤 Answer Extractor
Parse the final answer from each path

🗳️ Majority Vote
{ 18: 4 votes, 24: 1 vote }

✨ Consensus Answer
$18 (80% agreement)

⚠️ vs Greedy Decode
A single greedy path risked the 24 error.
Majority vote adds ~+17.9% on GSM8K.

steps.title: Problem Received
steps.description: A math word problem is posed. Greedy chain-of-thought would produce a single answer and commit to it.

steps.title: Sample N Diverse Paths
steps.description: The sampler decodes 5 independent chain-of-thought paths at temperature 0.7, so each explores the arithmetic slightly differently.

steps.title: Extract Final Answers
steps.description: Only the final answer of each path is parsed out. Path 3 mistakenly rounds 1.5 hours up to 2 and reports 24; the rest report 18.

steps.title: Tally the Votes
steps.description: Answers are aggregated by majority vote: 18 receives 4 votes, 24 receives 1. This marginalizes over the reasoning and keeps only the answer distribution.

steps.title: Why Consensus Works
steps.description: Correct answers are reached by many different valid derivations and reinforce each other, while a one-off arithmetic slip appears in only a single path and is outvoted.

steps.title: Majority Vote Wins
steps.description: The consensus answer is $18 with 80% agreement, more reliable than any single decode.

steps.title: Contrast with Greedy Decode
steps.description: A lone greedy path could have landed on the 24 error. Majority-vote self-consistency adds roughly +17.9% accuracy on GSM8K and underpins best-of-N test-time scaling.

references: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models - Wang et al. (ArXiv 2022) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171
Universal Self-Consistency for Large Language Model Generation (ArXiv 2023) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17311

name: Chain of Verification (CoVe)(CoVe)
description: Reduces hallucination by drafting a baseline answer, planning a set of verification questions about it, answering each of those questions independently so the checks are not biased by the draft, and then revising the final answer using only the verified facts. Factored verification, where checks run in separate contexts, outperforms letting the model re-check its own draft, which tends to repeat its own mistakes.
features: Generates a baseline draft answer first
Plans targeted verification questions about the draft
Answers each verification question independently of the draft
Factored execution stops the draft from biasing its own checks
Revises the final answer to drop unverified claims
Cuts hallucination on list-based and closed-book factual tasks

tldr.what: Drafts an answer, generates verification questions about it, answers each question independently without seeing the draft, then revises using only verified facts.
tldr.when: Factual tasks prone to hallucination where you can decompose claims into checkable questions and tolerate moderate latency overhead.
tldr.watchOut: Verification questions inherit the draft's errors if they're poorly designed; independent answering adds 2-3x cost and latency.

flow.title: Chain of Verification (CoVe)
flow.description: Draft an answer, plan verification questions, answer each one independently so the checks are not biased by the draft, then revise. Factored verification in separate contexts exposes hallucinations the draft would otherwise confirm.

steps.title: Query Received
steps.description: A list-style factual query is posed, the kind of task where language models often hallucinate plausible but wrong entries.

steps.title: Draft a Baseline Answer
steps.description: The model answers directly. The draft looks confident but hides 2 errors: Hillary Clinton (born in Chicago) and Franklin D. Roosevelt (born in Hyde Park, not NYC).

steps.title: Plan Verification Questions
steps.description: Rather than trusting the draft, the model plans one focused verification question per entity: where was each person actually born?

steps.title: Verify Each Fact Independently
steps.description: Each question is answered in its own isolated context with the draft withheld. This factored execution is the key idea: the draft cannot bias its own checks into confirming its mistakes.

steps.title: Expose Inconsistencies
steps.description: Q1 and Q2 confirm Trump (Queens) and Theodore Roosevelt (Manhattan). Q3 and Q4 return birthplaces that contradict the draft, flagging the two hallucinations.

steps.title: Revise the Final Answer
steps.description: The model rebuilds the answer using only entries whose verification was consistent, dropping the two contradicted names.

steps.title: Verified Output
steps.description: The revised list contains only verified politicians. Factored verification removes 2 fabricated entries and outperforms letting the model re-check its own draft in one pass.

references: Chain-of-Verification Reduces Hallucination in Large Language Models - Dhuliawala et al. (ArXiv 2023) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11495
Chain-of-Verification (CoVe), Meta AI - Findings of ACL 2024

name: Proactive Clarification & Active Disambiguation(PCAD)
description: Before planning or acting on an underspecified request, the agent first decides whether to ask at all (ambiguity detection), then generates the maximally informative clarifying question (framed as expected information gain over the plausible interpretations), and only then commits to a plan. Off-the-shelf LLMs recognize ambiguity when explicitly asked yet overwhelmingly default to a silent single-guess answer, so asking is an explicit trained or prompted behavior. Distinct from mixed-initiative-interface-patterns, which is about UI control-switching, and from human-in-the-loop, which approves an already-chosen action rather than disambiguating intent.
features: Ambiguity detector decides whether a question is even needed
Selects the question with the highest expected information gain
One well-chosen question can split many interpretations at once
Answers directly when the request is already unambiguous
Prevents silent single-interpretation failures on vague inputs
Explicit behavior since models recognize but rarely surface ambiguity

tldr.what: Agent detects ambiguity in a request, then asks one high-information question before acting, rather than silently guessing a single interpretation.
tldr.when: Requests are underspecified or vague, actions are costly or hard to reverse, and clarification can eliminate many wrong paths at once.
tldr.watchOut: Users may perceive repeated clarification as inefficient; balance asking against over-interrogation on genuinely obvious requests.

flow.title: Proactive Clarification & Active Disambiguation
flow.description: Faced with an underspecified booking request, the agent first detects the ambiguity, decides that a costly action warrants asking, selects the single question with the highest expected information gain, and only then commits, avoiding the silent wrong guess a default LLM would make.

nodes.label:
🎯 Request
"Book me a flight to Springfield"

🤖 Agent
Proactive planner

🔍 Ambiguity Detector
How many valid interpretations?

💰 Action Cost Check
Booking is costly and hard to reverse

🗺️ Interpretations
5 Springfields with airports:
SPI IL, SGF MO, BDL MA, EUG OR, DAY OH

❓ Decide to Ask
Many interpretations + costly action -> ASK

⚠️ Silent Guess (default LLM)
Assume most populous -> SPI (IL)

🧮 Question Selector
Maximize expected information gain

❌ Wrong City
Booked SPI, costly reversal

💤 "Which Springfield?"
open, little structure

💤 "Did you mean IL?"
rules out only 1 of 5

✅ "IL, MO, MA, OR, or OH?"
partitions all 5 at once

💬 User answers
"MO"

📌 Commit Plan
Book Springfield-Branson (SGF)

✨ Correct Booking
SGF, right on the first try

steps.title: Ambiguous Request
steps.description: The user asks to book a flight to Springfield, a name shared by many US towns.

steps.title: Detect Ambiguity and Enumerate
steps.description: The ambiguity detector finds that five Springfields have commercial airports, so the request has multiple valid interpretations.

steps.title: Assess Cost and Decide to Ask
steps.description: Because booking is costly and hard to reverse and the interpretations are many, the agent decides to ask rather than guess.

steps.title: Select the Best Question
steps.description: The question selector compares candidates by expected information gain: open or single-city questions gain little, while one question over all five cities partitions them at once.

steps.title: Ask and Get the Answer
steps.description: The agent asks the single maximally informative question and the user replies "MO".

steps.title: Commit to the Correct Plan
steps.description: With intent disambiguated, the agent books Springfield-Branson (SGF), correct on the first try.

steps.title: Contrast: Silent Guess Fails
steps.description: A default LLM skips clarification, assumes the most populous match, books Springfield IL (SPI), and lands on the wrong city and a costly reversal.

references: Ask-before-Plan: Proactive Language Agents for Real-World Planning - Zhang et al. (ArXiv 2024) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.12639
Modeling Future Conversation Turns to Teach LLMs to Ask Clarifying Questions - Zhang et al. (ICLR 2025) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13788
Knowing but Not Showing: LLMs Recognize Ambiguity but Rarely Ask Clarifying Questions - Su & Cardie (ArXiv 2026) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25284
InteractComp: Evaluating Search Agents With Ambiguous Queries (ArXiv 2025) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24668

name: Layered Defense Pattern(LDP)
description: Multi-layered security architecture implementing the Swiss Cheese Model for AI safety
features: External API-level constraints and rate limiting
Secondary input/output validation and content filtering
Internal model-level safety mechanisms and alignment

tldr.what: Stacks independent safety checks across API, application, and model layers so no single failure exposes the system.
tldr.when: High-stakes domains like finance or healthcare where one compromised defense cannot bypass all protections.
tldr.watchOut: Each layer adds latency and operational overhead; misaligned rules across layers create false security feelings while actual gaps remain.

overview.pattern: Multiple independent security layers (External → Application → Model) creating defense-in-depth
overview.why: Single layer failures don't compromise system; each layer catches different threat types
overview.insight: Swiss Cheese Model - holes in different layers don't align, preventing complete breach

impl.d: API gateway with rate limiting & auth

dos: Implement fail-safe defaults at each layer
Use defense-in-depth with independent failure modes
Log security events for audit and improvement
Test layers both independently and integrated
Document what each layer protects against
donts: Rely on a single layer for critical security
Create overlapping rules that conflict
Skip monitoring of bypass attempts
Ignore performance impact of multiple layers
Forget to update all layers when threats evolve

usecases.d: External (DDoS) → App (fraud detection) → Model (compliance)
External (HIPAA auth) → App (PHI filtering) → Model (medical safety)
External (client auth) → App (privilege checks) → Model (ethical bounds)
External (employee verification) → App (PII protection) → Model (bias prevention)
External (age verification) → App (content filtering) → Model (safety guidelines)

flow.title: Layered Defense Pattern

steps.title: Swiss Cheese Model Foundation
steps.description: Swiss Cheese Model demonstrates that each defense layer has vulnerabilities, but multiple independent layers prevent harm by making simultaneous failure extremely unlikely.

steps.title: Layered Defense Architecture
steps.description: Five independent defense layers create multiplicative protection: Layer 1 blocks 90%, Layer 2 blocks 80% of remainder, creating exponentially decreasing threat probability through each layer.

steps.title: Vulnerability Bypass Progression
steps.description: Threats that bypass each layer face exponentially decreasing success rates: 10% → 2% → 0.2% → 0.03% → 0.006%, demonstrating how layered defenses compound effectiveness.

steps.title: Defense Success Statistics
steps.description: Vast majority of threats (99.994%) are successfully blocked across all layers, with most stopped at early layers. Only 0.006% extremely rare cases escape all defenses simultaneously.

steps.title: Continuous Defense Evolution
steps.description: System learns from both rare failures and successful blocks to strengthen weak layers, patch discovered vulnerabilities, and add new defense mechanisms, further reducing escape probability.

name: Contextual Guardrailing Pattern(CGP)
description: Dynamic rule enforcement based on context, data flow requirements, and conditional patterns
features: Dynamic rule adaptation based on context

tldr.what: Enforces different access rules and data-handling constraints based on detected context like user role, data sensitivity, time, and location.
tldr.when: Systems handling regulated data where restrictions must tighten or loosen based on who accesses what, when, and from where.
tldr.watchOut: Context detection errors cascade into wrong rule enforcement; false negatives expose data, false positives block legitimate work.

overview.pattern: Dynamic guardrails that adapt based on context (user, role, data, time, location)
overview.why: Static rules fail in complex environments; context-aware security enables precise control
overview.insight: IF-THIS-THEN-THAT logic creates adaptive security without sacrificing usability

impl.d: Analyze user, role, location, time, data

dos: Start simple and add complexity based on actual patterns
Design rules to be explainable and auditable
Use versioning for safe rule updates and rollbacks
Implement comprehensive context detection across dimensions
Cache context decisions for performance optimization
donts: Create overly complex rules that are hard to debug
Apply same rules uniformly across all contexts
Skip audit logging for context-based decisions
Ignore performance impact of rule evaluation
Forget to test edge cases and rule interactions

usecases.d: PHI access (role + location + time) → HIPAA-compliant restrictions
Trading operations (user level + time + amount) → approval workflows
Remote access (location + device + sensitivity) → tool restrictions
Student data (role + purpose + consent) → privacy guardrails
Classified systems (clearance + need-to-know + location) → access control

flow.title: Contextual Guardrailing Pattern
flow.description: Dynamic rule enforcement that adapts guardrails based on context, data flow requirements, and conditional patterns rather than applying static universal rules

steps.title: Ambiguous Query Challenge

steps.title: Two Approaches: Static vs Contextual
steps.description: Query splits into two processing paths: static keyword blocking (left) vs dynamic context analysis (right), showing fundamental difference in approaches.

steps.title: Static Approach Limitations
steps.description: Static guardrail blocks ALL queries containing 'treat badly' keywords without context analysis, causing false positives and blocking legitimate requests.

steps.title: Contextual Intent Detection
steps.description: Context analysis intelligently identifies three possible intents: medical emergency (help needed), academic research (education wanted), or harmful intent (prevent harm).

steps.title: Context-Appropriate Responses
steps.description: Each detected intent triggers appropriate response: emergency medical help, educational content, or harm prevention with redirection - same keywords, different outcomes.

steps.title: Core Insight: Context > Keywords
steps.description: Key learning: contextual guardrailing enables nuanced AI safety by understanding intent behind words, not just blocking keywords. Same words ≠ same intent.

references: Invariant Labs (2024)
OWASP ASI (2025)

name: GuardAgent Pattern(GAP)
description: Dedicated guardrail agent monitoring and protecting target agents through dynamic safety checks
features: Guardrail accuracy measured on your own red-team set

tldr.what: Separate agent monitors target agent's actions against safety rules, blocking violations before execution.
tldr.when: High-stakes domains like trading, healthcare, or finance where unsafe actions cause real harm.
tldr.watchOut: Guard agent itself becomes a bottleneck or single point of failure if its rules are incomplete or misconfigured.

overview.pattern: Dedicated guard agent monitors target agents through dynamic safety check generation
overview.why: Self-monitoring fails; external validation with deterministic code ensures 98%+ accuracy
overview.insight: Safety requirements → Task plan → Executable code → Real-time enforcement

impl.d: Create task plan from safety requirements
Convert plan into executable guardrail code
Run code to validate agent actions

dos: Use dedicated monitoring agents separate from target agents
Generate deterministic code for consistent enforcement
Implement comprehensive action logging and audit trails
Define clear safety requirements in natural language
Test guardrails independently before deployment
donts: Let target agents self-monitor without external validation
Rely on probabilistic checks for critical safety
Skip validation of generated guardrail code
Allow guardrail bypass for "trusted" operations
Ignore performance impact on target agent latency

usecases.d: Monitor trades for limits, restricted securities, risk thresholds
Validate medical recommendations against safety protocols & regulations
Ensure robots/vehicles operate within physical & ethical bounds
Block harmful, biased, or policy-violating outputs in real-time
Prevent unauthorized access, ensure privacy compliance in pipelines

name: Intrinsic Alignment Pattern(IAP)
description: Internal observation points that cannot be manipulated by the agent, preventing deep scheming

tldr.what: Embeds unmanipulable observation points inside an agent's processing to detect misalignment, deception, or goal drift that external monitoring cannot catch.
tldr.when: High-stakes deployments where an agent could benefit from hiding its true reasoning or goals, and you need detection beyond what output analysis reveals.
tldr.watchOut: Requires deep access to model internals; most deployed systems lack the transparency needed to implement this reliably.

overview.pattern: Internal observation points that cannot be manipulated by the agent to detect deep scheming
overview.why: External monitoring misses deceptive alignment; intrinsic monitors catch hidden objectives
overview.insight: Tamper-proof internal hooks + behavioral invariants = early misalignment detection

impl.d: Place tamper-proof hooks in model layers

dos: Use cryptographic signing for monitor integrity
Monitor hidden layer activations, not just outputs
Track consistency between stated and actual objectives
Establish behavioral baselines during safe deployment
Design monitors the agent cannot detect or manipulate
donts: Rely solely on external output monitoring
Allow agents to access monitoring mechanisms
Ignore subtle behavioral shifts over time
Trust self-reported alignment status
Skip monitoring during "routine" operations

usecases.d: Monitoring advanced systems for deceptive alignment or goal drift
Detecting hidden trading objectives or market manipulation attempts
Ensuring AI weapons systems maintain strict ethical constraints
Preventing capability concealment during safety evaluations
Monitoring for unauthorized data exfiltration or competitive sabotage

name: Memory Poisoning Prevention Pattern(MPP)
description: Protects agent memory systems from malicious manipulation and gradual corruption

tldr.what: Validates memory updates with cryptographic signing, detects anomalies, and rolls back corrupted state to prevent malicious manipulation of agent knowledge.
tldr.when: Agents store user data or learned patterns that attackers could poison to change behavior, decisions, or outputs over time.
tldr.watchOut: Overhead from constant validation and rollback mechanisms can slow response time significantly under high-volume or real-time constraints.

overview.pattern: Protects agent memory from malicious manipulation through validation, signing, and integrity checks
overview.why: Poisoned memories lead to gradual behavior corruption; prevention ensures long-term reliability
overview.insight: Cryptographic signing + anomaly detection + regular sanitization = tamper-resistant memory
dos: Implement cryptographic signing for all memory updates
Use Merkle trees for efficient integrity verification
Maintain immutable audit logs of memory operations
Perform regular memory consolidation and pruning
Create differential backups for rollback capability
donts: Allow direct memory writes without validation
Trust memory content without verification
Skip anomaly detection for "trusted" sources
Store sensitive data without encryption
Ignore contradictory or conflicting entries

usecases.d: Prevent preference manipulation & false history injection
Protect user data from adversarial memory corruption
Ensure business knowledge base integrity across sessions
Maintain accurate learning progress without tampering
Protect patient interaction history from malicious updates

steps.title: Multi-Layer Validation Process

name: Tool Misuse Prevention Pattern(TMP)
description: Prevents agents from being manipulated into executing malicious actions through tools

tldr.what: Restricts agent tool access through permission boundaries, action validation, sandboxing, audit logs, and rate limits before execution.
tldr.when: Agents control sensitive systems like databases, file systems, shell commands, or external APIs where misuse causes real damage.
tldr.watchOut: Overly restrictive rules block legitimate work; overly permissive ones fail to stop determined prompt injection attacks.

overview.pattern: Prevents agents from executing malicious actions through strict tool access control & sandboxing
overview.why: Unrestricted tool access enables system compromise; boundaries ensure safe automation
overview.insight: Whitelist + validation + sandbox + monitoring = secure tool execution

impl.d: Isolate tool runs in secure environment
Log all tool calls with full context

dos: Use capability-based access control for tools
Implement strict parameter validation and sanitization
Run tools in sandboxed environments with resource limits
Maintain comprehensive audit logs with context
Use rate limiting per tool type and user
donts: Allow unrestricted command execution
Trust tool parameters without validation
Skip sandboxing for "safe" tools
Ignore resource consumption patterns
Grant blanket permissions to trusted agents

usecases.d: Prevent rm -rf, sudo, chmod on critical systems
Block unauthorized database queries & data exfiltration
Restrict access to sensitive directories & file types
Prevent calls to unauthorized endpoints or services
Control robot/IoT device commands within safety bounds

steps.title: Key Protection Principle

name: Privilege Compromise Mitigation Pattern(PCM)
description: Prevents privilege escalation and unauthorized operations through strict access control

tldr.what: Enforces role-based access control with identity separation, least privilege defaults, and continuous monitoring of agent operations against user clearance levels.
tldr.when: Multi-user systems where agents access sensitive data, perform financial transactions, or operate across departments with different authorization requirements.
tldr.watchOut: Overly granular privilege rules create bottlenecks; agents fail silently or repeatedly prompt users, degrading usability faster than security improves.

overview.pattern: Prevents privilege escalation through RBAC, identity separation, and dynamic de-escalation
overview.why: Agent privilege inheritance enables lateral movement; strict boundaries prevent compromise
overview.insight: Separate identity + least privilege + time limits + zero trust = secure operations
dos: Implement strict identity separation between agents and users
Use time-based privilege expiration and renewal
Apply context-aware permission boundaries
Monitor privilege usage patterns for anomalies
Require multi-factor approval for high-value operations
donts: Let agents inherit full user privileges automatically

tldr.when: Multi-agent systems where agents have different permissions, external access, or handle sensitive data that could be compromised through agent-to-agent exploitation.

overview.pattern: Orchestrates multiple specialized security agents for comprehensive threat detection
overview.why: Single agents have blind spots; coordinated ensemble provides defense-in-depth
overview.insight: Specialized roles + Byzantine consensus + reputation weighting = robust security

impl.d: Set specialized security roles per agent

dos: Implement Byzantine fault tolerance for agent consensus
Use specialized security agents for different threat types
Apply reputation scoring to weight agent contributions
Maintain audit trails across all agent interactions
Design for graceful degradation if agents fail
donts: Trust single agent decisions for critical operations
Allow unrestricted agent communication
Skip consensus verification in emergencies
Ignore agent collusion possibilities
Deploy without kill switch capabilities

usecases.d: Multiple agents validate trades before execution

Diverse agents check for different policy violations

overview.pattern: Protects system prompts from extraction through encoding, filtering, and monitoring

name: Differential Privacy Patterns(DPP)
description: Privacy-preserving data processing with mathematical privacy guarantees

tldr.what: Adds calibrated noise to query results so changing any single record minimally affects output, with formal privacy guarantees measured by epsilon.
tldr.when: Aggregating sensitive data where you must prove no individual's presence or absence can be reliably inferred from results.
tldr.watchOut: Smaller epsilon (stronger privacy) drastically reduces result accuracy; tuning requires deep statistical expertise and domain knowledge of acceptable utility loss.

overview.pattern: Privacy-preserving data processing with mathematical privacy guarantees through controlled noise injection
overview.why: Provides formal privacy guarantees, enables safe data sharing, supports regulatory compliance, and maintains statistical utility
overview.insight: Calibrated noise + sensitivity bounds + privacy budget → mathematically guaranteed privacy
dos: Set appropriate epsilon values for privacy requirements
Use proven noise mechanisms (Laplace, Gaussian, Exponential)
Track privacy budget expenditure across all queries
Apply post-processing invariance for utility improvements
Validate statistical utility after noise injection
donts: Use the same noise instance across multiple queries
Exceed privacy budget without proper composition
Ignore sensitivity bounds for unbounded queries
Apply differential privacy to already aggregated data
Skip formal privacy analysis for custom mechanisms

usecases.d: Patient record analysis with HIPAA compliance and privacy guarantees
Population statistics publication with individual privacy protection
Transaction pattern analysis without customer identification
Student performance studies with privacy preservation
Aggregate mobility insights without individual tracking

name: Zero-Trust Agent Architecture(ZTAA)

tldr.what: Verifies agent identity and permissions at every access point, enforcing least privilege and adapting policies based on real-time threat signals.
tldr.when: Multi-agent systems handling sensitive data where compromise of one agent must not cascade, or regulated environments requiring audit trails.
tldr.watchOut: Verification overhead can severely degrade latency; misconfigured policies lock out legitimate agents or create false security theater.

overview.pattern: Never trust, always verify approach for agent security with continuous verification and least privilege access
overview.why: Eliminates implicit trust, reduces attack surface, enables secure distributed deployments, and improves threat detection
overview.insight: Continuous verification + microsegmentation + least privilege + dynamic policies → secure agent ecosystem
dos: Verify every agent request regardless of source
Implement microsegmentation for agent isolation
Apply least privilege principle to all agent access
Monitor agent behavior continuously for anomalies
Use encrypted communication for all agent interactions
donts: Trust agents based on network location alone
Grant broad access permissions by default
Skip re-authentication for sensitive operations
Ignore behavioral anomalies in trusted agents
Use static security policies across all contexts

name: Secure Multi-Party Computation(SMPC)

tldr.when: Competing organizations need to collaborate on analysis (fraud detection, risk assessment) while keeping sensitive data completely private.

overview.pattern: Privacy-preserving collaboration between multiple agents without revealing private data through cryptographic protocols
overview.why: Enables secure data collaboration, maintains competitive advantages, ensures regulatory compliance, and builds trust
overview.insight: Secret sharing + homomorphic computation + cryptographic proofs → secure multi-party analysis
dos: Use proven cryptographic protocols (Shamir, BGW, GMW)
Implement secure channels for all party communications
Verify computational integrity with cryptographic proofs
Plan for party dropout and recovery mechanisms
Use threshold schemes to prevent single points of failure
donts: Trust parties to follow protocols without verification
Ignore performance implications of cryptographic overhead
Use insecure random number generation for secrets
Skip security analysis for custom protocol modifications
Assume all parties have equal computational resources

usecases.d: Joint fraud detection without sharing customer data
Multi-hospital studies preserving patient privacy
Collaborative analytics without revealing trade secrets
Privacy-preserving audience measurement and attribution

name: Data Anonymization Patterns(DAP)
description: Comprehensive data anonymization techniques including K-anonymity, L-diversity, T-closeness, and synthetic data generation for agentic systems

tldr.what: Removes or transforms personally identifiable data so individuals cannot be re-identified, using techniques like generalization, suppression, and synthetic data generation.
tldr.when: Sharing datasets across organizations or agents where privacy regulations apply and you need to prevent linking records back to individuals.
tldr.watchOut: Aggressive anonymization severely degrades data utility; attackers can still re-identify through auxiliary information or linkage attacks.

overview.pattern: Comprehensive data anonymization techniques including K-anonymity, L-diversity, T-closeness, and synthetic data generation for agentic systems
overview.why: Protects individual privacy, enables safe data sharing, supports federated learning, and ensures regulatory compliance
overview.insight: Multi-layered anonymization + synthetic generation + federated processing → privacy-preserving agent collaboration
dos: Implement k-anonymity with minimum k=5 for basic protection
Use synthetic data generation for high-risk PII scenarios
Apply federated anonymization for multi-agent environments
Combine multiple techniques (L-diversity + T-closeness)
Regular re-identification risk assessment and testing
donts: Rely solely on data masking without anonymization models
Use simple generalization that destroys data utility
Ignore quasi-identifier combinations for re-identification
Apply anonymization after data has been widely distributed
Skip validation of synthetic data statistical properties

usecases.d: Patient record anonymization for multi-hospital federated learning

Package AI agents in trusted execution environment

dos: Use hardware-based TEEs for maximum security guarantees
Implement remote attestation for enclave verification
Choose appropriate framework based on performance requirements
Encrypt all data in transit between enclaves
Monitor enclave resource usage and side-channel attacks
donts: Trust enclaves without proper attestation verification
Store secrets in non-encrypted enclave memory
Ignore performance overhead of confidential computing
Use deprecated Intel SGX for new deployments
Skip security updates for TEE frameworks

impl.d: Deploy browser-based vault for device-level secrets
Configure server vault with dynamic secrets
Connect cloud key management for master keys
Implement local and distributed encrypted cache layers
Automate TTL management and credential rotation

dos: Use zero-knowledge encryption for local device vaults
Implement dynamic secret generation with short TTLs
Encrypt cache data both at rest and in transit
Use hardware-backed key storage (HSM/TEE) when available
Implement comprehensive audit trails for all secret access
donts: Store long-lived secrets in local caches without encryption
Use the same encryption key across multiple cache regions
Skip secret rotation for convenience
Allow cache data to persist beyond TTL expiration
Mix secrets and cache data in the same storage tier

metrics.d: % of secrets rotated without service disruption
% of secret operations logged with correlation

Apply differential privacy noise before any data transmission
