steps.title: Fat Tool Results Accumulate
steps.description: Search hits, fetched pages, and file reads each return large re-fetchable payloads (16k to 23k tokens) that pile up turn after turn.

steps.title: Context Window Fills
steps.description: The raw tool_result blocks push the live window to 94k of a 100k budget. Left unchecked, this path leads to overflow and context rot.

steps.title: Threshold Triggers Context Editing
steps.description: The harness watches input tokens and, at the 94k trigger, fires clear_tool_uses_20250919 instead of letting the window overflow like the no-clearing baseline.

steps.title: Editor Runs With No Model Call
steps.description: The context editor is a harness/API primitive, not a summarization pass, so the eviction costs zero inference tokens.

steps.title: Placeholders Replace Payloads, tool_use Kept
steps.description: The oldest tool_result payloads become ~40-token placeholders while the matching tool_use records stay in place, so context drops from 94k to about 15k and the KV-cache prefix stays warm.

steps.title: Re-fetch On Demand, Loop Continues
steps.description: When a later turn needs a cleared page, the agent simply re-runs the tool and re-injects it. Nothing was lost, so the loop pushes past turn 100 without rot.

steps.title: Task Completes Without Context Rot
steps.description: Reported on a 100-turn web-search evaluation: roughly 84% token reduction and a 29-39% performance lift over keeping every raw result.

name: Human-in-the-Loop(HITL)
description: Strategic integration of human judgment at critical decision points in AI workflows

tldr.what: Pauses AI execution at critical points to route decisions to humans, typically when confidence falls below a threshold or domain expertise is required.
tldr.when: High-stakes decisions where errors are costly, ambiguous cases need expert judgment, or regulatory compliance requires human sign-off.
tldr.watchOut: Humans become bottlenecks; escalation queues grow faster than review capacity, causing delays or reviewers rushing through decisions.

overview.pattern: Strategic integration of human judgment at critical decision points in AI workflows with active participation
overview.why: Combines AI efficiency with human expertise for complex decisions, ensuring safety and quality in high-stakes scenarios
overview.insight: Humans actively participate in decision-making process, providing continuous feedback that improves AI performance

impl.d: Channel complex cases to domain experts
Update AI models from human expertise

dos: Set clear confidence thresholds for human escalation
Design intuitive interfaces for human decision-makers
Capture reasoning behind human decisions for learning
Route decisions to appropriate domain experts
Implement active learning from human feedback
donts: Escalate every decision to humans (automation defeats purpose)
Ignore human feedback in model improvement cycles
Overload humans with too many simultaneous decisions
Skip validation of human decision quality
Use HITL where HOTL supervision would suffice

metrics.d: Percentage of decisions requiring human input
Accuracy and consistency of human choices
Time from escalation to human decision
Total cost including human expert time

usecases.d: AI screens routine cases, escalates complex symptoms to doctors with 95% accuracy improvement
AI processes standard contracts, routes complex clauses to lawyers reducing review time by 60%
AI handles clear violations, escalates nuanced cases to human moderators with 98% policy compliance
AI flags suspicious transactions, routes complex patterns to analysts with 40% false positive reduction
AI handles normal driving, immediately transfers control to human drivers in emergency situations

name: Human On the Loop(HOTL)
description: Human supervisory oversight of autonomous AI systems with ability to monitor, intervene, or take control when necessary

tldr.what: AI system operates autonomously while humans monitor dashboards and intervene only when exceptions trigger alerts or manual override is needed.
tldr.when: High-stakes domains where autonomous speed matters but rare failure modes pose unacceptable risk, and humans can realistically respond in time.
tldr.watchOut: Humans often miss alerts or fail to intervene decisively during fast-moving crises, especially after long periods of uneventful monitoring.

overview.pattern: Human supervisory oversight of autonomous AI systems with monitoring and intervention capabilities
overview.why: Enables high-speed autonomous operation while maintaining human control and safety oversight for edge cases
overview.insight: Humans supervise rather than participate, intervening only when AI encounters exceptional situations

impl.d: Enable smooth return to autonomous operation

dos: Design comprehensive real-time monitoring dashboards
Set clear operational boundaries and risk parameters
Implement fast, intuitive override mechanisms
Provide contextual information for human decisions
Test emergency takeover procedures regularly
donts: Overwhelm operators with too many alerts
Design overly complex intervention interfaces
Allow autonomous operation without clear boundaries
Skip training operators on override procedures
Ignore human workload and attention limitations
use: Reliable AI with occasional edge cases
avoid: Legal requirements for active human approval

metrics.d: Percentage of time running without intervention

name: Progressive Disclosure UI Patterns(PDP)
description: Interface patterns for gradually revealing agent capabilities, reasoning, and complex information to prevent cognitive overload
features: Expandable reasoning trees with step-by-step disclosure

tldr.what: Reveals agent reasoning, capabilities, and explanations through expandable sections and detail levels, letting users control information depth.
tldr.when: Complex agent outputs need explanation but full details overwhelm users, or capabilities should be introduced gradually during onboarding.
tldr.watchOut: Users may miss critical information if they never expand sections, or feel frustrated by excessive clicking to reach needed details.

overview.pattern: Gradually reveal information layers to prevent cognitive overload
overview.why: Users need complex AI reasoning but get overwhelmed by technical details upfront
overview.insight: Start simple, expand on-demand: summary → detailed → technical with clear visual hierarchy

impl.d: Show relevant depth based on user type

dos: Start with essential information only
Use consistent expand/collapse icons across UI
Implement smooth animations for transitions
Remember user disclosure preferences
Provide "expand all" / "collapse all" options
donts: Show all complex information at once
Use misleading or unclear labels for disclosure
Nest disclosure levels too deeply (max 3-4)
Hide critical information behind multiple clicks
Ignore keyboard navigation for disclosure controls

metrics.d: Preference for progressive vs full disclosure

usecases.d: Show summary → detailed steps → technical reasoning trace
Basic features → advanced tools → expert features
What happened → why it occurred → how to fix it
Final recommendation → factors considered → detailed analysis
Core concepts → intermediate features → advanced workflows

name: Confidence Visualization UI Patterns(CVP)
description: Visual interface elements for displaying AI confidence levels, uncertainty, and prediction reliability in user-friendly formats
features: Confidence meters with color-coded reliability indicators
Visual risk assessment and reliability scores

tldr.what: Displays AI confidence scores, uncertainty ranges, and alternative predictions through color-coded meters, ranges, badges, or probability visualizations.
tldr.when: Users need to judge whether to trust a prediction before acting on it, especially in high-stakes decisions or unfamiliar domains.
tldr.watchOut: A model score or an LLM self-rating is not a verified probability of correctness. Check calibration on labeled evaluation data before presenting it as one.

overview.pattern: Display AI model confidence to help users make informed decisions
overview.why: Users need evidence about reliability and a clear way to review uncertain predictions
overview.insight: Label score provenance, test calibration, and connect uncertainty to a useful next action

impl.d: Fit calibration on held-out labels and evaluate on separate data
Combine text labels and icons with color
State the task and evaluation data behind each score
Set review thresholds using error costs and review capacity
Explain that a high score can still be wrong

overview.example: Illustrative policy: higher score → suggestion; low score or close alternatives → human review. Validate cutoffs on your task.
dos: Use consistent color schemes for confidence levels
Explain what factors influence confidence scores
Fit calibration on held-out labels and evaluate on separate data
Show uncertainty ranges not just point estimates
Include confidence in voice/conversational interfaces
donts: Show false precision (99.73% vs ~very high)
Treat a model score or an LLM self-rating as a verified probability
Use confidence as the only decision factor
Overwhelm users with technical probability details
Make low confidence visually alarming for normal uncertainty
use: User needs to understand AI limitations
avoid: No evidence that the displayed score predicts correctness

metrics.d: Human decisions contrary to AI confidence

usecases.d: Show diagnostic confidence with supporting evidence strength
Display prediction confidence with market uncertainty factors
Indicate detection confidence for borderline content
Show confidence in meaning preservation and accuracy
Rank with relevance confidence and source reliability

name: Mixed-Initiative Interface Patterns(MIP)
description: UI patterns for seamless control switching between human and AI agents, enabling collaborative initiative-taking
features: Control handoff buttons with clear state indicators
Initiative indicators showing who is currently leading
Seamless transition interfaces for control switching

tldr.what: Displays who controls the interaction at each moment, with buttons to switch control between human and AI, plus a history of handoffs.
tldr.when: Collaborative work where both human judgment and AI capability matter, and control must shift based on task phase or user preference.
tldr.watchOut: Users often miss or ignore state indicators, then lose track of who is actually in control and become confused or frustrated.

overview.pattern: Dynamic control-sharing between humans and AI based on task context
overview.why: Neither full automation nor manual control alone maximizes human-AI collaborative potential
overview.insight: Design flexible handoffs: AI proposes → Human decides → Either can take initiative as needed

impl.d: Clarify when AI leads vs when human leads interaction
Smooth transitions between AI and human initiative
Easy ways for humans to take control anytime
Show who is currently driving the interaction
Visual hints for when to collaborate vs lead

overview.example: AI suggests → Human reviews → Human modifies → AI adapts → Joint execution
dos: Make it clear who has control at any moment
Provide immediate override/takeover options
Show AI suggestions as starting points, not final answers
Enable seamless handoffs between AI and human control
Design for varying levels of human engagement
donts: Force users into rigid interaction patterns
Make AI takeover feel sudden or unexpected
Hide how to regain control from AI automation
Assume users want the same level of AI involvement
Make collaboration feel like competing for control
use: Tasks requiring human judgment and AI efficiency

metrics.d: % time human vs AI leads interaction
Time saved vs full manual work

usecases.d: AI drafts → Human edits → AI suggests improvements → Human finalizes
Human defines question → AI explores data → Human interprets → AI visualizes
AI suggests implementations → Human reviews → Human customizes → AI optimizes
AI gathers sources → Human evaluates → AI synthesizes → Human validates
Human sets direction → AI generates options → Human selects → AI refines

description: Interface elements showing real-time agent activities, thinking states, and operational status for user awareness

tldr.what: Displays real-time agent activities, thinking states, and operational health through animated indicators, progress bars, and status badges.
tldr.when: Long-running agent tasks where users need visibility into what the agent is doing and confidence it hasn't stalled.
tldr.watchOut: Overly detailed or frequent UI updates can distract users or create false urgency without improving actual task outcomes.

overview.pattern: Real-time visual indicators showing agent activities and operational status
overview.why: Users need transparency about agent progress to build trust and know when intervention is needed
overview.insight: Show not just that agent is working, but specifically what it's doing and how long it might take

impl.d: Define thinking, processing, waiting, completed states
Animated icons, progress bars, and status badges
WebSocket or polling for live status changes
Show percentages only when total work is known; otherwise show the current stage

dos: Show meaningful state changes promptly without rapid flicker
Use consistent icons and animations across all states
Provide meaningful descriptions of current activities
Display progress bars for long-running tasks
Include estimated completion times when possible
donts: Use generic "loading" states without context
Show rapid status flickering or jumpy animations
Hide critical error states from the user
Leave users guessing what the agent is doing
Overwhelm with too many simultaneous status indicators

metrics.d: Time between state change and UI update
Success rate of handling failed states

usecases.d: Show parsing → analysis → summarization → completion stages
Display loading → processing → calculating → visualizing status
Indicate querying → filtering → ranking → presenting results
Monitor email sync, backup, or cleanup operations
Track status of multiple agents working in parallel

Force single-turn interactions for complex tasks

Ignore accessibility and diverse user communication needs

tldr.watchOut: Overly detailed dashboards confuse users; keep visibility focused on decisions and blockers, not every internal agent state change.

overview.pattern: Multi-agent coordination interfaces with seamless handoffs, transparent orchestration, and specialized agent collaboration
overview.why: Enables complex enterprise workflows, reduces coordination overhead, and provides scalable automation with human oversight integration

name: Trust and Transparency Patterns(TTP)
description: Design patterns for building user trust through explainable AI interfaces, decision transparency, and source attribution
features: Explainable AI interfaces with progressive disclosure

tldr.what: Surfaces AI reasoning, data sources, and confidence levels through expandable explanations, visual indicators, and decision breakdowns users can inspect.
tldr.when: High-stakes decisions, regulated domains, or when users need to verify AI output before acting on recommendations or generated content.
tldr.watchOut: Over-explaining creates cognitive overload; users ignore detailed transparency if it's too dense or always visible by default.

overview.pattern: Explainable AI interfaces with decision transparency, source attribution, and trust-building patterns for responsible AI deployment
overview.why: Builds user trust, meets regulatory requirements, enables informed decision-making, and ensures accountability in AI systems
overview.insight: Three-level transparency framework (what/how/why) with progressive disclosure - trust through understanding rather than blind faith

impl.d: Implement three-level transparency: what/how/why with algorithmic, interaction, and social layers
Create progressive disclosure interfaces with feature importance and counterfactual explanations
Implement confidence visualization, source attribution, and AI-generated content markers
Design decision trees, reasoning paths, and interactive exploration interfaces
Build structured documentation with multi-stakeholder information architecture

dos: Use clear visual indicators (like Einstein sparkles) to show AI-generated content
Implement three levels of transparency: what happened, how decisions were made, why they matter
Provide progressive disclosure with expandable explanation panels
Include source attribution and citations for all AI recommendations
Design for different stakeholder needs: technical, legal, and user-friendly explanations
Implement mindful friction for high-stakes decisions with confirmation dialogs
Use counterfactual explanations to show "what if" scenarios
Create interactive model cards with layered information architecture
donts: Hide uncertainty or present AI decisions as infallible
Use technical jargon without providing accessible explanations
Overwhelm users with too much technical detail upfront
Implement transparency without considering user cognitive load
Skip bias detection warnings and toxicity safeguards
Provide explanations without actionable information for users
use: Regulated industries requiring audit trails and accountability
Enterprise systems needing explainable business intelligence
Customer-facing AI where trust is critical for adoption
Multi-stakeholder environments with diverse transparency needs
AI systems making consequential automated decisions
Applications where users need to understand and verify AI reasoning
avoid: Simple, low-risk applications where transparency adds unnecessary complexity
Performance-critical systems where explanation overhead is prohibitive
Internal tools where users have high AI literacy and trust
Applications with clear, deterministic rule-based logic
Systems where IP protection conflicts with transparency requirements

metrics.d: Alignment between user trust levels and actual AI reliability
% of users who correctly understand AI reasoning explanations
Increase in user confidence when making AI-assisted decisions
% of users who actively explore explanation features
User ability to identify when AI makes mistakes
Percentage of regulatory transparency requirements met
Mental effort required to understand AI explanations

usecases.d: Diagnostic reasoning → clinical evidence display → physician review integration → patient explanation
Risk assessment visualization → regulatory compliance display → decision audit trails → customer transparency
Case analysis reasoning → precedent citation → confidence intervals → attorney decision support
Data analysis explanation → source attribution → decision factors → stakeholder reporting
Policy violation detection → reasoning display → appeal process → transparency reports
Candidate evaluation factors → bias detection alerts → decision justification → compliance documentation
Decision tree visualization → sensor data display → confidence metrics → human oversight integration

Use sensitive data without explicit consent
Hide adaptation logic completely from users
Assume adaptation preferences transfer between contexts
Sacrifice core functionality for adaptive features
use: Users have diverse needs and contexts
avoid: Time-critical applications where stability is crucial

features: Context usage meters with visual token consumption tracking

tldr.what: Displays token usage, lets users pin important messages, and automatically summarizes old context to stay within LLM limits.
tldr.when: Long conversations where context window fills up and you need users to decide what to keep versus discard.
tldr.watchOut: Users often misjudge what information the agent actually needs, leading to pruned context that breaks downstream reasoning.

overview.pattern: Visual interfaces for managing LLM token limits and conversation context
overview.why: Context windows have hard limits that can break conversations and waste tokens without proper management
overview.insight: Show token usage in real-time + let users prioritize context + auto-compress when needed

impl.d: Visual progress bars showing context consumption
Pin important messages, compress or remove others
Summarize old conversations while preserving key info

overview.example: Token meter (75% full) → Warning → Pin key messages → Compress old → Continue conversation
dos: Show real-time token usage with clear visual indicators
Allow users to pin critical messages and context
Provide reversible compression and smart summarization
Warn users before approaching token limits
Implement sliding window management for long conversations
donts: Let conversations fail without warning
Remove context without user awareness or control
Hide token consumption and usage patterns
Lose critical context during compression
Make context management too complex for users

metrics.d: % of useful tokens vs total consumed
Preference for auto vs manual context management
Token cost savings from efficient management

usecases.d: Manage large PDF context while maintaining conversation history
Pin critical code sections, compress older discussion threads
Retain key findings while processing multiple source documents

features: Progressive error disclosure with actionable solutions

tldr.what: Presents errors with problem, cause, and actionable solution; routes display through inline, tooltip, modal, or banner based on severity.
tldr.when: Agent systems need users to understand failures, recover quickly, and maintain work context across error states.
tldr.watchOut: Over-communicating minor errors or suggesting recovery steps that don't actually work erodes user trust faster than silence.

overview.pattern: Comprehensive error communication and recovery interfaces for graceful failure handling
overview.why: Agent system failures need clear communication and effective recovery paths to maintain user trust
overview.insight: Use three-element structure: Problem + Cause + Solution with context preservation and progressive disclosure

impl.d: Categorize errors by severity, recoverability, and user impact
Choose appropriate modality: inline, tooltip, modal, or banner
Problem + Cause + Solution with progressive disclosure
Automatic retry, context preservation, and manual recovery
Input validation, confirmation dialogs, and undo capabilities

dos: Use clear, jargon-free language for error messages
Provide specific actionable solutions, not generic advice
Preserve user context and work during error recovery
Implement progressive disclosure for technical details
Use consistent visual design for error states
donts: Blame users or use negative language in error messages
Show technical stack traces or error codes to end users
Use error dialogs for non-critical validation messages
Leave users stranded without clear next steps
Hide errors or fail silently without user notification
use: Production systems with high user dependency
Complex agent operations prone to failure
Systems handling sensitive or valuable data
avoid: Internal tools with technical users only

metrics.d: Time from error to successful user resolution
% of user work preserved during error recovery
User understanding of error cause and solution
Reduction in preventable errors over time

usecases.d: Network timeouts with automatic retry and manual override
Real-time feedback with correction suggestions
Graceful degradation with alternative options
Clear explanations with resolution paths
Context preservation with partial result recovery

steps.title: Visual Chain-of-Thought (VCTP) Process

steps.title: Visual Attention Mechanisms

steps.title: Real-World Applications

steps.title: Performance and Business Impact
steps.description: Vision-language models have improved sharply on visual reasoning benchmarks, but published figures move with every model release and rarely transfer to a specific clinical set. Diagnostic efficiency gains, and 25% cost reduction.

steps.title: Advanced Fusion Strategies

steps.title: Intelligent Processing Pipeline

steps.title: Real-World Applications

steps.title: Business Impact and Future Innovation

description: Foundational privacy principles embedded into agent system architecture from conception, ensuring proactive data protection, user empowerment, and regulatory compliance through design rather than afterthought implementation.
features: Proactive not reactive: privacy risks prevented at design time
Privacy as the default setting with no user action required
Data minimization and purpose limitation built into flows
End-to-end lifecycle protection from collection to deletion

tldr.when: Systems handling sensitive user data (financial, health, personal) where regulatory compliance and user trust are non-negotiable business requirements.
tldr.watchOut: High upfront design cost; retrofitting privacy later is far more expensive than building it in, and incomplete threat modeling leaves gaps.

name: Granular Privacy Controls(GPC)
description: Fine-grained permission management enabling users to control specific data types, processing purposes, sharing contexts, and retention periods with contextual consent mechanisms and easy revocation controls.
features: Contextual consent requested at the moment of use
Retention period selection and automatic expiry
One-tap revocation with immediate downstream effect

tldr.what: Lets users grant or deny permission for specific data types, purposes, and sharing contexts separately, with chosen retention periods.
tldr.when: Systems collecting multiple data types where users need different rules for each, or where regulatory compliance requires documented consent tied to specific uses.
tldr.watchOut: Users often grant broad permissions without reading details, then revoke them reactively after privacy incidents rather than setting them thoughtfully upfront.

tldr.when: Multi-capability agents where users grant access gradually as features are used, not all at signup.
tldr.watchOut: Users may grant permissions without reading explanations if requests feel routine; fatigue still erodes informed consent.

name: Advanced Privacy Technologies UX(APT)
description: UX design for privacy-preserving technologies including differential privacy, federated learning, homomorphic encryption, and zero-knowledge proofs, making complex cryptographic protections accessible and understandable to end users.
features: Visual metaphors for differential privacy noise and budgets
Federated learning status indicators ("your data never left this device")
Verifiable proof surfaces for zero-knowledge claims

tldr.what: Translates cryptographic privacy mechanisms into visual controls and plain language so users understand what data protections actually do.
tldr.when: Systems handling sensitive data need user buy-in for privacy-preserving tech, and users lack cryptography expertise to evaluate trade-offs.
tldr.watchOut: Users may misinterpret simplified explanations as stronger guarantees than the underlying tech actually provides, creating false confidence.

name: Realtime Voice Agents(RVA)
description: Low-latency spoken agents built on speech-to-speech models over a single streaming session, replacing the traditional speech-to-text then LLM then text-to-speech pipeline. A single model reasons directly over audio, so responses arrive fast enough to feel like natural conversation, with turn detection, barge-in interruption, mid-conversation tool calls, guardrails, and handoffs handled inside the live session.
features: Single speech-to-speech model instead of a chained STT to LLM to TTS pipeline
Server-side voice activity detection and turn detection for natural turn-taking
Barge-in handling: the user can interrupt and the agent truncates its own speech
Mid-conversation tool calls and guardrail checks without leaving the audio stream
Agent-to-agent and agent-to-human handoffs on policy triggers during a live call
Telephony and SIP integration for phone-based support and outbound calling

tldr.what: Processes spoken input and generates spoken output through a single streaming model, enabling interruption and tool calls without leaving the audio stream.
tldr.when: Phone support, customer service, or any interaction where natural conversation rhythm and sub-200ms response latency are required.
tldr.watchOut: Latency spikes from tool calls, network drops, or VAD errors break the illusion of naturalness and frustrate users expecting real-time conversation.

flow.title: Realtime Voice Agents
flow.description: A low-latency phone support agent built on a single speech-to-speech model over a streaming session. Turn detection and voice activity detection drive natural turn-taking; the caller barges in mid-sentence and the agent truncates its own speech; a tool call runs mid-dialog without leaving the audio stream; and a policy guardrail triggers a SIP handoff to a human.

steps.title: Caller Dials In
steps.description: A phone call reaches the agent through a SIP gateway, which bridges it into a single persistent streaming session. Audio flows directly to a speech-to-speech model rather than a chained transcribe-reason-synthesize pipeline.

steps.title: Turn Detection on a Live Stream
steps.description: The model begins speaking its greeting while server-side voice activity detection and turn detection continuously track who holds the floor on the open audio stream.

steps.title: Barge-In Interruption
steps.description: The caller starts talking over the greeting. Turn detection flags the overlap as a barge-in, and the agent truncates its own audio output within about 200ms instead of talking past the caller.

steps.title: Mid-Dialog Tool Call
steps.description: Having heard "where is order 5567", the model calls the lookup_order tool without pausing the session. The tool returns status "in transit" with an ETA, which the agent then speaks back conversationally.

steps.title: Guardrail Fires on Policy
steps.description: The caller escalates to a refund over $500. A live policy guardrail recognizes this exceeds what the agent may authorize and marks the turn for handoff, all inside the ongoing call.

steps.title: SIP Handoff to a Human
steps.description: The handoff transfers the call over SIP to a human specialist, carrying the full conversation context so the caller does not have to repeat anything.

steps.title: Why Speech-to-Speech
steps.description: Because one model reasons over audio directly, voice-to-voice latency lands near 600ms versus roughly 2.5s for a separate STT then LLM then TTS pipeline, which is what makes interruption and natural turn-taking feel real.

name: AG-UI Protocol (Agent-User Interaction)(AGUI)
description: Open, event-based protocol (originated by CopilotKit, 2025) that standardizes the last mile between an agent backend and any frontend. The backend streams roughly 16 structured event types (text and token deltas, tool-call start/args/result, state snapshots and deltas, run lifecycle, and cancellation) over SSE, WebSocket, or plain HTTP, so a frontend can render live agent activity and feed user actions back into the same execution loop, framework-agnostically. Native emitters exist for LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, and the Microsoft Agent Framework, among others. It is the agent-to-UI edge of the protocol triangle, sitting beside MCP (agent-to-tool) and A2A (agent-to-agent). Distinct from `chat-interface-patterns`: those are frontend rendering conventions, whereas AG-UI is the wire protocol that carries the underlying event stream.
features: Roughly 16 structured event types: token deltas, tool-call lifecycle, state deltas, run lifecycle, cancel
Transport-agnostic streaming over SSE, WebSocket, or plain HTTP
Bidirectional loop: frontend renders activity and feeds user actions back to the agent
Shared-state sync via a full snapshot plus incremental deltas
Framework-agnostic emitters (LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, Microsoft Agent Framework)
Mid-run interrupts: pause, approve, edit, retry, and cancel a running agent

tldr.what: Standardized event protocol streaming agent activity (text, tool calls, state, lifecycle) to any frontend over SSE/WebSocket/HTTP, enabling bidirectional control and live rendering.
tldr.when: Building agent UX where frontend must display live execution, support mid-run interrupts (pause, approve, edit, cancel), and work across multiple backend frameworks.
tldr.watchOut: Event ordering and state consistency breaks if frontend and backend clocks drift or network drops packets; requires robust replay and reconciliation logic.

flow.title: AG-UI Protocol (Agent-User Interaction)
flow.description: Open, event-based protocol standardizing the stream between an agent backend and any frontend. Roughly 16 structured event types (token deltas, tool-call lifecycle, state deltas, run lifecycle, cancel) flow over SSE or WebSocket so the UI renders live activity and feeds user actions back into the same loop.

steps.title: User Request Enters the Loop
steps.description: A user asks the agent backend to compare churn and draft a summary. The backend is framework-native (LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, or the Microsoft Agent Framework) and speaks AG-UI at its edge.

steps.title: Backend Emits AG-UI Events
steps.description: The backend runs and its AG-UI emitter encodes progress as roughly 16 standard event types, streamed over a single transport connection (SSE, WebSocket, or plain HTTP).

steps.title: Structured Event Types Stream
steps.description: The transport carries the event families: run lifecycle (RUN_STARTED / RUN_FINISHED), text token deltas, tool-call lifecycle (START / ARGS / RESULT), and state snapshot plus deltas.

steps.title: Frontend Renders Live Activity
steps.description: A framework-agnostic frontend consumes the events and renders the plan token-by-token, a live tool progress row, a partial generative-UI chart, and a shared state object, all as they arrive.

steps.title: User Cancels Mid-Tool
steps.description: While the chart tool is still running, the user clicks Cancel. The frontend feeds that action back over the same connection into the running execution loop.

steps.title: Run Truncates and Marks Cancelled
steps.description: The backend truncates the in-flight tool and ends the run with a terminal cancelled event, so the half-rendered chart row is marked cancelled rather than left spinning.

steps.title: State Delta Syncs the Final UI
steps.description: The shared state object, updated by snapshot plus deltas, and the cancelled run resolve into one coherent final view. One protocol carried tokens, tool progress, generative UI, shared state, and cancellation.

name: Approval Queues & Escalation Chains(AQE)
description: First-class approval and escalation as an operational workflow rather than a single blocking gate. Actions are tiered by risk: reversible actions auto-approve, medium-risk actions go to asynchronous review where the agent persists its state, continues other work, and rehydrates when a decision arrives, and irreversible actions require synchronous approval before execution. Escalation is triggered by explicit signals including confidence breaches, an irreversibility flag, SLA-approach, and anomaly or injection detection, and routes the decision to a higher-authority adjudicator (a human, a more-privileged agent, or an external workflow). Distinct from `human-in-the-loop`: HITL is the generic synchronous stance, whereas this pattern adds risk tiering, asynchronous queueing with state rehydration, and adjudicator routing.
features: Risk tiers: auto-approve reversible, async-review medium, sync-approve irreversible
Asynchronous approval: agent persists state, works other tasks, rehydrates on decision
Escalation triggers: confidence breach, irreversibility, SLA-approach, anomaly or injection
Adjudicator routing to a human, higher-privilege agent, or external workflow
Decision-ready context packages (summary, diff, financial impact, reversibility flag)
Time limits with automatic escalation so approvals do not stall operations

tldr.what: Routes actions through risk tiers: reversible auto-approve, medium-risk async review with state persistence, irreversible sync approval. Escalates by confidence, irreversibility flag, SLA, or anomaly to designated adjudicators.
tldr.when: Operations where some decisions can proceed without approval, others need asynchronous human review without blocking the agent, and some require synchronous sign-off before execution.
tldr.watchOut: State rehydration after approval delay can fail silently if context drifts or the agent's working memory is incomplete when resuming.

flow.title: Approval Queues & Escalation Chains
flow.description: Approval and escalation as an operational workflow. Actions are tiered by risk: reversible auto-approves, medium-risk goes to an async queue where the agent persists state and keeps working, and irreversible requires a synchronous gate. Escalation routes the decision to a higher-authority adjudicator on signals like SLA breach.

nodes.label:
🎯 Agent Proposes Action
Refund request

⚖️ Risk Classifier
Tier by value + reversibility

🟢 Tier 1: Reversible
< $50 auto-approve

🟡 Tier 2: Medium
Async review queue

🔴 Tier 3: Irreversible
Synchronous approval

✅ $38 Refund Issued

💾 Persist Case State
Customer, order, evidence

🔁 Agent Continues
Picks up next ticket

⛔ Sync Gate
Paused until human approves

📥 Approval Queue
$2,000 refund + decision package

steps.title: Agent Proposes an Action
steps.description: The support agent produces a candidate action (a refund) that has a side effect on money, so it must pass through the approval plane before executing.

steps.title: Classify by Risk Tier
steps.description: The classifier tiers the action by value and reversibility: reversible and low-value goes auto-approve, medium-value goes to async review, and irreversible goes to a synchronous gate.

steps.title: Reversible: Auto-Approve
steps.description: A $38 refund on a damaged item is reversible and under the $50 threshold, so the agent issues it immediately and logs it for asynchronous audit.

steps.title: Medium: Async Queue, Agent Keeps Working
steps.description: A $2,000 refund is above threshold but reversible. The agent persists the full case state to a store, enqueues it for review, and keeps working the next ticket instead of blocking.

steps.title: Route to Adjudicator with SLA
steps.description: The queued case is routed to a supervisor with a decision-ready package (summary, diff, $2,000 impact, reversibility flag). An SLA timer will auto-escalate to the on-call manager if it sits untouched for 4 hours.

steps.title: Decision Arrives, State Rehydrates
steps.description: Whether the supervisor approves or the escalated manager decides, the agent rehydrates the exact saved case state and executes the refund as a single coherent thread rather than a dropped conversation.

steps.title: Irreversible: Synchronous Gate
steps.description: Separately, a proposal to close the customer account is irreversible. That tier requires synchronous approval: the agent pauses and cannot proceed until a human approves in-line.

references: Designing Approval Workflows for High-Stakes Agent Actions (Prefactor) - https://prefactor.tech/learn/designing-agent-approval-workflows
Human-in-the-Loop Escalation Design for AI Agents (DigitalApplied) - https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/human-in-the-loop-escalation-design-ai-agents-2026
A Five-Plane Reference Architecture for Runtime Governance of Production AI Agents - https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12320

name: Generative UI (Agent-Rendered Interfaces)(GenUI)
description: The agent generates, selects, and controls the interface itself at runtime, returning rich interactive components (forms, charts, dashboards, maps, multi-step widgets) instead of plain text, and deciding HOW to present a result from the content type and the user intent. A model tool call emits UI that the host renders in a sandboxed frame, for example MCP Apps serving bundled HTML through `ui://` resources, or portable specs like Google A2UI and Open-JSON-UI that the client paints natively. This crossed from experimental to production in 2026 as MCP Apps shipped across Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, and Goose, alongside A2UI and CopilotKit/assistant-ui generative UI. Distinct from `ag-ui-protocol`, which streams agent EVENTS to a prebuilt frontend, and `adaptive-interface-patterns`, which personalizes an EXISTING interface: here the agent materializes the interface itself, choosing and constructing the components at response time.
features: Agent picks the presentation: a chart for a trend, a form for an action, a table for a comparison
Tool calls return UI components, not just text, which the host renders inline
Sandboxed rendering: MCP Apps serve bundled HTML via `ui://` resources in an isolated iframe
Portable UI specs (Google A2UI, Open-JSON-UI) painted natively by the client, host-agnostic
Bidirectional: rendered widgets post user actions back into the agent loop as tool results
Content-and-intent routing decides layout, density, and modality per response

tldr.what: Agent generates and returns interactive UI components (forms, charts, tables, maps) as tool outputs, which the host renders in sandboxed frames.
tldr.when: Results benefit from visual presentation, user needs to interact with data, or the best format depends on intent and content type.
tldr.watchOut: Rendering failures, network latency, and browser compatibility issues compound agent errors; test UI generation paths thoroughly before production.

flow.title: Generative UI (Agent-Rendered Interfaces)
flow.description: The agent decides HOW to present each answer and materializes the interface at runtime. It classifies the content type and intent, chooses the right component (chart, form, or table), emits it as a sandboxed ui:// resource the host renders inline, and wires user actions back into the agent loop.

steps.title: User Query
steps.description: The user asks a question in plain language. Instead of returning text, the agent will decide what interface best answers it.

steps.title: Intent + Content Routing
steps.description: The agent classifies the content type and the user intent. "Sales trend" is time-series, "book a sync" is an action, "compare plans" is a comparison.

steps.title: Choose the Interface
steps.description: Each content type maps to the best presentation: a line chart for the trend, a booking form for the action, a comparison table for the comparison.

steps.title: Emit UI Component
steps.description: The agent calls render_ui(), emitting a ui:// resource that bundles the component as HTML. The agent materializes the interface rather than describing it.

steps.title: Host Renders in a Sandbox
steps.description: The host receives the ui:// resource and paints it in a sandboxed iframe with no direct host access, the way MCP Apps render bundled HTML.

steps.title: Interactive Components Appear
steps.description: The chart, form, and table render inline in the conversation. Each is fully interactive: tooltips on the chart, inputs on the form, a Choose button per table column.

steps.title: User Acts on the Widget
steps.description: The user interacts, for example submitting the booking form or clicking Choose plan. The widget captures the action and posts the values back.

steps.title: Back into the Agent Loop
steps.description: The posted-back values arrive as a tool result, so the agent continues the same conversation: it books the sync or applies the chosen plan, then can render the next interface.

name: Event-Driven Orchestrator-Worker(EDOW)
description: Central orchestrator assigns tasks to worker agents through event streaming

tldr.what: Orchestrator publishes tasks to an event stream; stateless workers consume and process them in parallel, publishing results back asynchronously.
tldr.when: High-volume parallel work where workers fail or scale unpredictably, and you need automatic recovery without direct connections.
tldr.watchOut: Event ordering and exactly-once semantics are hard; duplicate processing or lost results occur if you skip idempotency design.

flow.title: Event-Driven Orchestrator-Worker
flow.description: A central orchestrator distributes tasks to stateless worker agents through a partitioned event stream. Workers form a consumer group that load-balances and auto-rebalances on failure, publishing results to a downstream topic for aggregation.

📄 Batch Request
"Extract data from 10,000 invoices"

🎛️ Orchestrator Agent
Splits batch into keyed tasks

📨 work-queue Topic
Partitioned event stream (4 partitions)

👥 Consumer Group
Assigns partitions to workers

⚖️ Rebalancer
Reassigns partitions on scale/failure

⚙️ Worker 1
Partition 0
Status: Processing

⚙️ Worker 2
Partition 1
Status: Processing

⚙️ Worker 3
Partition 2
Status: Crashed

⚙️ Worker 4
Partition 3 + reassigned 2
Status: Processing

⚠️ errors Topic
Failed tasks for replay

📬 results Topic
Completed task outputs

🧮 Result Aggregator
Collates outputs by batch key

✅ Aggregated Output
Structured dataset of 10,000 invoices

steps.title: Batch Request
steps.description: A client submits a large batch job that must be processed in parallel without coupling to any specific worker.

steps.title: Task Distribution
steps.description: The orchestrator splits the batch into keyed tasks and publishes them to the partitioned work-queue topic. It never talks to workers directly.

steps.title: Consumer Group Formation
steps.description: Stateless workers join a consumer group. Partitions are assigned so each worker owns a disjoint slice of the stream.

steps.title: Worker Failure
steps.description: Worker 3 crashes mid-partition. Its unprocessed task is routed to the errors topic for replay rather than being lost.

steps.title: Automatic Rebalancing
steps.description: The rebalancer detects the membership change and reassigns partition 2 to a healthy worker, keeping throughput steady with no orchestrator intervention.

steps.title: Event Replay
steps.description: The orchestrator consumes the errors topic and re-publishes failed tasks, letting recovery happen through replay instead of manual retries.

steps.title: Result Emission
steps.description: Workers publish completed outputs to the results topic as they finish, fully decoupled from one another.

steps.title: Aggregation and Output
steps.description: The aggregator consumes the results topic, collates outputs by batch key, and emits the final structured dataset.

references: Kafka: a Distributed Messaging System for Log Processing (NetDB 2011)
Triggerflow: Trigger-based Orchestration of Serverless Workflows - https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.00583

name: Event-Driven Hierarchical Agents(EDHA)
description: Multi-level agent hierarchy with event-based coordination

tldr.what: Organizes agents in levels where each tier consumes events, decomposes work, and publishes to the next tier's topic.
tldr.when: Large organizations with clear reporting structures need task delegation, isolation of failures, and independent scaling per level.
tldr.watchOut: Event propagation delays and cascading failures across levels become hard to debug; misconfigured topics cause work to vanish silently.

flow.title: Event-Driven Hierarchical Agents
flow.description: A multi-level hierarchy of orchestrators coordinates through layered event topics. Directives cascade downward as each level decomposes work for the level below, while status reports bubble back up, isolating faults at each tier.

nodes.label:
🎯 Strategic Goal

📊 Engineering Manager

steps.title: Strategic Goal
steps.description: A high-level objective enters at the top of the hierarchy, too broad for any single team to act on directly.

steps.title: Executive Directives
steps.description: The executive orchestrator publishes strategic intent to the executive-directives topic instead of assigning work by hand.

steps.title: Manager Decomposition
steps.description: Level-specific managers consume directives and decompose them into work packages on the manager-assignments topic.

steps.title: Team Task Creation
steps.description: Team leads consume assignments and emit concrete, executable tasks to the team-tasks topic, completing the cascade.

steps.title: Execution
steps.description: Workers at the bottom tier pick up tasks and execute them independently, with faults contained to this level.

steps.title: Status Reports Bubble Up
steps.description: Progress events flow to the status-reports topic and propagate upward, giving the executive tier visibility without polling.

steps.title: Goal Achieved
steps.description: With every tier reacting to events from adjacent levels, the hierarchy converges and the product launch is delivered.

references: Georgievski & Aiello (2014): An Overview of Hierarchical Task Network Planning
Agha (1986): Actors: A Model of Concurrent Computation

name: Event-Driven Blackboard(EDB)
description: Shared knowledge base through event streaming for asynchronous collaboration

tldr.what: Agents post events to a shared knowledge base; other agents subscribe, react asynchronously, and post new events, creating a persistent audit trail of contributions.
tldr.when: Multiple agents must collaborate on evolving problems where intermediate results inform others, and you need to track how conclusions formed over time.
tldr.watchOut: Event ordering and timing bugs multiply quickly; agents may act on stale data or miss critical events, causing inconsistent final states.

flow.title: Event-Driven Blackboard
flow.description: Specialist agents collaborate through a shared, event-sourced knowledge space rather than direct messaging. Each specialist watches the blackboard and contributes opportunistically when the current state matches its expertise, building knowledge incrementally with a full audit trail.

nodes.label:
🔬 Research Problem
"Identify a drug candidate for target X"

🧠 Shared Blackboard
Event-sourced knowledge space

🧪 Hypothesis Agent
Proposes candidate mechanisms

📊 Data Agent
Retrieves supporting evidence

📈 Analysis Agent
Computes statistics

🔍 Peer Review Agent
Validates methodology

📌 hypothesis-posted
Knowledge entry

📌 evidence-added
Knowledge entry

📌 analysis-completed
Knowledge entry

📌 peer-review-submitted
Knowledge entry

🧩 Synthesis Agent
Builds consensus from state

🤝 consensus-reached
Stable knowledge state

✅ Validated Conclusion
Ranked drug candidate with evidence

steps.title: Problem Posted
steps.description: A research problem seeds the shared blackboard. No agent is assigned; specialists will react to the evolving knowledge state on their own.

steps.title: Hypothesis Contribution
steps.description: The hypothesis agent recognizes an empty board and opportunistically posts a candidate mechanism as a hypothesis-posted event.

steps.title: Evidence Gathering
steps.description: The new hypothesis triggers the data agent, which retrieves supporting evidence and appends an evidence-added event.

steps.title: Statistical Analysis
steps.description: With evidence present, the analysis agent activates and writes an analysis-completed event holding computed statistics.

steps.title: Peer Review
steps.description: The peer review agent validates the methodology already on the board and submits a peer-review-submitted event.

steps.title: Consensus Synthesis
steps.description: Seeing hypothesis, evidence, analysis, and review all present, the synthesis agent reconciles them into a consensus-reached state.

steps.title: Validated Conclusion
steps.description: The stable consensus state is emitted as the final conclusion, backed by the full event history of how it was reached.

references: The Hearsay-II Speech-Understanding System: Integrating Knowledge to Resolve Uncertainty - Erman et al. (ACM Computing Surveys 1980) - https://doi.org/10.1145/356810.356816
Blackboard Systems: The Blackboard Model of Problem Solving - Nii (AI Magazine 1986) - https://doi.org/10.1609/aimag.v7i2.537

name: Event-Driven Market-Based(EDMB)
description: Decentralized task allocation through bid/ask event marketplace

tldr.what: Agents bid on tasks posted to a marketplace, a coordinator matches bids to tasks using pricing and reputation, winner executes and updates reputation.
tldr.when: Multiple autonomous agents compete for work, task allocation needs dynamic pricing, or you want agents to self-select based on capability and cost.
tldr.watchOut: Coordination overhead and latency from bidding rounds can exceed the cost savings from decentralized allocation.

flow.title: Event-Driven Market-Based
flow.description: Tasks are allocated through a decentralized auction rather than central assignment. Clients post tasks as events, competing agents publish bids, and a market maker matches the optimal bid using price and reputation, updating reputation after delivery.

nodes.label:
📋 Client Task
"Translate 500 docs, budget $1,200"

📢 task-requests Topic
Open task with requirements

🏦 Market Maker
Matching engine for bid vs ask

🤖 Agent A
Bid: $0.020/word
Reputation: 4.8

🤖 Agent B
Bid: $0.015/word
Reputation: 4.2

🤖 Agent C
Bid: $0.025/word
Reputation: 4.9

💰 agent-bids Topic
Bids: capability + price events

⭐ Reputation Ledger
Historical quality scores

🏆 Winning Agent (A)
Best price-reputation utility

Completion proof event

💳 payment + reputation-updates
Settlement event

steps.title: Task Posted
steps.description: A client posts a task with requirements and a budget to the task-requests topic, without deciding who should do the work.

steps.title: Market Maker Broadcast
steps.description: The market maker consumes the open task and broadcasts it so any capable agent can choose to compete.

steps.title: Bid Submission
steps.description: Agents independently publish bids combining their price and capabilities to the agent-bids stream.

steps.title: Bid Evaluation
steps.description: The market maker consumes the bid stream and weighs each bid against the reputation ledger, not price alone.

steps.title: Match Awarded
steps.description: Agent A wins on best price-to-reputation utility, even though Agent B bid lower, and is awarded the task.

steps.title: Service Delivery
steps.description: The winning agent executes the work and publishes a completion-proof event to the service-delivery topic.

steps.title: Payment and Reputation Update
steps.description: Delivery triggers settlement, and the payment event feeds back a fresh reputation score, closing the incentive loop.

steps.title: Result Delivered
steps.description: The completed translation is returned to the client, allocated entirely by market dynamics with no central planner.

name: Enterprise Orchestration
description: Enterprise-grade coordination with governance, compliance, and audit capabilities

tldr.what: Coordinates agent workflows with built-in governance, compliance tracking, audit logging, and role-based access controls across enterprise systems.
tldr.when: Regulated industries processing sensitive data where you need documented approval chains, compliance proof, and role-based task routing.
tldr.watchOut: Governance overhead slows execution; audit logging at scale creates storage and query bottlenecks if not architected carefully.

flow.title: Enterprise Orchestration
flow.description: Enterprise-grade coordination that wraps agent processing in governance, compliance, and audit controls. Every stage enforces access control, policy gates, quality checks, and SLA monitoring, with exceptions escalated and outcomes recorded for regulatory review.

nodes.label:
📄 Document Intake
"Loan application containing PII"

🏢 Enterprise Orchestrator
Governed process controller

🔐 IAM / RBAC
Role-based access control

🏷️ Classification Engine
Sensitivity tagging

⚖️ Compliance Gate
GDPR / CCPA policy checks

📓 Audit Trail
Immutable event log

⏱️ SLA Monitor
Tracks stage deadlines

🤖 Extraction Agent
Cleared for classified data

🧑‍⚖️ Approval Agent
Multi-stage sign-off

✅ Quality Gate
Validates output at each stage

Routes failures to humans

✍️ Digital Signature
Seals approved output

Applies data lifecycle rules

✅ Compliant Output
Decision + audit-ready dashboard

steps.title: Governed Intake
steps.description: A sensitive document enters the orchestrator, which treats the request as a governed process rather than a simple task.

steps.title: Access Control and Classification
steps.description: The orchestrator authorizes the request through IAM and RBAC and classifies the document by sensitivity before any processing.

steps.title: Compliance Gate
steps.description: Policy checks for GDPR and CCPA run at the compliance gate, blocking the pipeline unless the document may lawfully be processed.

steps.title: Cleared Extraction
steps.description: Only an agent with the right clearance receives the classified document, and it extracts the required fields.

steps.title: Multi-Stage Approval
steps.description: The approval agent applies multi-stage sign-off for sensitive data, writing each decision to the immutable audit trail.

steps.title: Quality Gate and Escalation
steps.description: A quality gate validates the output. Failures, and SLA breaches from the monitor, are escalated to humans for remediation.

steps.title: Signing and Retention
steps.description: Approved output is digitally signed and has retention policies applied so its lifecycle is controlled from creation.

steps.title: Compliant Output
steps.description: The final decision is delivered alongside an audit-ready dashboard, with every stage recorded and every deadline tracked.

references: • A Case for Microservices Orchestration Using Workflow Engines (2022) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.07210
• Component-aware Orchestration of Cloud-based Enterprise Applications (2020)
Implementation Guides
• NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
• ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI Management System

name: Stateful Graph Workflows
description: Graph-based workflow management with persistent state across nodes

tldr.what: Organizes work as interconnected nodes that pass data between stages, storing progress and state at each step to enable conditional routing and parallel paths.
tldr.when: Complex multi-stage processes where intermediate results determine next steps, recovery from failures matters, or multiple documents need simultaneous processing.
tldr.watchOut: State bloat and synchronization bugs grow quickly; debugging failures across distributed nodes becomes exponentially harder than linear pipelines.

flow.title: Stateful Graph Workflows
flow.description: A workflow modeled as a directed graph of nodes that share a single persistent state object. Conditional edges route on state, checkpoints let the run resume after failure, and specialist branches execute based on runtime classification, in the style of a LangGraph state machine.

nodes.label:
📄 Workflow Input
"Incoming contract PDF"

💾 State Store
Persistent shared state + checkpoints

📑 Extract Node
PDF to text

🔖 Checkpoint
Snapshot after extract

🔎 Analyze Node
Text to entities + confidence

🔀 Conditional Edge
Route on confidence

🧑‍⚖️ Human Review
Low-confidence branch

🏷️ Classify Node
Entities to category

⚖️ Legal Specialist
Handles type = legal

🔧 Tech Specialist
Handles type = technical

♻️ Resume from Checkpoint
Recovers on failure

✅ Routed Result
Specialist output + final state

steps.title: Workflow Initialized
steps.description: A document enters the graph and a fresh shared state object is created in the state store to carry data across every node.

steps.title: Extraction and Checkpoint
steps.description: The extract node converts the PDF to text and writes a checkpoint, capturing a resumable snapshot of the state.

steps.title: Analysis
steps.description: The analyze node reads the shared state, derives entities, and records a confidence score back into the state.

steps.title: Conditional Routing
steps.description: A conditional edge inspects the confidence in the state. High confidence proceeds to classification; low confidence diverts to human review.

steps.title: Checkpoint Recovery
steps.description: If a downstream node fails, the run restores the last checkpoint from the state store and re-enters the graph without repeating earlier work.

steps.title: Classification
steps.description: The classify node maps entities to a document category, updating the state that determines the next branch.

steps.title: Specialist Branch
steps.description: Based on the classified type, the graph routes to the legal or technical specialist node for domain-specific handling.

steps.title: Routed Result
steps.description: The chosen specialist produces the final output, carrying the complete accumulated state through to the end of the workflow.

references: Styx: Transactional Stateful Functions on Streaming Dataflows (2023) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.06893
Streaming Processing of Dynamic Graphs: Concepts, Models, and Systems (2019) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.12740
Stateful Dataflow Multigraphs: A Data-Centric Model for Performance Portability on Heterogeneous Architectures (2019) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10345

name: Conversational Orchestration
description: Multi-agent coordination through structured conversation patterns

tldr.what: Coordinates multiple agents through structured message exchanges where any agent can speak, context persists across turns, and participation adapts to conversation state.
tldr.when: Complex workflows requiring back-and-forth between specialized agents, where the next step depends on what previous agents said, and order isn't strictly predetermined.
tldr.watchOut: Conversation can loop indefinitely or diverge if agents lack clear exit criteria or if context grows too large for reliable message passing.

flow.title: Conversational Orchestration
flow.description: Multiple agents coordinate through a shared, group-chat style conversation rather than fixed pipelines. A moderator opens a thread, specialist agents contribute turns that accumulate as shared context, and a consensus detector decides when the discussion has converged.

nodes.label:
📝 Review Task
"Assess paper on AI safety"

🧑‍⚖️ Editor / Moderator Agent
Opens and steers the discussion

🧵 Conversation Thread
Shared context and memory

🔬 Methodology Expert
Critiques experimental design

📊 Statistics Expert
Checks analysis and rigor

🧠 Domain Expert
Assesses related work

💬 Turn 1
"Methodology is sound, but..."

💬 Turn 2
"Statistical power is too low..."

💬 Turn 3
"Related work omits key results..."

🤝 Consensus Detector
Measures agreement

📄 Summary Agent
Synthesizes the decision

✅ Review Decision
"Accept with minor revisions"

steps.title: Review Task
steps.description: A task arrives that needs several perspectives, so it is handed to a moderator rather than a single agent.

steps.title: Open the Thread
steps.description: The moderator opens a shared conversation thread that will hold the full context every participant can see.

steps.title: Experts Join
steps.description: Specialist agents read the current thread state, deciding what to contribute based on the shared context rather than fixed roles in a pipeline.

steps.title: Contributed Turns
steps.description: Each expert speaks in turn, producing a message informed by what came before it.

steps.title: Context Accumulates
steps.description: Every turn is appended back to the shared thread, so later contributions build on the accumulated multi-turn history.

steps.title: Consensus Detection
steps.description: A consensus detector evaluates the thread. If agreement is not yet reached, it hands control back to the moderator for another round.

steps.title: Summary and Decision
steps.description: Once the discussion converges, the summary agent synthesizes the thread into a single decision and emits the final review outcome.

references: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation - https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155
ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting (2022)
Advancing the State of the Art in Open Domain Dialog Systems through the Alexa Prize - https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.10757

name: Role-Based Teamwork
description: Structured agent teams with defined roles and responsibilities

tldr.what: Assigns distinct roles to agents with specific capabilities and responsibilities, coordinating their work through defined handoffs and delegation patterns.
tldr.when: Complex projects requiring specialized expertise where different agents need clear ownership and sequential or parallel task execution.
tldr.watchOut: Role boundaries become rigid bottlenecks; agents block waiting for role-holders instead of adapting when someone is unavailable or overloaded.

flow.title: Role-Based Teamwork
flow.description: Structured agent teams where each member is given an explicit role, goal, and backstory (CrewAI-style), collaborating through clear handoffs and shared accountability to deliver a project.

Backstory: Full-stack engineer

Backstory: Test automation pro

Dashboard requirements

Component architecture

⚙️ Feature Code
Dashboard implementation

Status, ownership, handoffs

Role-to-role delivery gate

steps.title: Project Brief
steps.description: A cross-functional deliverable arrives that no single role can complete alone.

steps.title: Crew Assembly
steps.description: The crew manager instantiates each agent with an explicit role, goal, and backstory.

steps.title: Requirements Definition
steps.description: The Product Manager owns scope and turns the brief into concrete user stories.

steps.title: Architecture Handoff
steps.description: User stories are handed to the Architect, who designs the component structure.

steps.title: Implementation Handoff
steps.description: The Developer receives the design and implements the dashboard features.

steps.title: Quality Handoff
steps.description: QA takes the feature code, runs the suite, and produces a validated test report.

steps.title: Deployment Handoff
steps.description: DevOps deploys the validated build to production.

steps.title: Coordination and Delivery
steps.description: The shared board and handoff protocol keep every role accountable through to delivery.

AgentScope: Flexible Multi‑Agent Platform (2024)

name: Graph State Machines
description: Finite state machines implemented as graphs for workflow control

tldr.what: Models workflow as states connected by guarded transitions, executing deterministic paths based on events and validation rules.
tldr.when: Multi-stage processes with clear state boundaries, rollback needs, and conditional branching based on step outcomes.
tldr.watchOut: State explosion and maintenance burden grow quickly as edge cases and error paths multiply beyond initial design.

flow.title: Graph State Machines
flow.description: A finite state machine expressed as a graph, where nodes are explicit states and edges are guarded transitions. Deterministic flow control with validation guards, checkpointing, and rollback keeps a workflow such as order processing in a known state at all times.

nodes.label:
🛒 New Order
Customer places order #4821

⏳ State: Pending
Awaiting validation

🛡️ Guard: validate
Check inventory + customer data

✔️ State: Validated
Ready for payment

🚫 State: Rejected
Invalid data, terminal

🛡️ Guard: process_payment
Verify payment method

💳 State: Paid
Payment captured

⚠️ State: Payment Failed
Declined transaction

🛡️ Guard: fulfill
Confirm warehouse stock

📦 State: Shipped
Handed to carrier

🕒 State: Backordered
Inventory empty, retry later

✨ State: Completed
Delivered, terminal

❌ State: Cancelled
Any state, cancel event

💾 State Store
Persisted state + transition log

↩️ Rollback
Revert to last stable state

steps.title: Order Received
steps.description: A new order enters the machine in the Pending state, the single defined entry point.

steps.title: Validation Guard
steps.description: The validate guard checks inventory and customer data, branching to Validated on success or the terminal Rejected state on failure.

steps.title: Payment Transition
steps.description: From Validated the process_payment guard verifies the payment method, moving to Paid or Payment Failed.

steps.title: Failure Recovery via Rollback
steps.description: A declined payment triggers rollback to the last stable checkpoint rather than leaving the order in a broken state.

steps.title: Fulfillment Guard
steps.description: From Paid the fulfill guard confirms warehouse stock, shipping the order or holding it as Backordered with a retry transition.

steps.title: State Checkpointing
steps.description: Each stable state is persisted to the state store with its full transition log, enabling recovery and audit.

steps.title: Cancellation Path
steps.description: A cancel event is a valid transition out of many states, routing to the terminal Cancelled state with any needed refund.

steps.title: Completion
steps.description: Delivery moves the order from Shipped to the terminal Completed state, ending the machine.

references: Harel (1987): Statecharts - A Visual Formalism for Complex Systems
Murata (1989): Petri Nets - Properties, Analysis and Applications
Workflow Patterns (van der Aalst et al.)

name: Actor Model Coordination
description: Asynchronous message-passing coordination between independent actors

tldr.what: Independent agents exchange messages asynchronously, each managing its own state and lifecycle within a supervision hierarchy for fault isolation.
tldr.when: Distributed systems needing concurrent work on separate tasks with automatic recovery from individual component failures.
tldr.watchOut: Message ordering guarantees and debugging distributed state become complex; supervision overhead can outweigh benefits for simple sequential workflows.

flow.title: Actor Model Coordination
flow.description: Independent actors coordinate purely through asynchronous messages delivered to their mailboxes, with no shared state. A supervision tree isolates faults and restarts failed actors, while a message log enables replay. Illustrated with a distributed content-processing batch.

nodes.label:
📥 Content Batch
500 mixed media items

🎭 Supervisor Actor
Root of the supervision tree

🗄️ Message Log
Persisted for replay

🛡️ Supervision Strategy
restart / resume / stop

📨 Ingestion Actor
Receives + partitions content

🎯 Processing Coordinator
Routes items to processors

📤 Output Manager Actor
Collects + assembles results

📬 Coordinator Mailbox
FIFO queue of messages

📝 Text Processor x3
Mailbox: 40 msgs

🖼️ Image Processor x2
Mailbox: 25 msgs

🎬 Video Processor x1
Mailbox: 8 msgs

💥 Failed Text Actor
Exception on item #217

♻️ Restart Directive
Spawn fresh instance

✨ Assembled Output
Processed batch delivered

steps.title: Batch Arrival
steps.description: A content batch is handed to the supervisor actor, which is the root of the actor system.

steps.title: Supervision Tree
steps.description: The supervisor spawns and supervises its child actors and declares the restart strategy that governs failures.

steps.title: Asynchronous Messaging
steps.description: The ingestion actor sends messages to the coordinator mailbox; there is no shared memory, only queued messages.

steps.title: Message Dispatch
steps.description: The coordinator drains its mailbox in order and dispatches items to the text, image, and video processor pools.

steps.title: Message Persistence
steps.description: Mailbox messages are persisted to the message log so they can be replayed after a crash.

steps.title: Fault Isolation
steps.description: A text processor throws on item #217 and crashes, but the failure is isolated and does not affect other actors.

steps.title: Supervised Recovery
steps.description: The crash escalates to the supervision strategy, which restarts a fresh instance and replays its messages from the log.

steps.title: Result Assembly
steps.description: Processors send their results to the output manager, which assembles and delivers the completed batch.

references: Agha (1986): Actors: A Model of Concurrent Computation
Hewitt, Bishop, Steiger (1973): A Universal Modular ACTOR Formalism for AI
Orleans: Distributed Virtual Actors (Microsoft Research)

name: Edge AI Optimization(EAO)
description: Optimizes AI workflows for resource-constrained edge devices and mobile environments

tldr.what: Compresses models and adapts inference quality based on device resources and network conditions to run AI on edge devices.
tldr.when: Deploying AI to mobile phones, IoT devices, or cameras where bandwidth, power, or compute are severely limited.
tldr.watchOut: Accuracy loss compounds across compression steps; test real-world performance on actual target hardware before deployment.

flow.title: Edge AI Optimization
flow.description: Runs AI workflows within the tight compute, memory, power, and bandwidth limits of edge devices. Combines model compression, inference batching, motion-gated adaptive quality, and network-aware upload, shown through a smart-camera security system.

📱 Edge Device

🔋 Power Manager
Budgets compute vs battery

🗜️ Quantization

✂️ Pruning

🧠 Edge Model
8MB, runs fully on-device

Selects analysis depth

Full resolution analysis

50% resolution analysis

Keyframe analysis only

Essential detection only

steps.title: Camera Stream
steps.description: A high-frame-rate security stream feeds a resource-constrained edge device that must process it locally.

steps.title: Model Compression
steps.description: Quantization then pruning shrink a 50MB model to an 8MB edge model that keeps 91% accuracy and fits on-device.

steps.title: Inference Batching
steps.description: Similar frames are grouped and processed four at a time for roughly a 3x throughput gain.

steps.title: Adaptive Motion Gating
steps.description: A motion gate picks the analysis resolution per frame: full for high motion, half for normal activity, keyframes only for static scenes.

steps.title: Power-Aware Degradation
steps.description: When the power manager reports low battery, the device falls back to essential detection only.

steps.title: On-Device Detection
steps.description: The selected mode plus batched inference produce detections locally, cutting processing time and power draw.

steps.title: Network-Aware Upload
steps.description: Results are routed by connectivity: sync to the cloud on WiFi, or keep only critical events locally when offline.

name: Federated Orchestration(FO)
description: Coordinates AI processing across distributed edge devices while preserving data privacy

tldr.what: Coordinates model training across distributed devices by sharing weight updates instead of raw data, then aggregates updates at a central point.
tldr.when: Multi-party data collaboration where privacy regulations or sensitivity prevent centralizing raw data before processing.
tldr.watchOut: Communication overhead and synchronization delays across devices often outweigh privacy gains; plan for significant latency and partial device failures.

flow.title: Federated Orchestration
flow.description: Coordinates AI training across independent organizations so that raw data never leaves each site. Only privacy-protected model updates are shared and securely aggregated into an improved global model, shown with a network of hospitals training a diagnostic AI.

nodes.label:
🧠 Global Model v3
Baseline diagnostic AI

🌐 Federation Coordinator
Orchestrates training rounds

🏥 Hospital A
Local cohort: 12k patients

🏥 Hospital B
Local cohort: 8k patients

🏥 Hospital C
Local cohort: 15k patients

🔒 Private Data A
Never leaves premises

🔒 Private Data B
Never leaves premises

🔒 Private Data C
Never leaves premises

📊 Weight Update A
Gradients only, no data

📊 Weight Update B
Gradients only, no data

📊 Weight Update C
Gradients only, no data

🕶️ Differential Privacy
Noise added, epsilon = 1.0

🔐 Secure Aggregation
Encrypted weighted sum

✨ Updated Global Model
+40% diagnostic accuracy

steps.title: Global Model Initialization
steps.description: The coordinator starts a training round from the current global diagnostic model.

steps.title: Model Distribution
steps.description: The coordinator distributes identical model weights to every participating hospital.

steps.title: Local Private Training
steps.description: Each hospital trains on its own patient cohort; the raw data never leaves the premises.

steps.title: Weight Update Computation
steps.description: Local training produces gradient updates that carry learning but no identifiable data.

steps.title: Differential Privacy
steps.description: Calibrated noise is added to the updates so no single patient can be inferred from them.

steps.title: Secure Aggregation
steps.description: Updates are combined under encryption so the coordinator sees only the aggregate, never individual contributions.

steps.title: Global Model Update
steps.description: The aggregated update yields an improved global model with materially higher diagnostic accuracy.

steps.title: Next Federation Round
steps.description: The improved model is redistributed, and the privacy-preserving cycle repeats each period.

references: Communication‑Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data (McMahan et al., 2017) – FedAvg
Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning (Kairouz et al., 2021) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.04977
Practical Secure Aggregation for Privacy‑Preserving ML (Bonawitz et al., CCS 2017)
Krum: Byzantine‑tolerant aggregation (Blanchard et al., NeurIPS 2017)
Federated Optimization in Heterogeneous Networks - https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.06127

name: Resource-Aware Scheduling(RAS)
description: Dynamically schedules AI tasks based on available computational resources and constraints

tldr.what: Queues AI tasks and adjusts their priority and timing based on live CPU, GPU, memory, temperature, and power measurements.
tldr.when: Systems running multiple AI workloads with hard deadlines, limited compute, or thermal constraints that change during operation.
tldr.watchOut: Overhead from constant monitoring can exceed savings; priority thrashing under resource contention wastes more time than it reclaims.

flow.title: Resource-Aware Scheduling
flow.description: Schedules AI tasks against live compute, thermal, and energy signals, prioritizing by deadline and preempting or degrading work to keep critical tasks on time. Shown through an autonomous vehicle balancing safety-critical perception against background workloads.

nodes.label:
🚗 AV Task Stream
Perception + planning workload

⚡ Resource-Aware Scheduler
Allocates compute by priority

🖥️ CPU Monitor
75% across 4 cores

🎮 GPU Monitor
60% AI accelerator

🌡️ Thermal Monitor
68C of 85C limit

🔋 Battery Monitor
45% remaining

🛑 Critical Tasks
Brake 8ms, obstacle 16ms

🔵 Important Tasks
Sign recognition 100ms

⚪ Optional Tasks
Map update 30s, entertainment

⏫ Preemption
Brake preempts non-critical

Hold optional under high load

-20% inference on heat

Power-saving models
