steps.title: Task Stream
steps.description: A continuous stream of perception and planning tasks arrives at the resource-aware scheduler.

steps.title: Resource Monitoring
steps.description: The scheduler polls CPU, GPU, thermal, and battery monitors to read the current operating envelope.

steps.title: Priority Classification
steps.description: Tasks are sorted into critical, important, and optional tiers, each with its own deadline.

steps.title: Preemptive Scheduling
steps.description: A safety-critical event such as emergency braking preempts all non-critical work immediately.

steps.title: Load-Based Deferral
steps.description: High CPU load causes the scheduler to defer optional tasks like map updates until capacity frees up.

steps.title: Thermal Throttling
steps.description: Rising temperature reduces inference frequency for important tasks to stay under the thermal limit.

steps.title: Energy-Aware Adaptive Quality
steps.description: Low battery switches important tasks to lighter, power-saving models while preserving safety.

steps.title: Deadline-Compliant Execution
steps.description: Critical and important tasks always run on time; optional tasks run only when spare capacity exists.

references: Clockwork: Predictable Low-Latency Inference (OSDI 2020)
Nexus: Multi-tenant Inference Serving (SOSP 2019)
INFaaS: Automated Model-less Inference Serving (ATC 2021)
Salus: Fine-Grained GPU Sharing
Gandiva: Introspective GPU Scheduler (OSDI 2018)

name: Progressive Enhancement(PE)
description: Incrementally improves AI output quality based on available resources and time

tldr.what: Delivers initial results quickly, then progressively refines output quality if time and resources remain available.
tldr.when: Interactive systems where users need fast feedback but benefit from better results if the agent has spare compute capacity.
tldr.watchOut: Intermediate outputs may mislead users into acting before refinement completes, or refinement may never finish under load.

flow.title: Progressive Enhancement
flow.description: An anytime pipeline that returns a usable result almost immediately and keeps improving quality in layers while resources and time allow. Context checkpoints and graceful degradation let it stop at any satisfactory level, shown with a photo enhancement app.

nodes.label:
🖼️ Raw Image
User uploads a photo

📈 Enhancement Engine
Anytime, layered pipeline

⚡ Baseline (50ms)
Noise reduction + contrast
Score 6/10

🔵 Standard (200ms)
+ Denoise + color correct
Score 7.5/10

🟣 High (800ms)
+ AI upscale + detail
Score 9/10

💎 Premium (3000ms)
+ Deep learning + artifact removal
Score 9.5/10

⚙️ Resource Monitor
CPU, battery, network

⏱️ Time Budget
Deadline + user patience

👤 User Preference
Quality vs speed

🎯 Quality Checkpoint
Good enough? stop or continue

🔻 Graceful Degradation
Low battery: cap at Standard

👁️ Instant Preview
Returned at 50ms

✨ Best Available Result
Returned at chosen level

steps.title: Upload and Instant Preview
steps.description: The baseline layer runs in 50ms and returns an immediate preview so the user never stares at a blank screen.

steps.title: Layered Enhancement Begins
steps.description: While the preview is shown, the pipeline advances to the standard-quality layer.

steps.title: Context-Aware Checkpoint
steps.description: A checkpoint weighs resources, remaining time budget, and user preference to decide whether to keep enhancing.

steps.title: Continue to Higher Quality
steps.description: With time and resources available, the checkpoint lets the pipeline proceed to the high-quality layer.

steps.title: Anytime Return
steps.description: Because each layer produces a complete result, the pipeline can return the current best output at high or premium quality.

steps.title: Graceful Degradation
steps.description: If the resource monitor reports low battery, the pipeline caps at the standard layer and returns that result instead of stalling.

steps.title: Best Available Result
steps.description: Whenever the checkpoint judges the output good enough, it stops and delivers the best result achieved so far.

references: Zilberstein (1996): The principles of anytime algorithms
Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding - https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192
Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling - https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01318
Shinn et al. (2023): Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback

name: Durable Execution & Checkpointing(DE)
description: Persists workflow and agent state at every step so long-running runs can crash-resume from the last checkpoint, replay deterministically without repeating completed work, pause and resume for human input, and time-travel by forking from an earlier checkpoint. Checkpointer-backed graph engines such as LangGraph and Temporal-style durable engines provide the substrate for reliable, long-lived, human-in-the-loop agents.
features: Crash recovery resumes from the last checkpoint
Time-travel: fork alternate runs from any checkpoint
Durable timers for long waits and retries

tldr.what: Persists workflow state after each step so crashes resume from the last checkpoint, replays skip completed work, and runs fork from earlier points.
tldr.when: Long-running multi-step work where crashes are costly, human approval is needed mid-flow, or you must retry without redoing finished steps.
tldr.watchOut: Checkpoint storage and serialization overhead can dominate runtime; non-deterministic steps (randomness, external calls) break replay guarantees.

flow.title: Durable Execution & Checkpointing
flow.description: A long-running agent persists state at every step so it can crash-resume from the last checkpoint, replay deterministically without repeating completed work, pause and resume for human input, and time-travel by forking from an earlier checkpoint. Substrate behind LangGraph checkpointers and Temporal-style durable engines.

nodes.label:
🎯 Run
40-step agent compiling a market report

⚙️ Durable Workflow Engine
LangGraph / Temporal-style

🗄️ Checkpointer / State Store
SQLite / Postgres, one write per step

🔢 Steps 1-22 executed
state saved after each step

💾 Checkpoint 22
{ sources: 18, draft: 60% }

💥 Step 23 CRASH
LLM API timeout, process dies

⏩ Deterministic Replay
completed steps skipped
no re-billing, no rework

♻️ Resume from Checkpoint 22
continue steps 23-40

⏸️ Human Interrupt @ step 31
approve / edit state

✏️ State Edited
budget 5M -> 8M, then resume

🌱 Time-Travel Fork
branch from checkpoint 18
alternate assumption

✨ Report completed
40/40 steps, main + forked branch archived

steps.title: Persist Every Step
steps.description: The run begins. The durable engine executes each step and writes the resulting state to the checkpointer, so no progress lives only in memory.

steps.title: Checkpoint 22 Written
steps.description: Steps 1-22 complete. The latest durable checkpoint records { sources: 18, draft: 60% }.

steps.title: Crash at Step 23
steps.description: Step 23 fails on an LLM API timeout and the live process dies. Without durability the whole run would restart from zero.

steps.title: Crash-Resume + Replay
steps.description: The engine reloads checkpoint 22 from the store and replays deterministically, skipping steps 1-22 (no re-billing, no rework), then continues 23-40.

steps.title: Human Interrupt
steps.description: At step 31 an interrupt pauses the run for review. A human edits state (budget 5M -> 8M); the edit is saved as a new checkpoint and the run resumes.

steps.title: Time-Travel Fork
steps.description: Separately, an alternate branch is forked from checkpoint 18 to test a different assumption without disturbing the main run.

steps.title: Completion
steps.description: The run finishes 40/40 steps. Both the main run and the forked branch are archived as replayable histories.

references: LangGraph Durable Execution - https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution
Temporal: Durable Execution meets AI - https://temporal.io/blog/durable-execution-meets-ai-why-temporal-is-the-perfect-foundation-for-ai

name: Reversible Actions & Compensation (Agent Saga)(Saga)
description: A pattern for making agent side effects safe to undo. Structure the trajectory as a saga: every forward action (book a flight, charge a card, create a record) is paired with a compensating action that reverses its business effect, and every tool is made idempotent with an idempotency key so a retry or a rollback produces the same end state instead of duplicating work. When a step fails partway through, the agent runs the compensations for the already-completed steps in reverse order rather than leaving the system half-applied. There is no automatic ACID rollback across services, so compensations are explicitly designed as the logical inverse of each action. Distinct from `durable-execution`: that persists and replays a run so it can continue to completion after a crash, whereas this defines how to semantically undo committed side effects when completion is no longer the right outcome.
features: Every forward action paired with a compensating action (semantic undo)
Idempotency keys make retries and rollbacks converge to the same end state
Ordered rollback of completed steps on mid-trajectory failure
Check-before-act and upsert guards prevent duplicate side effects
No automatic ACID rollback: compensations are explicitly authored
Distributed side effects modeled as a saga of local transactions

tldr.what: Pairs each forward action with an explicit compensating action that reverses its business effect, using idempotency keys to make retries and rollbacks converge to the same state.
tldr.when: Multi-step workflows across services where failures mid-trajectory require undoing already-committed side effects without automatic ACID rollback.
tldr.watchOut: Compensations must be authored correctly and remain available; a broken or missing compensation leaves the system in an inconsistent state with no automatic recovery.

flow.title: Reversible Actions & Compensation (Agent Saga)
flow.description: A travel-booking agent structures its side effects as a saga: each forward action registers a compensating action, and each tool call carries an idempotency key. When the hotel step fails, the agent rolls back the already-booked flight with an idempotent retry instead of leaving a half-applied trip.

nodes.label:
🧳 Booking Request
Flight, then hotel, then car

🎗️ Saga Orchestrator
Runs forward path, tracks compensations

🔑 Idempotency Store
One key per action

📚 Compensation Log
Registered undo stack

✈️ book_flight
key=trip-42-flight

🟢 Flight Booked
AF1234, $420

↩️ Register Compensation
cancel_flight(AF1234)

🏨 book_hotel
key=trip-42-hotel

❌ Hotel Failed
No availability for the dates

🔁 Rollback Trigger
Stop forward path, pop compensations

✈️ cancel_flight(AF1234)
key=trip-42-flight-cancel

⏱️ Attempt 1 Times Out
Retry with the same key

🧷 Idempotent Retry
API dedupes on key, no double refund

🟢 Flight Cancelled
One clean refund

✅ Consistent End State
Zero partial bookings, no double charge

steps.title: Start the Saga
steps.description: The orchestrator accepts the multi-step booking and sets up the two ingredients that make it reversible: an idempotency key per action and a compensation log for registered undo actions.

steps.title: Forward: Book Flight
steps.description: The flight books successfully (AF1234, $420). Before moving on, the agent registers its compensating action, cancel_flight(AF1234), onto the compensation log.

steps.title: Forward: Hotel Fails
steps.description: The next forward step, booking the hotel, fails: there is no availability for the requested dates. The trajectory is now half-applied with a live flight booking.

steps.title: Trigger Rollback
steps.description: Instead of retrying the whole trip or pressing on, the saga aborts the forward path and pops the registered compensations from the log to run them newest-first.

steps.title: Compensate: Cancel Flight
steps.description: The agent invokes cancel_flight(AF1234) with its own idempotency key. The first attempt times out, so the agent retries with the exact same key.

steps.title: Idempotent Retry
steps.description: The airline API dedupes on the idempotency key, so the retry returns the same cancellation rather than issuing a second refund or erroring. The flight is cleanly cancelled.

steps.title: Consistent End State
steps.description: The system lands in a clean state: zero partial bookings, one refund, and no double charge. Compensation undid the committed side effect instead of leaving it stranded.

references: Saga pattern (microservices.io) - https://microservices.io/patterns/data/saga.html
Saga Design Pattern Made Easy (Temporal) - https://temporal.io/blog/saga-pattern-made-easy
Idempotent Agent Operations: Safe to Retry (AgentPatterns) - https://www.agentpatterns.ai/agent-design/idempotent-agent-operations/

name: Latent Space Visualization(LSV)
description: Visualize and interpret AI reasoning processes in continuous latent spaces

tldr.what: Maps AI reasoning into visual 2D or 3D spaces, showing how concepts cluster and connect during problem-solving.
tldr.when: Debugging complex multi-step reasoning, validating model behavior on high-stakes tasks, or understanding failure patterns in generation.
tldr.watchOut: Visualizations can mislead; dimensionality reduction loses information, making apparent clusters meaningless or contradicting actual model decisions.

flow.title: Latent Space Visualization
flow.description: Project a model's internal activations into a low-dimensional map (UMAP / t-SNE), cluster them by concept, and trace the reasoning trajectory to reveal how an agent thinks and where it is biased.

nodes.label:
🎯 Input Prompt
"Plan a sustainable city"

🤖 Reasoning Agent
Generates chain-of-thought
over many hidden layers

🧠 Activation Capture
Hidden-state vectors
per token and layer

🗄️ Embedding Matrix
4096-dim activations
collected across steps

📉 Dimensionality Reduction
UMAP / t-SNE projects
4096-dim to 3D

🔮 Concept Clustering
k-means over projected
points -> semantic groups

⚡ Energy Cluster (green)
Solar, grid, storage
Dense, central

🚊 Transport Cluster (blue)
Transit, EV, bike lanes

🏘️ Housing Cluster (orange)
Density, materials
Tightly coupled to energy

💰 Economics Cluster (sparse)
Budget, jobs
Few, scattered points

🧭 Reasoning Trajectory
Energy -> Transport -> Integration

🖱️ Interactive Explorer
Zoom, hover, filter
clusters and paths

💡 Insight Panel
Bias + coupling detection
Technical over social

📄 Interpretability Report
Reasoning map + findings
for audit and debugging

steps.title: Capture Reasoning Activations
steps.description: As the agent reasons about the sustainable-city prompt, hidden-state vectors are recorded for each token and layer.

steps.title: Build the Embedding Matrix
steps.description: The captured 4096-dimensional activations are stacked into a single matrix spanning every reasoning step.

steps.title: Project to Low Dimensions
steps.description: UMAP or t-SNE reduces the high-dimensional matrix to a 3D map that preserves neighborhood structure.

steps.title: Cluster by Concept
steps.description: k-means groups the projected points into semantic clusters: dense energy, transport, and housing groups plus a sparse economics group.

steps.title: Trace the Reasoning Trajectory
steps.description: Following points in generation order reveals the path Energy -> Transport -> Integration, with housing tightly coupled to energy.

steps.title: Explore Interactively
steps.description: An analyst zooms, hovers, and filters the map to inspect individual clusters and how thoughts move between them.

steps.title: Surface Insights and Biases
steps.description: The panel flags that the model prioritizes energy first, strongly couples housing to energy, and barely considers economics, favoring technical over social solutions.

steps.title: Deliver Interpretability Report
steps.description: The reasoning map and findings are packaged into a report for auditing reasoning quality and debugging unexpected outputs.

references: Visualizing Data using t-SNE - van der Maaten & Hinton (JMLR 2008) - https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v9/vandermaaten08a.html
UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction - McInnes et al. (2018) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03426
The Building Blocks of Interpretability - Olah et al. (Distill 2018) - https://distill.pub/2018/building-blocks/

name: Contrastive Explanations(CE)
description: Explain AI decisions by showing what would change the outcome

tldr.what: Shows what input changes would flip an AI decision by finding minimal modifications to cross the decision boundary.
tldr.when: Users need to understand why they were rejected and what concrete actions could change the outcome, especially in high-stakes decisions.
tldr.watchOut: Counterfactuals may suggest unrealistic or unfair changes, misleading users about what's actually achievable or appropriate to attempt.

flow.title: Contrastive Explanations
flow.description: Explain a decision by showing what would flip it. A counterfactual search finds the minimal change to the inputs that turns a loan denial into an approval, then reports it as actionable guidance.

nodes.label:
🧑 Loan Application
Credit 580, income $60K
15% down payment

🏦 Underwriting Agent
Approve / Deny classifier

❌ Factual Outcome: DENIED
Driver: credit score 580
below 620 threshold

⚖️ Contrastive Engine
Search nearest inputs
that flip the outcome

📊 Feature Importance
Rank the decision drivers

🧭 Decision Boundary
Probe the APPROVE region

🔀 Counterfactual A
Credit 580 -> 620 (+40)

🔀 Counterfactual B
Income $60K -> $75K (+$15K)

🔀 Counterfactual C
Down 15% -> 25% (+10%)

✨ Minimal Change
+40 credit points
is the smallest flip

🟰 Non-Factors
Employment history OK
Debt-to-income acceptable

✅ Contrastive Outcome: APPROVED
if credit score >= 620

📄 Actionable Explanation
Steps that flip the decision

steps.title: Factual Decision
steps.description: The underwriting agent denies the application, naming the credit score of 580 as the driving factor.

steps.title: Invoke the Contrastive Engine
steps.description: Rather than restate the score, the engine asks what would have to differ for the model to approve instead.

steps.title: Rank Features and Probe the Boundary
steps.description: Feature importance ranks the drivers while a boundary probe searches for the nearest region where the outcome becomes APPROVE.

steps.title: Generate Counterfactuals
steps.description: Three candidate changes each cross the boundary: +40 credit points, +$15K income, or +10% down payment.

steps.title: Identify the Minimal Change
steps.description: Comparing the candidates, raising the credit score by 40 points is the smallest change that flips the decision.

steps.title: Confirm the Flipped Outcome
steps.description: With a credit score of 620 or above the model now approves, verifying the counterfactual is valid.

steps.title: Note What Did Not Matter
steps.description: Employment history and debt-to-income were already sufficient, so they are called out as factors that did not affect the outcome.

steps.title: Deliver Actionable Explanation
steps.description: The applicant receives concrete steps: pay down balances, correct report errors, and raise the score past 620.

references: Explanations based on the Missing: Towards Contrastive Explanations with Pertinent Negatives - Dhurandhar et al. (NeurIPS 2018) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.07623
Counterfactual Explanations without Opening the Black Box - Wachter et al. (2017) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.00399
Explanation in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Social Sciences - Miller (2017) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.07269

name: Causal Reasoning Transparency(CRT)
description: Make causal reasoning chains explicit and understandable

tldr.what: Explicitly maps cause-effect relationships with strength scores, identifies confounders, and predicts intervention effects to make reasoning auditable.
tldr.when: High-stakes decisions where stakeholders need to verify the agent's logic chain and understand which factors drove each conclusion.
tldr.watchOut: Causal strength scores and confounding factor lists can feel rigorous but remain subjective; users may over-trust numbers without validating assumptions.

flow.title: Causal Reasoning Transparency
flow.description: Expose the explicit causal chain behind an agent decision. Each cause-effect link carries a strength and an evidence source, mediators and confounders are made visible, and assumptions are stated openly.

nodes.label:
🩺 Patient Presentation
Chest pain + shortness of breath
Symptoms occur at rest

🤖 Diagnostic Agent
Builds an explicit causal chain

1️⃣ Observed Symptoms
Chest pain + dyspnea

🔗 Causal Link
Strength 0.85

2️⃣ Possible Cardiac Event
Acute coronary syndrome

🧬 Mediating Factors
Age 60, male, smoker
Raise cardiac risk

3️⃣ Risk Assessment
HIGH

💉 Intervention Effect
-70% risk if treated < 1 hour

🌀 Confounders Checked
Exercise (ruled out, at rest)
Anxiety, medication effects

🚑 Recommendation
Immediate emergency care

📚 Causal Assumptions
Age and gender raise risk
Time-to-treatment matters

🔬 Evidence Sources
Clinical literature cited
per causal link

📄 Transparency Report
Chain + strengths + evidence
+ stated assumptions

steps.title: Observe the Symptoms
steps.description: The agent takes the presentation of chest pain and shortness of breath at rest as the first node in the causal chain.

steps.title: Draw the Causal Link
steps.description: A quantified link of strength 0.85 connects the symptoms to a possible cardiac event, making the inference explicit rather than hidden.

steps.title: Account for Mediators
steps.description: Age 60, male sex, and smoking are surfaced as mediating factors that strengthen the path toward a cardiac hypothesis.

steps.title: Rule Out Confounders
steps.description: Exercise-induced symptoms are ruled out because they occur at rest; anxiety and medication effects are considered and set aside.

steps.title: Assess Risk
steps.description: With the cardiac path supported and confounders addressed, the chain resolves to a HIGH risk assessment.

steps.title: Predict the Intervention Effect
steps.description: The model projects that treatment within one hour reduces risk by roughly 70%, driving urgency.

steps.title: State Assumptions and Cite Evidence
steps.description: Every assumption (age, gender, time-to-treatment) is written out and each causal link is tied to a clinical evidence source.

steps.title: Deliver Transparency Report
steps.description: The full chain, its link strengths, cited evidence, and open assumptions are packaged so a clinician can audit the reasoning end to end.

references: Causal Reasoning and Large Language Models: Opening a New Frontier for Causality - Kiciman et al. (2023) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00050
Causality: Models, Reasoning, and Inference - Pearl (Cambridge University Press) - https://bayes.cs.ucla.edu/BOOK-2K/

name: Attention Flow Analysis(AFA)
description: Track and visualize where AI systems focus their attention during reasoning

tldr.what: Visualizes which inputs or reasoning steps an AI model prioritizes by mapping attention weights across layers, heads, and time steps.
tldr.when: Debugging unexpected model outputs, validating reasoning quality, or understanding why a system ignored relevant information.
tldr.watchOut: Attention patterns don't always reflect actual reasoning; high attention to a token doesn't guarantee it influenced the final decision.

flow.title: Attention Flow Analysis
flow.description: Trace where a transformer focuses by reading attention weights across tokens, sections, layers, and heads. Mapping the focus intensity of a summarization task reveals that methodology is under-attended.

nodes.label:
📄 Task
"Summarize this research paper"

🤖 Transformer Agent
Multi-head attention
over the full document

🔤 Tokenizer
Split document into
sections and tokens

👁️ Attention Extractor
Read weights per
layer and head

📝 Abstract
75% ██████

📖 Introduction
45% ████

🧪 Methods
25% ██ (low)

📊 Results
70% ██████

🎯 Conclusion
85% ████████

🔖 References
10% █ (low)

🧠 Multi-Head Analysis
Per-head focus map
across layers

⚠️ Anomaly Detector
Methods + references
under-attended

💡 Insight
Favors conclusions,
skips methodology

📄 Summary + Attention Report
Focus map with a caveat
on technical accuracy

steps.title: Receive the Summarization Task
steps.description: The agent is asked to summarize a research paper, and its multi-head attention will be inspected while it works.

steps.title: Tokenize the Document
steps.description: The paper is split into sections and tokens so attention can be attributed back to meaningful spans.

steps.title: Extract Attention Weights
steps.description: The extractor reads attention weights for every layer and head, ready to aggregate them by section.

steps.title: Map Focus Intensity per Section
steps.description: Aggregated weights show heavy focus on Title (90%), Conclusion (85%), and Abstract (75%), lighter focus on Results and Introduction, and little on Methods and References.

steps.title: Analyze Multi-Head Patterns
steps.description: Per-head maps across layers confirm the focus is concentrated on high-level framing rather than spread across the paper.

steps.title: Detect Attention Anomalies
steps.description: The detector flags Methods and References as anomalously under-attended for a technical summarization task.

steps.title: Surface the Insight
steps.description: The panel concludes the model favors conclusions and skips methodology, which risks missing important technical nuance.

steps.title: Deliver Summary with Caveat
steps.description: The summary ships alongside the focus map and a note to ask specifically about methods for technical accuracy.

references: Quantifying Attention Flow in Transformers - Abnar & Zuidema (ACL 2020) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.00928
Attention is not Explanation - Jain & Wallace (NAACL 2019) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10186
Attention is not not Explanation - Wiegreffe & Pinter (EMNLP 2019) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.04626

name: Uncertainty Quantification(UQ)
description: Quantify and communicate AI confidence and uncertainty in predictions

tldr.what: Separates model uncertainty from irreducible noise, then reports prediction ranges and confidence levels alongside point estimates.
tldr.when: High-stakes decisions where users need to know prediction reliability, or when downstream systems must adjust behavior based on confidence.
tldr.watchOut: Poorly calibrated intervals mislead users into false confidence; validation on held-out data is essential and often skipped.

flow.title: Uncertainty Quantification
flow.description: A medical-triage agent reports calibrated confidence instead of a bare label. It separates epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty, produces a calibrated confidence interval, and routes or abstains based on how sure it is.

nodes.label:
🧑 Triage Input
54yo, fever 39.2C, cough
O2 sat 91% on room air

🤖 Triage Agent
Predicts acuity plus
calibrated confidence

🎲 Model Ensemble
MC-dropout / deep ensemble
samples the prediction

🎯 Point Prediction
Pneumonia, ESI level 2

📉 Epistemic Uncertainty
Model + data gaps
±12% (reducible)

🎰 Aleatoric Uncertainty
Inherent case noise
±8% (irreducible)

📏 Confidence Interval
P(pneumonia) = 0.78
90% CI [0.66, 0.88]

⚖️ Calibration Check
Reliability diagram
Expected calib. error 0.03

🟢 High Confidence
Escalate: start
sepsis screen

🔴 Low Confidence
Flag: needs
chest X-ray

✋ Abstention Gate
Defer to clinician
if interval too wide

🚑 Risk-Adjusted Recommendation
Urgent workup, monitor O2

📄 Uncertainty Report
Calibrated probability
+ sources of doubt

steps.title: Receive Triage Input
steps.description: A patient presents with fever, cough, and a low oxygen saturation, and the agent must judge acuity under uncertainty.

steps.title: Sample with an Ensemble
steps.description: Monte Carlo dropout or a deep ensemble draws many predictions so their spread can quantify uncertainty.

steps.title: Produce a Point Prediction
steps.description: The mean of the samples gives a point prediction of pneumonia at ESI level 2.

steps.title: Decompose the Uncertainty
steps.description: The spread is split into epistemic uncertainty (reducible model and data gaps, ±12%) and aleatoric uncertainty (irreducible case noise, ±8%).

steps.title: Estimate a Confidence Interval
steps.description: Combining the sources yields a probability of pneumonia of 0.78 with a 90% confidence interval of 0.66 to 0.88.

steps.title: Check Calibration
steps.description: A reliability diagram confirms the stated probabilities match observed frequencies, with an expected calibration error of just 0.03.

steps.title: Route by Confidence or Abstain
steps.description: High-confidence findings escalate to a sepsis screen, low-confidence findings are flagged for a chest X-ray, and intervals too wide defer to a clinician.

steps.title: Deliver Risk-Adjusted Output
steps.description: The agent issues an urgent-workup recommendation with oxygen monitoring alongside a report of the calibrated probability and its sources of doubt.

references: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning - Gal & Ghahramani (ICML 2016) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02142
Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles - Lakshminarayanan et al. (NeurIPS 2017) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01474
On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks - Guo et al. (ICML 2017) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04599

name: RDF Knowledge Modeling(RDF)
description: Structured knowledge representation using Resource Description Framework for semantic data modeling and linking

tldr.what: Represents knowledge as subject-predicate-object triples with URIs, enabling machines to link and query structured semantic relationships.
tldr.when: You need interoperable, queryable knowledge graphs where entities and relationships must be unambiguous across systems.
tldr.watchOut: URI design and ontology choices lock in your schema; changing them later breaks existing links and queries across the graph.

flow.title: RDF Knowledge Modeling
flow.description: Structured knowledge representation using the Resource Description Framework. A source record is modeled as subject-predicate-object triples over shared namespaces and URIs, then assembled into a linked-data knowledge graph that machines can query and reason over.

nodes.label:
📄 Source Record
"Machine Learning in Healthcare"
by John Smith, Stanford, 2024

🕸️ RDF Modeling Agent
Map facts to triples

🔑 URI Minting
Assign stable resource identity
ex:paper123, ex:johnsmith

🟢 Subject Resource
ex:paper123 a ex:ResearchPaper

🔺 Triple: Title
ex:paper123 dc:title
"Machine Learning in Healthcare"

🔺 Triple: Creator
ex:paper123 dc:creator
ex:johnsmith

🔺 Triple: Subject
ex:paper123 dc:subject
ex:MachineLearning, ex:Healthcare

🔺 Triple: Citation
ex:paper123 ex:citedBy
ex:paper456

🔺 Triple: Affiliation
ex:johnsmith foaf:affiliation
ex:StanfordUniv

🗄️ Triple Store
Assemble RDF graph

📝 Turtle Serialization
Standards-based exchange

🌐 Linked-Data Knowledge Graph
Machine-queryable research network

steps.title: Ingest Source Record
steps.description: A source fact (a research paper and its author) enters the modeling agent as free-form data to be turned into structured triples.

steps.title: Declare Namespaces
steps.description: Shared vocabularies are bound to prefixes (ex:, foaf:, dc:) so that terms resolve to global, reusable URIs rather than local strings.

steps.title: Mint URIs and Type the Subject
steps.description: Each real-world entity is given a stable URI. The paper becomes ex:paper123, typed with the triple ex:paper123 a ex:ResearchPaper.

steps.title: Assert Triples About the Paper
steps.description: Facts are expressed as subject-predicate-object statements: title, creator, subject topics, and citations, all hanging off ex:paper123.

steps.title: Model Linked Entities
steps.description: The creator URI is expanded into its own resource: ex:johnsmith a foaf:Person with a name and an affiliation, linking the paper into a wider graph.

steps.title: Assemble the Triple Store
steps.description: All asserted triples are merged into a single RDF graph where shared URIs automatically join facts about papers, people, and institutions.

steps.title: Serialize as Turtle
steps.description: The graph is written out in Turtle using the declared prefixes, producing a standards-compliant, portable representation for exchange.

steps.title: Query the Linked Data
steps.description: A SPARQL query traverses the triples to answer questions such as which papers John Smith authored, yielding a machine-queryable knowledge graph.

references: RDF 1.1 Concepts and Abstract Syntax - W3C Recommendation - https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-concepts/
RDF 1.1 Primer - W3C Working Group Note - https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-primer/

name: SHACL Constraint Validation(SHACL)
description: Shapes Constraint Language for validating RDF data against defined schemas and business rules

tldr.what: Validates RDF data against declarative shape definitions specifying cardinality, type, and custom constraints on properties.
tldr.when: RDF knowledge graphs need schema enforcement, data quality gates, or compliance checks before downstream processing.
tldr.watchOut: Complex nested shapes and custom validation rules become brittle and expensive to debug when constraints interact unexpectedly.

flow.title: SHACL Constraint Validation
flow.description: Shapes Constraint Language validates RDF data against declared node and property shapes before it is admitted to the graph. Agent-extracted patient facts are checked for datatype, cardinality, pattern, and value constraints, and only conforming records are inserted.

nodes.label:
📥 Agent-Extracted Records
ex:pat1 ex:patientId "P123456"
ex:pat2 ex:patientId "P12"

✅ SHACL Validation Engine
Validate data graph vs shapes graph

🔒 Property: patientId
sh:datatype xsd:string
sh:minCount 1 ; sh:maxCount 1
sh:pattern "^P[0-9]{6}$"

🔒 Property: birthDate
sh:datatype xsd:date
sh:minCount 1
sh:lessThan ex:admissionDate

🔒 Property: medicalRecord
sh:node ex:MedicalRecordShape
sh:minCount 1

🟢 Record ex:pat1
patientId "P123456"
birthDate 1980-05-02

🔴 Record ex:pat2
patientId "P12"
birthDate after admissionDate

✔️ Conforms: true
All constraints satisfied

⛔ Violation
sh:PatternConstraintComponent
patientId "P12" fails ^P[0-9]{6}$

⛔ Violation
sh:LessThanConstraintComponent
birthDate not < admissionDate

📋 sh:ValidationReport
sh:conforms false
2 result(s), severity sh:Violation

🗄️ Insert to Knowledge Graph
Conforming records only

🚫 Quarantine
Reject and route for repair

steps.title: Receive Candidate Records
steps.description: Facts an extraction agent proposes for the graph arrive as an RDF data graph, including one well-formed patient and one malformed one.

steps.title: Load the Target Shape
steps.description: The engine selects ex:PatientShape, a sh:NodeShape whose sh:targetClass ex:Patient tells it which nodes in the data graph to validate.

steps.title: Expand Property Constraints
steps.description: The shape unfolds into property constraints: a pattern and cardinality on patientId, a datatype and lessThan rule on birthDate, and a nested shape on medicalRecord.

steps.title: Evaluate Each Record
steps.description: Every focus node is checked against every constraint. Record pat1 satisfies the pattern and nested record shape; pat2 is tested against the same rules.

steps.title: Detect Violations
steps.description: pat1 conforms. pat2 raises two results: a PatternConstraintComponent on "P12" and a LessThanConstraintComponent because birthDate is not before admissionDate.

steps.title: Emit the Validation Report
steps.description: A sh:ValidationReport aggregates the results with sh:conforms false and per-focus-node details at sh:Violation severity for downstream handling.

steps.title: Gate the Knowledge Graph
steps.description: Only conforming records are inserted into the graph; the non-conforming record is quarantined and routed back for repair, keeping the graph clean.

references: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL) - W3C Recommendation - https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/
SHACL Advanced Features - W3C Working Group Note - https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl-af/

name: OWL Ontological Reasoning(OWL)
description: Web Ontology Language for defining complex semantic relationships and enabling automated logical reasoning

tldr.what: Defines formal semantic relationships and class hierarchies, then applies logical rules to automatically infer new facts and validate consistency.
tldr.when: Complex domains with strict taxonomies where you need automated classification, constraint validation, or derivation of implicit knowledge from explicit rules.
tldr.watchOut: Reasoning performance degrades sharply with ontology size and rule complexity; misaligned axioms cause silent inconsistencies hard to debug.

flow.title: OWL Ontological Reasoning
flow.description: Web Ontology Language defines class hierarchies and property restrictions that let a description-logic reasoner infer new facts. Given only a patient's asserted symptoms, the reasoner classifies the patient's condition, checks consistency, and materializes entailed triples.

nodes.label:
🩺 Asserted Facts (ABox)
med:p1 med:hasSymptom med:HighBloodSugar
med:p1 med:hasSymptom med:InsulinResistance

🦉 OWL Ontology (TBox)
Formal class & property axioms

📚 Classes
med:Patient a owl:Class
med:Symptom a owl:Class
med:Treatment a owl:Class

🔗 Object Properties
med:hasSymptom rdfs:domain Patient
med:treatedBy rdfs:range Treatment

🧩 Axiom: DiabeticPatient
med:DiabeticPatient rdfs:subClassOf med:Patient ,
[ owl:onProperty med:hasSymptom ;
  owl:someValuesFrom med:HighBloodSugar ]

🧩 Axiom: Type2DiabeticPatient
owl:equivalentClass owl:intersectionOf (
  med:DiabeticPatient
  [ hasSymptom some med:InsulinResistance ] )

🧠 OWL Reasoner
HermiT / Pellet DL engine

🟠 Consistency Check
Ontology is satisfiable

🗂️ Classification
Subsumption: match p1 symptoms
to class restrictions

❌ Inconsistency Guard
Flag if disjoint classes both hold

💠 Inferred
med:p1 a med:DiabeticPatient
(HighBloodSugar restriction met)

💠 Inferred
med:p1 a med:Type2DiabeticPatient
(InsulinResistance restriction met)

💠 Inferred
med:p1 med:treatedBy
med:InsulinTherapy

🌐 Materialized Inferences
Entailed triples added to graph

steps.title: Assert Ground Facts
steps.description: Only raw observations are stated: patient p1 has the symptoms HighBloodSugar and InsulinResistance. No disease class is asserted directly.

steps.title: Load the Ontology Schema
steps.description: The TBox supplies the vocabulary: the Patient, Symptom, and Treatment classes plus the domain and range of hasSymptom and treatedBy.

steps.title: Read the Defining Axioms
steps.description: DiabeticPatient is defined as a Patient with some HighBloodSugar symptom; Type2DiabeticPatient is equivalent to a DiabeticPatient that also has some InsulinResistance.

steps.title: Check Consistency
steps.description: The reasoner first proves the combined TBox and ABox are satisfiable; the disjointness guard would fire if contradictory class memberships were entailed.

steps.title: Classify by Subsumption
steps.description: The reasoner matches p1's symptoms against the class restrictions, computing which defined classes the individual necessarily belongs to.

steps.title: Infer Class Membership
steps.description: Because p1 has HighBloodSugar it is inferred to be a DiabeticPatient; because it also has InsulinResistance it satisfies the equivalent-class definition of Type2DiabeticPatient.

steps.title: Entail Downstream Facts
steps.description: From the Type2Diabetes classification the reasoner derives a treatment relationship, showing how one inference cascades into further entailed triples.

steps.title: Materialize Inferences
steps.description: The entailed triples are written back into the graph so downstream queries see the derived disease and treatment facts alongside the asserted ones.

references: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Document Overview - W3C Recommendation - https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-overview/
OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Primer - W3C Recommendation - https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-primer/

name: Knowledge Graph Construction(KGC)
description: Systematic construction of knowledge graphs from structured and unstructured data sources

tldr.what: Extracts entities and relationships from multiple data sources, then links and organizes them into a queryable graph structure.
tldr.when: You need to connect information across structured databases, unstructured text, and APIs to enable relationship queries and reasoning.
tldr.watchOut: Entity linking errors compound through the graph; one misidentified entity can corrupt downstream relationships and queries.

flow.title: Knowledge Graph Construction
flow.description: Systematic assembly of a knowledge graph from heterogeneous sources. Structured, semi-structured, and unstructured inputs flow through entity extraction, linking, relationship discovery, schema alignment, and fusion, with quality checks before triples land in an e-commerce product graph.

nodes.label:
🗃️ Product Database
Structured catalog rows

💬 Customer Reviews
Unstructured text

📦 Supplier Feeds
Semi-structured XML/CSV

📈 Market APIs
Real-time pricing

🔗 KG Construction Pipeline
Orchestrate ingestion to graph

🔍 Entity Extraction
NER over sources
"iPhone 15", "Apple", "Camera"

🎯 Entity Linking
Disambiguate to canonical URIs
"Apple" to ex:Apple

🕸️ Relationship Discovery
hasFeature, manufacturedBy,
competesWith

🧭 Schema Alignment
Map codes to standard IDs
Normalize brands & categories

⚗️ Entity Fusion
Merge duplicates
ex:Apple = "Apple Inc."

🟠 Quality Assurance
Consistency, dedup,
referential integrity

⛔ Conflict Flagged
Contradictory price / broken ref

💠 ex:iPhone15 a ex:Smartphone ;
ex:brand ex:Apple

💠 ex:iPhone15 ex:hasFeature
ex:AdvancedCamera , ex:LongBattery

🌐 E-commerce Knowledge Graph
Recommendations, competitor analysis, search

steps.title: Integrate Multiple Sources
steps.description: Structured product rows, unstructured reviews, semi-structured supplier feeds, and real-time market APIs are all routed into a single construction pipeline.

steps.title: Extract Entities
steps.description: Named-entity recognition pulls candidate mentions from every source: products like iPhone 15, brands like Apple, and features like Camera.

steps.title: Link Mentions to URIs
steps.description: Each surface mention is disambiguated and resolved to a canonical resource, so every spelling of "Apple" collapses onto ex:Apple.

steps.title: Discover Relationships
steps.description: The pipeline mines predicates between linked entities: hasFeature, manufacturedBy, and competesWith connect products to features, brands, and rivals.

steps.title: Align Schema and Fuse Entities
steps.description: Product codes map to standard identifiers and category hierarchies are normalized, then duplicate nodes are fused so one entity is not represented twice.

steps.title: Assess Quality
steps.description: Consistency, deduplication, and referential-integrity checks gate the candidate triples; contradictions such as conflicting prices are flagged for review.

steps.title: Emit Product Triples
steps.description: Validated statements are written: iPhone 15 is a Smartphone made by Apple, with camera and battery features and a competes-with link to the Galaxy S24.

steps.title: Publish the Knowledge Graph
steps.description: The accumulated triples form an incremental product graph that powers recommendations, competitor analysis, and richer semantic search.

references: Knowledge Graphs - Hogan et al. (ACM Computing Surveys 2021) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.02320
A Survey on Knowledge Graphs: Representation, Acquisition and Applications - Ji et al. (2020) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00388

name: Semantic Data Validation(SDV)
description: Multi-layered validation of semantic data using ontological constraints, business rules, and logical consistency checks

tldr.what: Validates data against ontological schemas, business rules, and logical constraints across multiple layers to catch semantic violations.
tldr.when: Complex domains with strict compliance requirements, cross-entity relationships, or temporal dependencies that simple type checking misses.
tldr.watchOut: High implementation cost and maintenance burden; rule conflicts and constraint interactions often surface only in production.

flow.title: Semantic Data Validation
flow.description: Multi-layered validation of semantic data against ontological constraints, business rules, temporal constraints, and cross-references. Agent-asserted facts are grounded and checked for logical consistency before a compliance decision and audit trail are produced.

nodes.label:
🔍 Semantic Validation Orchestrator
Run layered checks in order

📐 Layer 1: Ontology
amount someValuesFrom xsd:decimal
currency owl:cardinality 1

📜 Layer 2: Business Rules (SWRL)
amount > 10000
-> requiresApproval(?t, true)

⏱️ Layer 3: Temporal
transactionDate < settlementDate
reportingDate <= today

🔗 Layer 4: Cross-Reference
Account exists, KYC status,
AML blacklist screening

🟠 Grounding Check
Facts map to known ontology terms

🟠 Consistency Check
No contradictory entailments

🟢 Layer 1 Pass
Structure valid

⚠️ WARNING: AMOUNT_THRESHOLD
Large transaction requires approval
suggestion: add approval workflow

⛔ CRITICAL: AML_SCREENING
Transaction involves sanctioned entity
entity: fin:t12345

📋 Validation Report (JSON)
validationStatus: "failed"
1 critical, 1 warning

🗄️ Audit Trail
Signed, timestamped decision log

🚫 Reject & Escalate
Block settlement, notify officer

steps.title: Receive Agent Knowledge
steps.description: The orchestrator ingests facts an agent asserted about a transaction: a 15000 amount in USD that must be validated before it is trusted or settled.

steps.title: Layer 1: Ontological Constraints
steps.description: The structure is checked against the ontology: amount must be a decimal and currency must have exactly cardinality one. The facts are well-typed.

steps.title: Layer 2: Business Rules
steps.description: A SWRL rule fires: because amount exceeds 10000, the transaction is entailed to require approval, raising an AMOUNT_THRESHOLD warning.

steps.title: Layer 3: Temporal Constraints
steps.description: Date ordering is verified: transactionDate must precede settlementDate and reportingDate must not be in the future, keeping the timeline coherent.

steps.title: Layer 4: Cross-Reference Screening
steps.description: External references are consulted: account existence, customer KYC status, and AML blacklist screening, which flags the counterparty as a sanctioned entity.

steps.title: Compile Multi-Level Report
steps.description: Results across layers are merged into a JSON report with validationStatus failed, one critical AML error and one threshold warning, each tagged to its rule.

steps.title: Decide, Log, and Escalate
steps.description: The critical violation blocks settlement and escalates to a compliance officer, while the full decision is written to a timestamped audit trail.

references: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL) - W3C Recommendation - https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/
JSON Schema Specification - https://json-schema.org/specification

name: Adaptive Compute Scaling(ACS)
description: Dynamically adjusts computational resources based on workload demands and performance requirements

tldr.what: Monitors workload metrics in real time and automatically adds or removes computational resources to maintain performance targets while controlling costs.
tldr.when: Services face unpredictable traffic spikes, variable computational demands, or need to balance performance guarantees against infrastructure spend.
tldr.watchOut: Scaling decisions lag behind demand changes, causing cascading failures or wasted resources if thresholds and prediction models are poorly tuned.

flow.title: Adaptive Compute Scaling
flow.description: Dynamically dials test-time compute up or down per query and scales serving infrastructure in real time, spending heavy reasoning only where a query is hard while keeping easy traffic cheap and fast.

nodes.label:
📥 Incoming Queries
45 requests queued
Mixed difficulty

📊 Resource Monitor
CPU 85% | Mem 77%
Queue 45 | p95 1.2s

🧭 Difficulty Classifier
Scores each query 0-1
Routes to a compute tier

🟢 Easy (score < 0.3)
"What is 2 + 2?"
1 pass, 0 reasoning tokens

🟡 Medium (0.3 - 0.7)
"Summarize a 5-page doc"
1 pass + 2k reasoning tokens

🔴 Hard (score > 0.7)
"Prove the theorem"
8 samples + 32k reasoning

🎛️ Compute Scheduler
Allocates test-time budget
& runs best-of-N

🎯 Quality Guard
Stop reasoning early when
confidence > 0.95

⚖️ Autoscaler
Scale up +2 instances
when CPU > 80% & queue > 30

🖥️ GPU Pool
4 to 6 A100 instances
Load balanced

💸 Spot Instances
Burst capacity
70% cheaper

🚨 Budget Cap Hit
Hard queries throttled
Downgrade to 4 samples

🔮 Predictive Scaler
+40% load forecast at 2pm
Pre-warm at 1:45pm

✅ Responses Served
p95 450ms | $18/hr
Quality maintained 98%

steps.title: Query Intake & Monitoring
steps.description: Requests arrive while the resource monitor tracks CPU, memory, queue depth, and p95 latency in real time.

steps.title: Difficulty Classification
steps.description: Each query is scored 0-1 and routed to an easy, medium, or hard tier so compute matches the work required.

steps.title: Test-Time Compute Allocation
steps.description: The scheduler sets the reasoning budget per tier: 0 tokens for easy, 2k for medium, and best-of-8 with 32k reasoning for hard.

steps.title: Infrastructure Autoscaling
steps.description: CPU at 85% and queue depth above 30 trigger the autoscaler to add 2 GPU instances, backed by cheaper spot capacity.

steps.title: Predictive Pre-Warming
steps.description: A forecast of +40% load at 2pm pre-warms instances at 1:45pm, avoiding cold-start latency and saving ~30% on emergency scaling.

steps.title: Quality Gate & Budget Caps
steps.description: The quality guard halts extra reasoning once confidence passes 0.95, and a budget cap throttles the hard tier down to 4 samples when spend runs high.

steps.title: Responses Served
steps.description: The right amount of compute per query lands p95 at 450ms and holds cost at $18/hr while quality stays at 98%.

references: Scryer: Netflix Predictive Autoscaling (ACM, 2018)
Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention - https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180

name: Cost-Aware Model Selection(CAMS)
description: Intelligently selects AI models based on cost-performance trade-offs for specific tasks

tldr.what: Routes requests to different models based on cost-performance trade-offs, switching dynamically when quality thresholds or budget limits are approached.
tldr.when: Applications with variable task importance, strict budget constraints, or mixed workloads where some requests tolerate cheaper models.
tldr.watchOut: Quality degradation on edge cases when cheaper models are selected; inconsistent outputs across model tiers confuse downstream systems.

flow.title: Cost-Aware Model Selection
flow.description: A smart router picks the cheapest model that still clears the quality bar for each task, escalating from Haiku to Sonnet to Opus by difficulty while respecting a live budget and logging the exact model version served.

steps.title: Task Intake
steps.description: A high-volume workload of 12,000 support tickets/day arrives and the router estimates difficulty and the quality bar it must hit.

steps.title: Cost/Quality Analysis
steps.description: The analyzer combines live per-token prices and remaining budget to score each candidate model on expected quality versus cost.

steps.title: Tier Selection
steps.description: Simple work routes to Haiku ($0.25/Mtok in), standard work to Sonnet, and only high-stakes reasoning to Opus ($15/Mtok in).

steps.title: Task Routing by Difficulty
steps.description: Sentiment classification lands on Haiku, doc summarization on Sonnet, and legal contract review on Opus.

steps.title: Quality Gate & Escalation
steps.description: Each result is checked against the eval set; anything under 0.90 is re-run one tier up so a cheap model never ships a failing answer.

steps.title: Budget Guardrail
steps.description: At 77% of the $200 daily cap, the guardrail tells the analyzer to downgrade standard tasks to Haiku while still passing quality checks.

steps.title: Serve & Monitor

name: Energy-Efficient Inference(EEI)
description: Optimizes AI inference for minimal energy consumption while maintaining performance

tldr.what: Reduces energy use during inference by lowering precision, scaling hardware frequency, compressing models, and batching requests together.
tldr.when: Mobile or edge devices with limited battery, thermal constraints, or high inference volume where power consumption directly impacts cost or runtime.
tldr.watchOut: Aggressive optimization degrades accuracy or latency unpredictably; measure both before and after on your actual hardware and workload.

flow.title: Energy-Efficient Inference
flow.description: On-device AI stretches battery and stays cool by batching similar requests, quantizing weights, exiting early on easy inputs, and placing work on the NPU, all under a power budget and thermal guard.

nodes.label:
📥 Inference Requests
120 req/s on-device
Battery 25% | 42°C

🔋 Power Monitor
Battery 25% | 42°C
Power budget 3.5W

🧭 Energy Scheduler
Picks precision, batch,
& hardware target

📦 Batch Optimizer
Group similar requests
Batch 8, +3ms wait

🔢 Quantizer
FP32 to INT8
4x smaller, 3.8x less energy

🚪 Early-Exit Layers
Simple inputs exit at
layer 6 of 24

🧪 Distilled Model
Student 60% pruned
Teacher-guided

🗃️ Prediction Cache
Reuse hot results
34% hit rate

⚡ Hardware Placement
NPU matmul 8 TOPS/W
CPU idled

🎚️ DVFS Governor
CPU 2.4 to 1.8GHz
Throttle on heat

🌡️ Thermal Guard

Drop batch, lower clock

🎯 Accuracy Check
Hold >= 95% of FP32
else keep FP16

🧩 Batched Workload
8 requests on NPU
INT8, layers 1-6

✅ Served On-Device
70% less energy
3x battery, 32°C

steps.title: Request Intake & Power Budget
steps.description: On-device traffic hits 120 req/s while the power monitor reports 25% battery, 42°C, and a 3.5W ceiling to the scheduler.

steps.title: Energy-Aware Strategy Selection
steps.description: The scheduler fans out four energy levers: batching, quantization, early-exit, and NPU placement.

steps.title: Model Compression
steps.description: Weights drop from FP32 to INT8 for 4x smaller memory and 3.8x less energy, distillation prunes 60% of parameters, and an accuracy check reverts to FP16 if quality falls below 95% of FP32.

steps.title: Batching & Early Exit
steps.description: Similar requests are grouped into batches of 8 with a 3ms wait, hot results are reused from a cache at a 34% hit rate, and simple inputs exit at layer 6 of 24.

steps.title: Hardware Placement & DVFS
steps.description: Matrix multiplies move to the NPU at 8 TOPS/W and the DVFS governor drops the idle CPU from 2.4GHz to 1.8GHz.

steps.title: Thermal Management
steps.description: At 42°C above the 40°C limit, the thermal guard shrinks the batch and lowers the clock to shed heat before throttling gets worse.

steps.title: Efficient Serving
steps.description: The tuned workload ships with 70% less energy, roughly 3x battery life, and a 10°C cooler device while holding ~95% of original accuracy.

references: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post‑Training Quantization for LLMs (2022)
AWQ: Activation‑Aware Weight Quantization for LLMs (2023)

name: Memory Optimization(MO)
description: Efficiently manages memory usage through caching, compression, and garbage collection strategies

tldr.what: Reduces memory footprint by caching frequent data, compressing stored values, and freeing unused allocations during runtime.
tldr.when: Systems handling large datasets or models where available RAM is significantly smaller than working set size.
tldr.watchOut: Aggressive compression or eviction can degrade latency unpredictably if cache miss rates spike under load.

flow.title: Memory Optimization
flow.description: Serving a 175B model whose 350GB of weights will not fit in 80GB of GPU memory, this flow combines quantization, sharding, dynamic layer loading, and paged KV-cache management, guarded by an out-of-memory watchdog and a garbage collector.

steps.title: Load Request & Memory Budget
steps.description: A request to serve a 175B model with 350GB of weights meets 80GB of GPU memory; the manager reads current usage from the monitor.

steps.title: Weight Quantization
steps.description: Weights are quantized from FP16 to INT4, shrinking the model from 350GB to roughly 88GB so far more fits in VRAM.

steps.title: Sharding & Memory Pool
steps.description: The model is split across 8 GPUs with pipeline parallelism, and a memory pool pre-allocates common tensor sizes to cut fragmentation.

steps.title: Dynamic Layer Loading
steps.description: Hot layers stay in VRAM while cold layers are swapped to NVMe SSD at 6GB/s and paged back in on demand.

steps.title: KV-Cache Optimization
steps.description: Paged attention stores KV in 16-token blocks shared across 1000 sequences, and block-sparse plus sliding-window compression bounds the cache to an 8k window.

steps.title: OOM Guard & Garbage Collection
steps.description: At 98% usage the watchdog evicts cold layers and old KV entries while the GC tuner defrags the pool to reclaim 9GB.

steps.title: Optimized Serving
steps.description: The combined techniques cut memory use by 80%, raise throughput 5x, and hold p50 latency near 50ms for 10x more concurrent users.

references: vLLM: Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention (2023)
QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs (2023) - https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314
ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion-Parameter Models (2019) - https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02054
FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Memory Utilization (2023)

name: Latency Optimization(LO)
description: Minimizes response time through predictive loading, caching, and request optimization

tldr.what: Reduces response time by prefetching likely models, caching frequent responses, batching requests, and processing asynchronously.
tldr.when: User-facing systems where sub-second latency matters, especially voice assistants, real-time chat, or high-traffic APIs.
tldr.watchOut: Aggressive prefetching and caching consume memory and may serve stale data if invalidation logic fails.

flow.title: Latency Optimization
flow.description: A real-time voice assistant hits sub-200ms responses by serving from a semantic cache, prefetching warm models, speculative decoding, continuous batching, parallel tool calls, and edge deployment, with an SLO guard that escalates on breach.

steps.description: A voice request arrives with a sub-200ms target while the monitor feeds live p95 and cache hit rate back to the router.

steps.title: Semantic Cache Lookup
steps.description: The router checks a semantic cache first; a >0.95 embedding match returns in 5ms and 78% of traffic never touches a model.

steps.title: Predictive Prefetch & Warm Pool
steps.description: Session patterns prefetch the likely next models into a warm pool and an edge PoP so there is no cold start on a miss.

steps.title: Continuous Batching
steps.description: On the 22% cache miss, the example query joins a continuous batch with a 4ms wait that lifts throughput ~3x.

steps.title: Speculative Decoding
steps.description: A small draft model proposes 4 tokens at a time that the target verifies in one pass, generating ~2.1x faster.

steps.title: Parallel Tool Calls

steps.title: SLO Guard & Edge Escalation

steps.title: Streamed Response

name: Sleep-Time Compute(STC)
description: Use idle time between user interactions to do background reasoning instead of waiting for the next query. The agent reorganizes and compresses memory, precomputes likely-needed inferences, and pre-answers anticipated questions so work is shifted off the latency-critical path. At inference time the answer is largely ready, cutting test-time compute and latency.
features: Latency shifted off the critical path

tldr.what: Performs reasoning and inference during idle periods between user interactions, precomputing answers and reorganizing memory to reduce latency when queries arrive.
tldr.when: Sporadic user interactions with large, stable context where background compute capacity exists and query patterns are somewhat predictable.
tldr.watchOut: Precomputed answers become stale or wrong if context changes between idle time and query, wasting both compute and user trust.

flow.title: Sleep-Time Compute
flow.description: Use idle time between interactions for background reasoning. The agent reorganizes memory, precomputes likely-needed inferences, and pre-answers anticipated questions, storing a learned context. The next query is answered instantly off the latency-critical path.

steps.title: Context Accumulates
steps.description: The agent holds a large, slowly changing context: a codebase, a document set, the day's notes. Queries arrive only sporadically.

steps.title: Idle Window Detected
steps.description: With no user activity for minutes or overnight, spare compute is available off the critical path, so the idle detector wakes the sleep-time agent.

steps.title: Background Reasoning
steps.description: The agent reorganizes memory (dedupe, merge, compress), precomputes inferences (which modules changed and what depends on them), and pre-answers the summaries the user usually asks for.

steps.title: Store the Learned Context
steps.description: All three outputs are written into a stored, queryable learned context, ready before the next interaction.

steps.title: Morning Query Answered Instantly
steps.description: The query "What broke in the refactor?" is assembled from the precomputed dependency analysis and change summary rather than derived from scratch.

steps.title: Off-Path Payoff
steps.description: Moving reasoning off the critical path yields about 5x less test-time compute for the same accuracy and up to 13% and 18% accuracy gains (on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME respectively) at a fixed budget, amortized further when many queries share the context.

references: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time - https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13171

name: Semantic Caching(SCA)
description: Cache LLM or agent responses keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact string match, so semantically equivalent queries reuse a stored answer. A similarity threshold decides a hit, a freshness TTL bounds staleness, and an invalidation policy evicts entries when source data changes. This cuts cost and latency on high-volume traffic and is distinct from prompt-prefix or KV caching.
features: Cost and latency reduction at high volume

tldr.what: Caches LLM responses by embedding similarity rather than exact text match, reusing answers when new queries exceed a similarity threshold.
tldr.when: High-volume query workloads where many semantically equivalent questions repeat and cost or latency reduction matters more than freshness.
tldr.watchOut: Similarity threshold tuning is brittle; too low causes stale answers on drifted topics, too high misses valid cache hits.

flow.title: Semantic Caching
flow.description: Cache LLM responses keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact string match. A support bot serves two different phrasings of the same intent from one cache entry at 0.93 similarity, with a similarity threshold, freshness TTL, and invalidation policy.

steps.title: Query Arrives and Is Embedded
steps.description: The support bot receives "reset my password" and embeds it into a vector for similarity lookup rather than an exact string match.

steps.title: Nearest-Neighbor Cache Lookup
steps.description: A nearest-neighbor search over the cache store finds an existing entry, "how do I change my password?", at cosine similarity 0.93.

steps.title: Threshold Check
steps.description: The similarity 0.93 clears the 0.90 hit threshold, so the two phrasings are treated as the same intent and served from one entry.

steps.title: Cache Hit Served
steps.description: On a hit the stored answer is returned directly without calling the LLM: p50 latency of about 40ms versus 2.1s for a fresh generation.

steps.title: Miss Path and Write-Back
steps.description: When similarity is below threshold it is a miss: the LLM generates the answer, then the new (embedding -> answer) pair is written back into the cache store.

steps.title: Freshness, Invalidation, and Outcome
steps.description: A 24h TTL bounds staleness and a policy-doc update evicts matching entries. Across real traffic this yields a high hit rate and a large latency and token-cost reduction. Distinct from prompt-prefix / KV caching.

GPT Semantic Cache: Reducing LLM Costs and Latency via Semantic Embedding Caching - https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05276

name: Budget-Guarded Autonomy(BGA)
description: Hard, enforced per-task and per-session budgets on tokens, dollars, wall-clock time, and tool-call count that are checked before each call and pause or terminate execution, rather than after-the-fact cost alerts. Mechanisms include pre-flight budget checks that raise a budget-exceeded stop before the next call reaches the provider, a token-velocity circuit breaker that trips on runaway loops, loop detectors that halt no-progress cycles, and delegated budget ceilings where a parent agent grants a child a spend cap the child cannot exceed. Distinct from `cost-aware-model-selection`, which routes to cheaper models to lower unit cost but does not enforce a ceiling or halt spend.
features: Pre-flight enforcement: budget checked before the next call, not after spend
Hard caps on tokens, dollars, wall-clock time, and tool-call count
Token-velocity circuit breaker trips on runaway or ping-ponging loops
Loop detection halts repeated no-progress cycles
Delegated ceilings: a parent grants a child a spend cap it cannot exceed
Pause-with-state on breach so a human can raise the cap or kill the run

tldr.what: Enforces hard ceilings on tokens, dollars, time, and tool calls before each execution step, halting or pausing when limits are reached.
tldr.when: Autonomous agents running unsupervised tasks where runaway loops, token bloat, or unexpected costs pose real financial or operational risk.
tldr.watchOut: Overly tight budgets starve legitimate work; undersized caps breed false alarms and frequent pauses that frustrate users and waste engineering time.

flow.title: Budget-Guarded Autonomy
flow.description: Hard per-task budgets on tokens, dollars, time, and tool calls, checked before each call rather than after. A token-velocity circuit breaker and loop detector catch runaway loops, delegated ceilings cap sub-agents, and a breach degrades to a safe pause with checkpointed state instead of a surprise invoice.

steps.title: Task Granted a Hard Budget
steps.description: The research task is admitted with an enforced ceiling: $2.00, 10 minutes of wall-clock, and 40 tool calls. A budget guard and a running ledger sit in front of the agent.

steps.title: Pre-Flight Check Admits Each Call
steps.description: Before every model or tool call the guard compares projected spend against the ceiling and admits it only if it stays under budget. Early calls at $0.10 and $0.35 pass and update the ledger.

steps.title: Delegated Ceiling to a Sub-Agent
steps.description: The agent spawns a sub-agent to scrape 5 sources and grants it a $0.50 sub-budget. The child cannot exceed its cap even if the parent still has headroom.

steps.title: Monitors Watch for Runaway
steps.description: A token-velocity circuit breaker and a loop detector watch the loop. Two sub-agents begin ping-ponging, re-reading the same pages, and token velocity spikes far above the task baseline.

steps.title: Circuit Breaker Trips
steps.description: The velocity spike, the loop detector confirming no new progress, and the runaway loop all feed the breaker, which trips at $1.20 of the $2.00 cap before the next call reaches the provider.

steps.title: Pause With State Checkpoint
steps.description: Rather than silently overspending, execution pauses and the state is checkpointed. The run stops before the next call instead of running up an open-ended bill.

steps.title: Human Raises Cap or Kills
steps.description: The operator sees "paused: anomalous token velocity, 60% of budget spent" and either raises the cap to $5 and resumes from the checkpoint, or kills the run. Either way spend stayed bounded by construction.

name: Multi-Source Context Fusion(MSCF)
description: Intelligently combines contextual information from multiple sources with quality weighting and conflict resolution

tldr.what: Merges data from multiple sources using quality weights and conflict resolution to build a single unified context representation.
tldr.when: Systems need current information from several databases or APIs where sources may conflict, have different reliability, or update at different rates.
tldr.watchOut: Stale or contradictory data from slow sources can corrupt the unified view; weighting rules that seemed right become wrong as source reliability shifts.

flow.title: Multi-Source Context Fusion
flow.description: An agent merges customer data from CRM records, product docs, chat history, and real-time signals into one coherent context. It weights sources by reliability and recency, detects and resolves conflicts, and attaches provenance so every fact is traceable.

steps.title: Incoming Request
steps.description: An agent is asked whether to offer a specific customer an upgrade, which requires a complete and trustworthy picture of that customer.

steps.title: Gather From Sources
steps.description: The fusion agent pulls the same customer from four systems in parallel: CRM records, product docs, chat history, and streaming real-time signals.

steps.title: Source Quality Assessment
steps.description: Each source is scored for reliability and completeness, then the weighting engine assigns per-source weights so trusted systems count for more.

steps.title: Temporal Weighting
steps.description: The temporal handler applies age-decay so stale values lose influence, keeping the merged view biased toward the freshest reliable data.

steps.title: Conflict Detection and Validation
steps.description: Weighted fields are checked for disagreements (for example the CRM email differs from the chat email) while the cross-validator confirms each value against two or more sources.

steps.title: Conflict Resolution
steps.description: Detected conflicts and validated fields flow to the resolver, which applies the newest-verified-value-wins rule to pick a single authoritative value per field.

steps.title: Provenance and Unification
steps.description: The provenance tracker tags every resolved field with its originating source, and both the merged values and their provenance assemble into one unified context.

steps.title: Grounded Response
steps.description: The agent answers the upgrade question from the unified 360° context, citing which source backs each claim so the recommendation is auditable.

name: Intelligent Context Routing(ICR)
description: Dynamic routing of contextual information to the most appropriate processing components based on capability matching

tldr.what: Routes incoming context to specialized agents based on content type, language, domain, and capability match, with fallback chains when primary routes fail.
tldr.when: Multi-modal or multi-domain requests where different components handle different content types or expertise areas better than a single processor.
tldr.watchOut: Routing decisions add latency and can misroute if capability metadata becomes stale or misaligned with actual agent performance.

flow.title: Intelligent Context Routing
flow.description: A router agent splits a mixed-modality customer complaint into typed context slices, scores each for relevance, then directs it to the best-matched specialist under token and time budget constraints. Overloaded agents trigger fallback rerouting, and results are reassembled into one resolution.

steps.title: Incoming Mixed Context
steps.description: A high-priority Spanish customer complaint arrives bundling text, images, and video with a two-hour SLA, more than any single agent handles well.

steps.title: Context Decomposition
steps.description: The router hands the payload to the decomposer, which splits it into typed slices so each modality can be routed independently.

steps.title: Relevance Scoring
steps.description: The relevance scorer ranks each slice by how much it contributes to resolving the complaint, producing prioritized text, image, and video slices.

steps.title: Budget and Load Balancing
steps.description: The budget manager sets token and time limits per route while the load balancer checks agent capacity and primes the fallback router for overflow.

steps.title: Capability-Based Routing
steps.description: Each slice is routed to the best-matched specialist: Spanish text to the text specialist, screenshots to the image analyzer, and the recording to the video processor.

steps.title: Overflow Fallback

α = 0.01, γ = 0.95

✨ Optimized Policy
clearly beats random, in this simulation

steps.title: Observe Environment State
steps.description: The agent reads the current state from the environment: user profile, engagement history, time, and device context.

steps.title: Score Actions with Policy
steps.description: The policy network maps the observed state to action scores across the 10,000+ item catalog.

steps.title: Balance Exploration and Exploitation
steps.description: The selector chooses a strategy: epsilon-greedy (ε=0.2), UCB uncertainty bonus, Thompson sampling, or a greedy exploit of the best known action.

steps.title: Take Action
steps.description: The chosen strategy produces a recommendation that the agent serves into the environment.

steps.title: Collect Reward
steps.description: The environment returns a reward: click +1, watch +3, skip -1. Weak engagement is flagged as a penalty signal.

steps.title: Update Policy
steps.description: The TD error drives a gradient step (α=0.01, γ=0.95), reinforcing rewarded actions and discouraging penalized ones.

steps.title: Loop and Improve
steps.description: The updated policy feeds back to the agent for the next cycle, shrinking ε from 0.4 to 0.1 as confidence grows.

steps.title: Converge to Optimal Policy
steps.description: After thousands of cycles the simulated policy stabilizes well above a random baseline. The gap is a property of this toy environment, not a result you should expect to reproduce.

name: Curiosity-Driven Exploration(CDE)
description: Intrinsic motivation-based exploration that drives discovery of novel and surprising information

tldr.what: Agent explores by seeking high-uncertainty or high-surprise states, using information gain or prediction error to prioritize which unknowns to investigate.
tldr.when: Open-ended discovery tasks where the agent must autonomously identify valuable questions without a predefined goal or reward signal.
tldr.watchOut: Agent may chase novelty for its own sake, wasting compute on tangential or low-value discoveries instead of converging on useful findings.

flow.title: Curiosity-Driven Exploration
flow.description: An agent explores an undocumented REST API guided by intrinsic reward. It predicts the outcome of each call, and the surprise, novelty, and information gain of unexpected responses pull it toward unexplored regions rather than a fixed goal.

nodes.label:
🌐 Undocumented REST API
120 endpoints, no docs
Goal: map its behavior

🔍 Curiosity Agent
Seeks novel, surprising states

🧬 State Encoder
Embed endpoint + response

🔮 Forward Model
Predict next response

🗂️ Visited Memory
Buffer of seen states

⚡ Prediction Error
surprise = |pred - actual|
score: 8.7 / 10

✨ Novelty Detector
distance from visited
k-NN in embedding space

📊 Information Gain
expected reduction in
uncertainty: 2.3 bits

💡 Intrinsic Reward
r = surprise + novelty + gain
no external reward needed

🆕 Novel Endpoint
/v2/graph unseen schema
high intrinsic reward

🔁 Known Region
already mapped
reward ≈ 0, skip

🔧 Policy Update
Bias action toward
high-reward regions

🗺️ Knowledge Map
34% more coverage, 12 discoveries

steps.title: Observe Current State
steps.description: The agent calls an endpoint and encodes the endpoint plus its response into an embedding, checking it against the visited-states buffer.

steps.title: Predict the Outcome
steps.description: The forward model predicts the response before the call resolves, so the agent can later measure how wrong it was.

steps.title: Measure Surprise
steps.description: Prediction error compares the predicted and actual response. An unexpected schema scores 8.7 out of 10 surprise.

steps.title: Assess Novelty and Information Gain
steps.description: The novelty detector measures distance from previously visited states, and information gain estimates 2.3 bits of uncertainty reduction.

steps.title: Compute Intrinsic Reward
steps.description: Surprise, novelty, and information gain combine into a single intrinsic reward that needs no external goal signal.

steps.title: Steer Toward Novelty
steps.description: A novel endpoint like /v2/graph earns high reward and is recorded, while already-mapped regions score near zero and are skipped.

steps.title: Update Policy and Loop
steps.description: The policy shifts toward high-reward regions and feeds back to the agent to pick the next call to make.

steps.title: Integrate Discoveries
steps.description: Confirmed discoveries fold into the knowledge map, yielding 34% more coverage and 12 previously unknown behaviors.

name: Multi-Armed Bandit Optimization(MAB)
description: Sequential decision-making under uncertainty with optimal exploration-exploitation trade-offs

tldr.what: Balances trying new options against exploiting known good ones, using confidence bounds to decide which arm to pull each round.
tldr.when: Repeated decisions with uncertain payoffs where you learn from each choice and need to minimize total regret over time.
tldr.watchOut: Slow convergence or poor decisions if reward signals are noisy, delayed, or the environment shifts faster than the algorithm adapts.

flow.title: Multi-Armed Bandit Optimization
flow.description: An agent A/B-tests five system-prompt variants for a support bot. Each round it pulls one arm using epsilon-greedy, UCB, or Thompson sampling, observes whether the ticket resolved, updates its posteriors, and drives cumulative regret down toward the best variant.

Maximize ticket resolution rate

🎰 Bandit Agent
Sequential decisions under uncertainty

pulls: 42, μ=0.61

🅱️ Arm B: Empathetic
pulls: 38, μ=0.68

🇨 Arm C: Step-by-step
pulls: 91, μ=0.87

🇩 Arm D: Formal
pulls: 25, μ=0.54

🇪 Arm E: Playful
pulls: 19, μ=0.49

🎲 Epsilon-Greedy
ε=0.1 explore
0.9 best arm

📈 UCB1
μ + √(2·ln t / n)
optimism bonus

🔔 Thompson Sampling
sample Beta(α, β)
pick max sample

👆 Pull Selected Arm
Serve variant to next ticket

💰 Reward Signal
Resolved +1, escalated 0

📉 Regret Tracker
Cumulative regret vs
optimal arm: 3.2%

🔧 Posterior Update
Beta(α+1, β) on success

🏆 Winner: Arm C
